content:
# Zyx Academy Architecture

Zyx Academy is a full-stack, multi-platform learning management system built with Next.js 16.3 (App Router), React 19, TypeScript, Drizzle ORM, Neon PostgreSQL, Neon Object Storage, Neon Functions, Cloudflare Edge/AI services, Capacitor 7 (mobile), and Tauri v2 (desktop).

```text
Clients: Web Browser | Capacitor 7 (Android/iOS) | Tauri v2 (Windows/macOS/Linux)
  |
  v
Web Tier: Next.js 16.3 App Router
  |-- Production: Vercel (sin1)
  |-- Staging: Vercel custom staging OR Cloud Run Bangkok (asia-southeast3) behind Cloudflare Edge Worker
  |-- Route groups: (marketing), (student), (tutor), (admin), /api/*, /api/mcp/authoring, /offline
  |
  +--> Data Layer (Drizzle ORM -> PostgreSQL only, no SQLite/Turso fallback)
  |      |-- Neon PostgreSQL (separate staging & production branches)
  |      |-- Neon Object Storage (private S3-compatible buckets, STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon)
  |
  +--> Background Compute & Queues
  |      |-- Queue Abstraction (QUEUE_PROVIDER): Inngest Cloud (default) | Google Cloud Tasks + Scheduler
  |      |-- Worker Runtime: Neon Functions (workers/neon-background, function zyxcompute)
  |
  +--> Cloudflare Edge & AI Platform
         |-- Cloudflare AI Gateway (multi-provider routing, BYOK aliases, query-key fallback)
         |-- Cloudflare Vectorize (768d canonical-content-v2 & admin_ops_knowledge namespaces)
         |-- Cloudflare Workers KV (12h AI model catalog cache, profile-free tutor cache)
         |-- Cloudflare Workers: vector-api, zyra-control-plane, realtime, diktat-renderer, python-runtime, staging-web-edge
```

- **PostgreSQL only**: `lib/db/index.ts` requires PostgreSQL (`DATABASE_URL`). Isolated contract tests use PGlite.
- **Private object storage**: Serving staging and production use private Neon S3-compatible buckets (`STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon`). Authorized files are served through access-checked routes or short-lived signed URLs; no public asset proxy exposes private academic or user objects.
- **Non-blocking heavy work**: Ingestion, vector sync, PDF rendering, mastery recomputation, calendar sync, and AI batch generation execute via the queue abstraction (`QUEUE_PROVIDER`) and `workers/neon-background`.
- **Web vs Worker separation**: Modules consumed by `workers/neon-background` must remain framework-neutral (no Next.js or React imports). Verified by `bun run audit:web-boundaries` and `bun run worker:deno:audit`.

section: Separated Mobile and Desktop LMS Shells
content:
LMS surfaces separate mobile and desktop navigation and views under `features/` (`student-dashboard`, `student-assessment`, `student-profile`, `student-schedule`, `tutor-dashboard`, `tutor-schedule`, `admin-home`, `discussions`, `grading`), verified by `bun run audit:ui-separation`:
- **Navigation**: Desktop uses hybrid domain-grouped sidebars; mobile uses `MobileNavbar`, bottom navigation tabs, and sheet drawers with history-backed overlay dismissal (Android Back closes the top dialog/sheet/sidebar before navigating back).
- **Sticky Tabs**: `components/ui/tabs.tsx` provides full-width sticky horizontal tabs with automatic overflow collapse into a `More` / `Lebih` popover.
- **Global Search**: Unified command-menu search (`cmdk`) scoped by role and access permissions.

Client data ownership follows [data-fetching.md](data-fetching.md):
- Account-scoped query keys prevent cross-account cache leaks during account switching.
- Server Components (RSC) handle initial page hydration and streaming boundaries; TanStack Query manages interactive client reads, optimistic updates, and mutation invalidation.
- Request-scoped session and read deduplication avoid redundant database queries within a single request.

- **Mobile (`apps/mobile`)**: Capacitor 7 shell loading the live origin with native bridges for FCM/APNs push notifications, local study reminders, camera restore recovery, OS share/files, haptics, pull-to-refresh, Android App Links (`/.well-known/assetlinks.json`), iOS Universal Links, and offline fallback (`/offline`).
- **Desktop (`apps/desktop`)**: Tauri v2 shell with single-instance deep-link routing (`zyxacademy://`, `zyxacademy-nightly://`), persisted side-by-side window geometry, desktop push bridge, and signed `tauri-plugin-updater` / delta updates.
- **Offline Shell**: Decoupled offline service worker and native offline reader store saved readings in account-scoped private storage and clean up on sign-out or account switch.

- Authentication is powered by Better Auth (`user`, `session`, `account`, `verification`) with Google OAuth and PKCE.
- Canonical domain authorization uses `pengguna`, `peran` (`admin`, `tutor`, `murid`), and `pengguna_peran` (many-to-many role assignments), allowing multi-role users.
- Active sessions visiting marketing entry routes redirect to their role dashboard using the canonical public origin.

The sidebar account menu supports up to 5 concurrent saved Zyx sessions:
- **Web & Desktop**: Saved sessions switch active cookies without re-authenticating with Google; adding an account uses system-browser OAuth with `login_hint`.
- **Android**: Uses the `ZyxGoogleAuth` Credential Manager plugin with explicit browser fallback on cancellation or older APKs.
- **Isolation on switch**: Switching or removing an account clears account-scoped TanStack Query caches, private offline reader caches, guarded coding drafts, and active Zyra conversation overrides, while pausing receiving-tab interactions until the new session identity settles.

Zyx separates authoring from publication using deterministic, versioned bundles:

```text
Source PDFs / Documents
  -> Source Pack (lossless transcription, page checksums, figure extraction)
  -> Idea Bundle V3 (atomic Ideas, provenance, learning sections, relations)
  -> Product Bundle V4 (structured scientific Articles, authored Diktats, flashcards)
  -> Product Bundle V5 (standalone reviewed solution collections)
  -> Flexible Revisions (stable-ID MCP edits, selective review reuse, atomic release, restore)
```

- **Product V4 (default for Article & Diktat)**: Supports ordered scientific blocks, KaTeX math, typed `zyx-visual` Markdown embeds, sandboxed `interactive_document` widgets (with theme/resize/offscreen-pause messaging), source figure assets, and static 1 to 4 page Diktat PDFs.
- **Verification and Review**: Staged drafts require browser and PDF verification (`local_playwright`, `cloudflare`, or `steel`) bound to the exact import, revision, and web build fingerprint, followed by explicit semantic review before atomic publication.
- **MCP Surface (`/api/mcp/authoring`)**: Streamable HTTP MCP server exposing authoring, assessment, and admin operations with OAuth PKCE consent, 4 default OAuth scopes plus explicit publication/admin grants, capability discovery, and operation receipts.

section: Cloudflare AI Gateway and Dynamic Model Registry
content:
All LLM requests route through Cloudflare AI Gateway (`CF_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, `CF_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN`):
- Supports multi-provider BYOK aliases and query-key fallback configured per feature or globally in `/admin/ops/models`.
- Dynamic model-list discovery caches provider catalogs in Workers KV for 12 hours (14-day stale-usable window) and sorts newest first by verified release date then provider `created` timestamp.
- Scheduled (00:00 and 12:00 UTC) and manual 3-sample median latency probes monitor provider responsiveness.
- Three consecutive failures trigger a 5-minute alias cooldown with automatic fallback to healthy aliases.

`workers/zyra-control-plane` (Cloudflare Worker with SQLite Durable Objects) coordinates distributed allowance leases, fairness across project slots, and masked health diagnostics:
- Every learner generation acquires a lease before provider dispatch and commits or refunds idempotently on completion or terminal failure.
- Standard student daily turns scale by gamification rank bonus (15 to 18 turns per Jakarta day).
- Operational telemetry uses fixed-column `zyra_operational_events` and never stores prompts, responses, raw keys, object keys, or learner identities.

- **Canonical learning index**: 768-dimensional cosine Cloudflare Vectorize index (`canonical-content-v2`). Legacy namespaces (`learning`, `practice`, `past_exams`, `idea`, `product`) are retired and quarantined (`VECTOR_SYNC_LEGACY_NAMESPACE_RETIRED`); no legacy KO retrieval fallback exists.
- **Transactional outbox (`vector_sync_queue`)**: Canonical publication, withdrawal, and question mutations enqueue deterministic outbox rows. Workers reread canonical state under advisory locks before provider writes, isolate failures by vector identity, and enforce assessment answer safety (no answer keys in shared caches or active-attempt retrieval).
- **Admin Ops Knowledge**: Separate `admin_ops_knowledge` Vectorize namespace and prebuilt `lib/admin-ops-ai/ops-docs-index.json` index curated documentation (`CURATED_ADMIN_KNOWLEDGE_ALLOWLIST`), never mixing with student tutoring namespaces.
- **Zyra streaming & pedagogy**: Live SSE streaming with response progress indicators, KaTeX macro normalization, subtle follow-up quick actions, automatic AI thread titles, and in-memory per-session language overrides (bounded to 32 sessions).

- **Assessments**: Canonical `soal`, `asesmen`, `percobaan_asesmen`, and `jawaban_murid` with compatibility projections (`quiz_templates`, `student_quiz_attempts`). Timed quizzes accept timeout/late submissions and cap recorded duration at `timeLimitSeconds`; untimed quizzes omit deadlines.
- **Live Classroom (`FEATURE_LIVE`)**: `workers/realtime` WebSocket sessions authenticated with `LIVE_HMAC_SECRET`.
- **Python Learning**: Editable Python blocks in Articles, viewport-aware Playground editor, browser Pyodide runtime, staging WASI terminal via `workers/python-runtime`, explicit Submit grading (`CODING_BROWSER_PROVIDER`), and Zyra Python/Tutor coaching. See [coding-foundation.md](coding-foundation.md).
- **Discussions**: 13 PostgreSQL tables with GIN full-text search (`0041`), bilingual scoped channels, immutable retry keys, `@Zyra` AI dispatch with cooldowns, mention handles, and emoji status. See [discussions.md](discussions.md).
- **Google Calendar Sync**: `google_calendar_sync` (`0040`) syncs personal offline OAuth calendars and the shared Zyx host primary calendar via daily queue dispatch and manual toolbar actions.

Gamification and social features are student-only (admin gamification pages were removed):
- **Projection boundary**: Public student profiles (`/students/[publicId]`), `StudentProfileDialog`, and people search expose only authorized public fields (public ID, display name, photo/frame, rank, featured badges, equipped owned Zyra mascot, follow counts). LP balances, emails, internal account IDs, and private academic stats are never exposed.
- **Privacy & moderation**: Enforces member visibility (`0037_member_profile_visibility.sql`), bidirectional block filtering, report controls, and leaderboard opt-in.
- **Public Demo**: `/demo` reuses the exact student shell and renderers with `StudentAccountBoundary` and browser-local fictional state, never mutating live accounts or spending AI quota.

- Supported locales: `id` and `en` via `next-intl` and paired JSON catalogs under `messages/id/` and `messages/en/`.
- `proxy.ts` handles finite public locale rewrites while preserving canonical origins.
- Preference precedence: authenticated `account_locale_preferences` -> cookie/browser locale -> default `id`.
- Background email and notification templates are worker-safe (no React/Next.js imports).

# Simpler Idea and Product authoring

Status: `OPEN / IN PROGRESS`. PR #480 continuation, 2026-11-25. Local implementation and repeatable synthetic measurements. Hosted acceptance, installed skill distribution and real time/token savings remain separate release checks.

| Friction | Change | Boundary |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Agent builds Idea source records, offsets, metadata and ZIP | `authoring.create_idea_draft` accepts atomic Ideas, teaching sections, explained relations and exact source quotes. The server reads the bound validated Source Pack and builds V3. | All documents and units remain in coverage checks. Ambiguous quotes require a longer unique quote or an exact offset. |
| Agent cannot inspect a raw draft cheaply | `bun run authoring:preview` renders the same Product draft JSON with shared learner and print components, without login, DB or network. `--watch` reuses compiled assets, server and browser. | Local preview, never trusted release evidence. Reports retain exact input hash and honest untested states. |
| Agent assembles Product manifests, hashes and ZIP bytes | `authoring.create_product_draft` accepts typed Article/Diktat content and source/Idea IDs. The server loads current references, assigns missing mechanical IDs and constructs the canonical archive. | Initial V4 only; existing admission and staging policy still run. |
| Every edit returns the entire artifact and review state | Opt-in `responseMode: "compact"` on context, create, patch and restore. A `target` selects one stable unit on context reads. | Full remains the default. Integrity and scope still load and validate the stored archive; compact saves response size and review/readiness queries. |
| Agent manually tracks successor IDs and run tokens | `createIdeaAuthoringClient` and `createProductAuthoringClient` wrap existing revision MCP calls through an injected transport. Exact reads cannot silently adopt a different kind/import/revision; `readFull()` obtains review context. | In-repo helper, not a published SDK. Errors preserve the last observed identity; no automatic write retries, reviews or publication. |
| One validation failure starts another blind loop | Error responses add `category`, `retryable`, `nextAction` and bounded `diagnostics`. Final draft validation preserves all independent issues. | Existing error fields and OAuth challenges remain. Transient failures require a status check before retry. |
| Browser work runs before deterministic findings are resolved | Structure/model checks run first and collect their findings. | Blocked browser/print checks remain `NOT_TESTED`. The requirement matrix and final acceptance are unchanged. |
| PDF renders twice for its file and page images | The PDF check captures every page from the same bytes. The paired image check reuses those captures. | Older executors that return only a PDF keep the separate image execution fallback. |
| Failed attempts rerun successful work | Private signed batch checkpoints bind the exact plan, staging audit, requirement and capture batch. Retries verify metadata and bytes, then copy valid artifacts to the new attempt. | No reuse across changed revisions, references, runtime or browser bindings. Failed and incomplete checks are not proof. |

Bootstrap the Idea stage and start an `idea_product` run with the exact validated stored Source Pack. Read `ideaBundle.initialDraft` and fetch `ideaDraftInput` from `ideaBundle.schemaDocuments`. Send a stable `draftKey` and `draft: { ideas, learningSections, relations }`. Each Idea supplies a local key, code, atomic statement, explanation, kind, role and exact quotes addressed by document ID and source-unit number. Sections and relations use those local keys. The server derives identity, provenance, attribution, timestamps, versions, source records, hashes and ZIP.

Source pack ID, import, checksum, status, quality report, course and chapter must match the run. Spans use JavaScript UTF-16 offsets into LF-normalized text, matching the canonical validator; embedded source bytes and their checksums remain intact. Aggregate reference, document, unit, archive-file and byte limits fail before staging. Canonical V3 and quality validation still run before the original admission/staging service.

The Idea playbook now links to runtime schemas instead of repeating unsupported relation names, wrong section/provenance fields and an incomplete manifest. This removes avoidable repair loops. Every source unit remains visible, but 100% unit coverage is not proof that all concepts within every unit were covered. Review must still assess atomicity, meaning, completeness, prerequisites and evidence.

Discover the current playbook/contract, read published Ideas and admitted source excerpts, then call the advertised `initialDraft` tool. Send a stable `draftKey`, `runToken`, `bootstrapToken` and `draft: { products: [...] }`. The server returns a staged import and checksum without returning the ZIP. Repeating the same input with the same key, run token and bound reference versions produces the same archive. Changed content or updated references under that key cannot overwrite a staged draft; read current context and use the revision tools.

Supply titles, content, Idea IDs, and source/excerpt IDs. Missing entity/section/block/part IDs and order are mechanical. Supply explicit stable IDs when other content needs to reference them. Source selections inherit only from an explicitly selected parent. The server does not invent sources, scientific facts or visual models. Optional `ideaLinks: [{ id, weight, role }]` preserves authored priorities for exactly the selected `ideaIds`; the server still owns reference versions and hashes. Without that field, equal shares and `supporting` roles remain compatible. Invalid sums, duplicates, missing/extra IDs and forged metadata are rejected.

For a draft edit, read one unit, patch it and continue with the returned successor identity. Read full context at the review boundary and use the release planner for current blockers. `evaluation.review` and `evaluation.readiness` return `not_requested` in a compact response; those fields cannot stand in for approval or publication readiness.

The typed creation path currently supports standalone Articles, standalone Diktats and a Diktat derived from an Article in the same request. Flashcards, V5 collections, binary interactive documents and external Article lineage retain the archive path. Read or patch one Diktat unit with `{ entityType: "diktat", entityId, unitId }`, without section/block/item selectors. Address its parts with stable paths such as `parts[summary-part].markdown`. The server rebuilds projections and hashes and invalidates affected review and print evidence.

```sh
bun run authoring:preview --input /absolute/path/draft.json --out artifacts/authoring-preview
bun run authoring:preview --input /absolute/path/draft.json --out artifacts/authoring-preview --watch
```

Use `--check` for structural checks and an outline without a browser. `--example short` and `--example long` create deterministic examples. `--executable-path /path/to/chromium` selects a local browser explicitly; its recorded version does not change trusted release pins. The raw input is the same `productDraftInput` object sent to the creation tool, without fake source hashes or preview-only fields.

`preview-report.json` records input hash, check states, issues, timing, browser launches, PDF renders and capture paths. `outline.json` lists teaching order, objectives, Ideas and parts. Article captures cover 380 by 844 and 1536 by 864 in both themes. Diktat output includes the actual PDF and every page image from its bytes, with page-budget and overflow checks.

The server binds loopback only and serves fixed in-memory routes under a random prefix. Browser requests outside that route are blocked. Input/output aliases are rejected; report writes use exclusive temporary files and atomic rename. Missing browser setup is a runtime issue, not an instruction to rewrite the draft. Watch replaces stale success on invalid edits and keeps one browser alive between valid edits.

Preview explicitly leaves live references, human visual review and publication unverified. Server grading, coding execution and saved progress require hosted checks. Binary figures and HTML documents use the admitted-asset verifier. Inspect the initial render locally, then inspect all required control states and PDF evidence through the trusted verifier before release.

```sh
bun scripts/authoring/benchmark-agent-workflow.ts
```

The benchmark uses actual builders, response projections and verification coordinators with deterministic synthetic content, storage and renderer observations. It measures JSON bytes and executor calls, not model tokens, money, duration, live DB/storage or visual quality.

| Response | Short example | Long example |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Full context | 19,483 bytes | 138,362 bytes |
| Compact context | 443 bytes | 443 bytes |
| One selected block | 1,325 bytes | 1,325 bytes |
| Compact reduction | 97.73% | 99.68% |
| Selected-block reduction | 93.20% | 99.04% |

The PDF scenario reduces PDF calls from 2 to 1 and retains all 10 requirements. After an interruption, retry uses 5 executor calls instead of 8 and retains all 8 requirements. Failed structural preflight starts no browser work and records blocked checks as untested.

Direct JSON is not always smaller than ZIP transport: these examples use 9,537/81,078 bytes of author input versus 6,884/12,716 bytes of ZIP base64. The creation benefit is removing metadata/hash/archive work. Do not report response or call reductions as measured token or monetary savings.

Both creation tools use existing `authoring:stage` consent. No new OAuth scope, feature flag or database migration is added. Bootstrap checks run before context or storage access. The context loader limits references to published same-course Ideas, active same-chapter or course-wide sources and their current excerpts, and published same-chapter learning sections. Existing staging and later release checks remain authoritative.

Runtime discovery includes limits, compact response semantics and recovery fields. The MCP tool catalog carries small input envelopes; agents fetch full checksum-pinned `ideaDraftInput` and `productDraftInput` schemas on demand. Idea descriptors use `/api/authoring/contracts/idea-v3`. The server still parses the complete strict schema before loading references or staging. The Idea, Product and pipeline playbooks, repository plugin skill sources and their host prompts use the new path only when advertised by the connected server. Existing archive tools and full responses remain available. Initial authoring remains discoverable through `workflow.get_contract`; `admin.capabilities` continues to advertise its existing revision-only authoring surface.

The hosted skill build uses `authoring-skills.lock.json` pins in the separate `zyx-authoring-mcp` repository. [Package PR #3](https://github.com/soezyxstt/zyx-authoring-mcp/pull/3) released staging 0.5.2 after bot review completed without findings, advancing the older six-skill staging package to all 12 workflows. The staging lock now selects its merge commit `dcb6098002e4e730f7da610d6c13417388cd45fc`; the production lock is unchanged. Package source, external release, server build and installed-host refresh are distinct states; this PR does not claim installed clients or deployed servers have changed.

Release 0.5.2 updates every skill and its host prompt against the current runtime:

| Skill | Main change |
| --- | --- |
| `zyx-authoring-pipeline` | Start at the needed stage, reuse valid context and choose the advertised draft path. |
| `zyx-source-pack-mcp` | Use actual manifest fields, source-unit markers, original-byte hashes and complete coverage evidence; resume extraction without blind rework. |
| `zyx-idea-bundle-mcp` | Author atomic Ideas and exact quotes while the server builds mechanical fields and archives. |
| `zyx-product-bundle-mcp` | Preview the same Article/Diktat input, retain archive paths for unsupported content and review the final canonical artifact. |
| `zyx-content-revisions` | Find stored imports without an old run, read one stable target, then review full current context and follow the profile's evidence requirements. |
| `zyx-question-authoring-mcp` | Use the runtime draft example, published Idea links and actual bank gaps; original questions remain drafts. |
| `reference-question-ingest` | Use legitimate private file-key arguments, strict payload fields and honest provenance; historical essays stay outside quiz assembly. |
| `zyx-blog-mcp` | Search metadata first, validate actual create/edit shapes and distinguish draft creation from live published edits. |
| `zyx-forms-mcp` | Preserve full definitions, simulate without submitting responses and inspect Sheets conflicts even when a job succeeds. |
| `zyx-media-mcp` | Resolve public serving paths, respect the bounded upload job and verify assets after manual reconciliation. |
| `zyx-admin-operations` | Discover only relevant domains and use the exact environment, scopes, signed plan and request identity. |
| `zyx-operation-recovery` | Separate database receipts, provider outcomes and authoring revisions; preserve original operation identity before retry. |

Runtime playbooks were corrected with the skills. The complete Source Pack example and historical-reference example now pass their actual validators. Product V4 examples use typed fields; obsolete provenance and assessment fields no longer cause preventable repair loops. Packaging tests cover all 12 host prompts and verify version substitution in both JSON-style and prose bootstrap instructions when the next release version changes.

Compared with the previous PR head, Idea and Product skill files plus host prompts shrink from 21,151 to 17,467 UTF-8 bytes (17.4%). All 12 pairs total 70,458 bytes versus 70,978 previously, including added recovery and evidence rules. These are instruction-file measurements, not measured tokens, costs or teaching quality. Independent source review and six read-only workflow walkthroughs checked stage selection, standalone Diktat, existing-unit revisions, historical ingest and admin recovery. They do not replace a hosted run.

1. **New draft authority and content:** Confirm source/course/chapter/version checks, deterministic retry identity, unchanged canonical admission, valid generated IDs and Article-to-Diktat lineage. Check the optional authored Idea weights and compatible equal-share default.
2. **Revision compatibility:** Confirm full responses remain usable, compact/target reads clearly defer review, successor imports and execution tokens stay bound, and stale/CAS failures cannot become automatic retries.
3. **Evidence trust:** Confirm a checkpoint cannot cross plans, audits, requirements, batches or executor identity; corrupted metadata/bytes rerun; artifacts retain the current attempt prefix; final receipt/PDF attachment checks still reject stale evidence.
4. **Print completeness:** Confirm one PDF yields every required page, preserves the page budget and overflow checks, and cannot approve an incomplete or failed capture. Inspect actual PDF and page images during hosted acceptance.
5. **Agent usability:** Run one new Article, one standalone Diktat and one small edit with the advertised tools. Record tool calls, response bytes, render invocations, wall time and manual recovery steps.

- Complete authenticated staging acceptance with a synthetic authorized draft and real storage, including scope denial, concurrent edits, failed verification retry and final review. The current private local operator deliberately targets its configured production origin; do not relabel that as a staging run or use production data for this PR.
- Measure real short and long chapter authoring before claiming lower token cost or duration. The synthetic response/executor benchmark above does not measure model tokens, money, wall time or live storage. Compare quality with the same source and a blind rubric for correctness, coverage, teaching order and readability.
- Decide whether binary-asset input and external Article lineage belong in the next typed-draft contract. Preserve reference and asset admission checks in each extension.
- Design any reuse across revisions separately. Split content/runtime fingerprints only with dependency-specific invalidation tests. The exact-plan cache here deliberately does not claim that unrelated edits are safe to ignore.
- Check the refreshed package in installed hosts and their OAuth sessions. The reviewed external staging release and exact source pin are complete; a server build alone does not establish host acceptance.
- Review CI and bot comments on the latest commit before merging to staging. The owner marked PR #480 ready for review on 2026-11-25 while the skill update was in progress. A code merge does not run the authenticated checks above or deploy the application; deployment and content publication retain their own verification.

The initial PR recorded 265 passing tests across 27 focused files. The continuation adds direct Idea, descriptor, client, unit-edit, preview and measurement checks; the current PR verification record supersedes the initial counts. Pinned staging and repository-candidate skill builds remain distinct. Focused TypeScript checking includes changed TypeScript source/test files and their imports. The repository ESLint configuration excludes test files. Initial CI identified two older test fixtures that needed the new tool name and production-compatible missing-object errors; both affected contracts now pass. The PR description records reproducible commands, current test/type/visual results and the latest CI status.

The subsequent 12-skill refresh passed 15 Python distribution tests and 69 tests across 10 focused Bun contract files, using the latest result for each file. Both environment packages built with 35 allowlisted files. The staging release check accepted the 0.4.1 to 0.5.2 advance. The new executable playbook examples cover original bytes, hashes, coverage and strict assessment eligibility. Final review corrected conditional V4 PDF evidence, the 100-import search limit, media lookup after reconciliation and Sheets confirmation after a successful job. Focused TypeScript checking, source lint and diff checks passed. After the external package merged, a normal locked staging build succeeded; a local MCP HTTP smoke read and hash-checked the full catalog (12 skills, 24 files) and compact catalog (one router, 25 files). This exercised the released commit with staging identity, not a workspace-candidate manifest or an installed host.

Tests exercise typed packaging, database source/Idea binding, internal staging delegation, compact projections, exact selectors, immutable revision replay, diagnostic redaction, cheap-check scheduling, single-PDF capture and signed-checkpoint retry/isolation. The web retry fixture includes the renderer's full output of multiple PNGs plus JSON observations, as well as paginated output.

The continuation's latest local results total 342 passing tests across 37 focused files. A PostgreSQL PDF fixture models the private storage adapter's wrapped NoSuchKey/404 response; permission and transport errors still propagate. The local preview handles theme initialization and deferred visual rendering. JSXGraph uses its interpreter under the preview's strict local CSP; the production renderer and trusted browser pin are unchanged.

No learner layout changed. Synthetic checks cover orchestration and evidence handling; they do not establish visual quality of a real chapter. Live OAuth/storage contention, deployed MCP and installed skill behavior require their own evidence. The current PR records actual typecheck, visual and CI results separately from synthetic tests.

# Authoring Context Pack V1

Plan 007 defines a deterministic, redacted export for external authoring. The boundary is always-on and admin-only by default.

The pack contains a versioned manifest, course and chapter metadata, published current Ideas, active source metadata, exact source excerpts, Idea provenance and relations, active learning objectives, safe content requirements, allowed benchmark summaries, and the authoring contract. An allowed benchmark projection includes its benchmark ID, dedicated ITB `referenceId`, exact `sourceLabel`, dataset key, version, checksum, and safe summary. The benchmark ID must never be used as the question source reference. The projection uses explicit fields and never serializes database rows directly.

Ideas must be published, current, and reviewed. Draft, stale, superseded, withdrawn, needs-review, or unreviewed Ideas are excluded. Source excerpts must belong to an active source version in the selected course.

Holdout benchmark stems, options, answers, solutions, embeddings, and identifying paraphrases are excluded. The manifest records only the number of holdout records excluded. Murid profiles, emails, enrollments, attempts, answers, mastery, chats, credentials, provider secrets, signed URLs, internal URLs, and user identity fields are excluded.

The content scanner fails closed on forbidden fields, secret canaries, signed URLs, internal URLs, and protected fixture values. New fields stay excluded until the allowlist and adversarial tests are updated.

The same snapshot ID, request policy, input content, creation timestamp, and retention timestamp produce identical entity checksums, pack checksum, and ZIP bytes. Files are sorted and JSON keys are serialized deterministically.

Private artifacts use the exact staging key `overhaul/<runId>/authoring-context/<packId>.zip`. The key is recorded in `audit_mutasi` with actor, policy version, source entity versions, holdout exclusion count, artifact checksum, correlation ID, and retention timestamp. The artifact is never exposed through a public URL. Rollback removes only explicitly named test objects by exact key.

```bash
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:preflight
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:test-authoring-context -- --run-id <runId> --course tutorial-pka
bun --env-file=.env.staging run staging:scan-context-pack -- --run-id <runId>
```
# Authoring Job Pack V1

Authoring Job Pack adalah workflow legacy untuk handoff berbasis ZIP. Workflow aktif sekarang menggunakan tiga skill MCP baru (`zyx-source-pack-mcp`, `zyx-idea-bundle-mcp`, dan `zyx-product-bundle-mcp`) dan tidak memerlukan download Authoring Job Pack atau Authoring Context Pack sebagai langkah antar-agent. Dokumen ini dipertahankan untuk kompatibilitas dengan workflow lama dan kontrak ZIP yang masih dibaca validator.

1. Upload satu Source Pack ZIP.
2. Tunggu analisis dokumen, unit, section, formula, visual, soal, dan pembahasan.
3. Pilih satu mata kuliah aktif.
4. Pilih satu atau lebih bab aktif.
5. Petakan setiap section sumber ke tepat satu bab. Jika hanya satu bab dipilih, seluruh section dipetakan otomatis.
6. Pilih keluarga produk. Artikel selalu aktif. Soal selalu dipasangkan dengan pembahasan, dan blueprint memerlukan soal.
7. Unduh `authoring-job-{name}.zip`.

Analisis dan pembuatan ZIP berlangsung di memori. Keduanya tidak menulis R2 atau database. Penyimpanan baru terjadi pada workflow upload dan konfirmasi Idea Bundle atau Product Bundle.

```text
manifest.json
authoring-job.json
source-pack/manifest.json
source-pack/documents/*.md
source-pack/coverage/*.json
contracts/authoring-job.schema.json
contracts/source-pack/manifest.schema.json
contracts/idea-bundle/*.json
contracts/product-bundle/*.json
instructions/external-authoring-workflow.json
```

Root manifest mendeklarasikan setiap file, ukuran byte, checksum SHA-256, job ID, Source Pack ID, dan course ID. File yang tidak dideklarasikan atau checksum yang berubah membuat pack ditolak.

`authoring-job.json` menyimpan label manusia dan ID teknis untuk course serta bab. Agent harus mempertahankan ID teknis persis, tetapi operator cukup bekerja dengan label di UI.

Setiap section mapping memuat document ID, section ID, judul, rentang source unit inklusif, chapter ID, dan label chapter. Semua section harus dipetakan tepat satu kali. Chapter yang dipilih tetapi tidak menerima section tidak disertakan dalam job final.

Attribution memakai sentinel `$UPLOADER` dan `$APPROVING_REVIEWER`. Zyx menyelesaikan sentinel tersebut menjadi identitas pengguna yang bertanggung jawab saat publikasi.

`generator.provider` pada manifest Source Pack mencatat provider yang benar-benar menghasilkan transkripsi, bukan host MCP yang mengirimnya. Validator menerima `google` dan `openai`; `model` dan `promptVersion` harus mencerminkan model serta instruksi yang dipakai.

Pada workflow legacy, `source-pack-translator` menghasilkan Source Pack dan `package-source-pack.js` menetapkan seluruh entry ke mode `0644`; generic archiver dan packaging direktori skill dilarang. Validator JavaScript memverifikasi binary asli, count Markdown, marker, blok visual, dan quality report. Pada workflow MCP aktif, agent dapat memilih PDF yang sudah tersimpan melalui `source.list_files`, membacanya per halaman melalui `source.read_file`, lalu mengirim referensi terenkripsi sebagai `storedOriginals` ke `source.ingest`. Jalur file lokal tetap memakai input ephemeral `originals`. Kedua jalur menjalankan pemeriksaan yang sama, sedangkan stored originals juga mengikat token ke course dan chapter pilihan catalog MCP. Source Pack yang valid secara otomatis disimpan ke Cloudflare R2 dan dicatat di tabel `impor_bundle` dengan status `validated`, sehingga dapat diperiksa lewat `source.list_packs` dan `source.get_pack`, serta digunakan kembali langsung melalui `sourcePackId` pada `workflow.start` jika tahap Idea atau Product Bundle berikutnya perlu diulang.

Workflow legacy `zyx-product-authoring` menerima Authoring Job Pack dan Context Pack terbaru. Workflow MCP aktif melakukan pengecekan published Idea, version, semantic hash, dependency freshness, dan chapter scope langsung sebelum Product Bundle staging. Checkpoint publikasi Idea tetap wajib dan tidak dapat dilewati.

Seluruh packager dan validator yang dibundel dalam ketiga skill memakai file `.js` dan dijalankan langsung oleh Bun. Packager menolak file tambahan dan symlink, menetapkan mode ZIP `0644`, lalu menjalankan validator kontrak sebelum menulis hasil. Import ke modul kontrak `.ts` repository tetap diizinkan karena modul tersebut adalah implementasi otoritatif aplikasi, bukan script skill.

```bash
bun test tests/contracts/authoring-job-pack.test.ts
```

Gate tersebut mencakup Source Pack tanpa dokumen pembahasan, mapping lengkap, pack mandiri, dan deteksi file yang dirusak.

# Flexible Idea and Product revisions

Status: `ACTIVE`. Implemented and verified with focused local contracts. Remote migrations, deployment and live-service acceptance remain separate.

The revision workflow supports Idea V3 and learning Product V3, V4 and V5. It rejects bundles below V3. Assessment authoring remains in its separate workflow. Existing historical records are not deleted or converted by this feature.

Each editable artifact retains its existing single-chapter scope. A release can combine scoped artifacts within the same canonical course. It does not move content between courses or silently reinterpret a multi-chapter archive as one chapter.

A product or Idea retains its logical identity while its content evolves through reviewed revisions. An immutable admitted ZIP is the transport and historical record; an agent edits a draft through stable-ID operations rather than rebuilding that ZIP itself. The server computes the archive, content hashes, dependencies and changed entity versions.

Creating a draft from an existing published import leaves the current publication live. Each draft carries its source import, observed checksum and immutable lineage. Editing and restoration require an exact observed draft revision. A stale revision is a conflict, never permission to overwrite newer work.

A release manifest refers to exact Idea and Product draft imports. It can combine independently validated profiles, including Article/Diktat V4 and standalone Pembahasan V5. Each artifact keeps its own strict schema and required gates. A release does not turn a collection into an Article or remove V4 trusted verification.

Prospective dependency resolution currently covers incoming Ideas and dependencies between Products inside one admitted artifact. A dependency on a not-yet-published Product in another import remains a blocker; the planner must not claim that graph is ready. Existing cross-import dependencies continue to require exact published upstream content.

Publication validates the release manifest and repeats its snapshot and dependency checks under transaction locks. Replacement retires the superseded ownership and promotes the new revisions in one transaction. Failure preserves the old live state. Shared canonical ownership and published dependents require explicit reconciliation; the agent must not silently rewrite another owner's content.

For a single-product correction, call `authoring.create_revision` with `entityIds: [productId]` from the observed edit context. Direct patches must target that ID. Check the reported derived-product and print evidence changes before approving the successor bundle.

Operations address entities, sections, blocks, Diktat units and collection items by stable ID. Diktat reads and patches use `unitId` with the exact product parent, without section/block/item selectors. Stable part selectors such as `parts[part-id].markdown` support a small edit; the server refreshes projections and invalidates affected evidence. Array offsets are not stable identities. Scope, stored identity, lineage and computed hashes are server-controlled. Structural edits and explicit provenance changes must pass the complete original validators, including graph and source references. A source change cannot be justified by copying the previous provenance.

The source documents and excerpt archives themselves remain immutable in this editing workflow. Provenance changes must reference admitted active sources. Ingesting a new source follows the source-grounded authoring workflow. Existing V3 rules for unique section and block IDs within an artifact remain enforced; the review persistence also records the owning Product ID.

The release plan reports the exact revision manifest, changed and preserved units, review requirements, affected dependencies, stale evidence, blockers and next actions. Metadata and semantic no-ops must not cause every entity to receive a new version. A changed Article can invalidate its derived Diktat and PDF. The server does not invent replacement Diktat content or a verification receipt.

A Diktat's published PDF key is immutable for its canonical version. A meaningful bundle change requiring fresh PDF evidence therefore advances the Diktat evidence revision even when its authored text is unchanged. The impact distinguishes a print-context change from changed print content. Unrelated Article and flashcard content keeps its own version unless its content or dependency context changes.

Existing review evidence can be reused only when the reviewed unit, applicable parent and source context, reviewer and decision still match. A release decision remains explicit. Changes to structure, prerequisites or provenance can require broader review than a single text field. Reuse is auditable and never amounts to automatic mathematical approval.

The [draft agent workflow update](authoring-agent-workflow.md) adds optional `responseMode: "compact"` for context, create, patch and restore, plus exact `target` selectors on context reads. Compact/target replies retain identity, bounded impact and current execution tokens while marking review/readiness as not evaluated. They skip those review queries but still admit the stored artifact and check its exact scope. Full stays the default. Use full context and the release planner before approval; never infer readiness from a compact edit response.

The Idea and Product injected-transport clients carry successor identity after successful calls and refuse overlapping edits. They reject mismatched exact reads, expose `readFull()` for review, and never replace stale checksums or retry writes. Additive diagnostics distinguish content, conflict, permission and runtime failures while preserving existing error codes and OAuth challenges.

The common tools are `authoring.get_edit_context`, `authoring.create_revision`, `authoring.patch_revision`, `authoring.prepare_revision_verification`, `authoring.plan_release`, `authoring.review_revision`, `authoring.publish_release`, `authoring.list_revisions` and `authoring.restore_revision`. Runtime discovery supplies their schemas, requirements and bounded inputs.

Every meaningful content patch creates an immutable successor draft with a new import ID and checksum. An unchanged patch retains the current draft. The previous unpublished draft becomes superseded; its artifact and reviews remain historical records. Continue with the returned identity. A repeated identical patch against its superseded predecessor resolves to the existing successor instead of creating duplicate work.

When a V4 Product depends on Idea revisions in the same release, call `authoring.prepare_revision_verification` with those exact entries before trusted verification. The server records the prospective dependency graph and current live baseline in an immutable audit. The trusted operator verifies against that bound graph. A changed candidate or baseline invalidates the context; preparing a new context does not fabricate rendering evidence or approve content.

Existing-content editing uses its stored artifact and server-derived course and chapter scope. It does not require a new Source Pack, an unexpired original authoring run or draft adoption into a replacement run. A fresh compatible bootstrap, authenticated active canonical admin and the relevant read, stage, review or explicit publication grant remain required. New content still follows the source-grounded authoring workflow.

An agent reads the current context, forks a draft, patches the requested units, inspects the release plan, completes the required evidence and reviews, and explicitly publishes the exact plan. A stale plan requires a fresh read and a new decision. The Admin website is optional.

History retains immutable admitted artifacts and audit lineage. Restoration creates a new draft based on the historical authored content, with versions rebased against the current live state. It does not rewrite the historical revision or immediately replace the live version. Current source, access, review and verification gates still apply before release.

Root runs focused checks sequentially with a process-group memory and time guard. Workers perform source edits without heavy validation processes. No full local lint, typecheck or build is requested. Local mocks and PGlite do not establish deployed MCP availability, OAuth, storage behavior or real multi-session PostgreSQL contention. Remote migration, deployment and publication require their own verified authorized target.

Local integration covers consecutive Idea releases, CAS and rollback, provenance replacement, historical reactivation, V5 item review reuse, dependency-only edits, mixed Idea/V5 release, fresh V4 Diktat evidence and mixed Idea/V4 verification before promotion. V4 integration uses the actual receipt, persistence, review and publication services with explicitly synthetic renderer observations and memory storage. It does not establish a complete trusted operator run. The reconciled generated migration `0017_quiet_the_hand.sql` remains a prerequisite before rollout.

# Idea Bundle V3 Contract

Status: `ACTIVE` behind `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1` for new submission. V2 remains readable during transition.

Idea Bundle V3 adds a pedagogical outline to the source grounded Idea graph. The new entity file is `entities/learning-sections.json`, declared as `learning_sections` in the manifest. Source materials, source chunks, Ideas, provenance, and relations retain their V2 identity and checksum rules.

The ZIP, strict unknown field, deterministic checksum, source grounding, provenance, and relation cycle boundaries from V2 remain in force. V3 additionally validates learning section hierarchy, depth, slug, ordering, Idea coverage, and source chunk references.

Admin draft editing accepts only safe textual and ordering fields with `expectedRevision`. Stable IDs, Idea membership, provenance, and lineage cannot be edited. The server rebuilds checksums after an accepted edit. Admin and headless approval require explicit decisions for every Idea, bound to the exact revision and item hashes. The publishing admin must be the reviewer who recorded the complete approval.

`authoring.create_idea_draft` accepts atomic content, pedagogical sections, explained relations and exact Source Pack quotes. Read `ideaBundle.initialDraft` and the checksum-pinned `ideaDraftInput` descriptor through `workflow.get_contract`. The server binds the exact validated source revision and scope, derives spans and IDs, constructs V3, and invokes the original validators, quality checks and staging service. Full source-unit coverage remains visible; reviewers still decide semantic completeness. Compact envelopes do not weaken the strict server schema. Archive input remains supported, and neither creation path reviews or publishes automatically. See [the agent workflow](authoring-agent-workflow.md).

`workflow.get_contract`, validation, submission, Context Pack, and Job Pack advertise V3. Readers accept V2 and V3. When `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1=1`, new Idea Bundle submission must use V3. Disabling the flag restores V2 submission without deleting V3 artifacts.

`authoring.withdraw_idea_bundle` accepts the same `runToken`, `bootstrapToken`, `importId` and exact `expectedRevision` identity as publication, with `authoring:withdraw`. The active authenticated admin is server-derived. Withdrawal uses the shared transactional lifecycle, preserves canonical entities owned by other published imports, and permits idempotent retries. No Admin website visit is required.

For an old published import whose run expired, omit `runToken` and explicitly send `recovery: "exact_import"` with a fresh Idea `bootstrapToken`, the import ID and its observed checksum. This withdrawal-only recovery verifies the validated artifact, course mapping, active actor and exact snapshot; it requires no Source Pack or new authoring run. It cannot review, publish or restage content. A supplied run token is still checked normally and is never silently bypassed.

`authoring.get_idea_review_context`, `authoring.review_idea_revision` and `authoring.publish_idea_bundle` use the authenticated admin, locked course/chapter run, Idea bootstrap and exact `expectedRevision`. Publication requires explicit `authoring:publish` consent and a complete current per-Idea review. The publishing admin's own exact-revision approval and complete item evidence determine eligibility. Another reviewer's rejection remains in history and the latest-decision status, but does not veto that approval. An identical publication retry is idempotent.

Draft replacement through MCP or Admin carries the caller's last-read checksum into `stageIdeaBundle` as `expectedPreviousChecksum`. The service locks the bundle identity and import row and checks that checksum before clearing reviews or writing a revision. Submission without a replacement identity creates a new bundle only. Before replacement bytes are processed, MCP also checks the target draft's checksum, course and complete chapter scope. Ideas, learning sections and chapter-scoped sources in both the target and replacement must match the run chapter before staging. Content-addressed objects from failed or superseded staging are retained for reference-aware cleanup, preventing a concurrent retry from deleting an active object.

MCP Idea and Product submission and restaging check any supplied or run-bound bootstrap against the authenticated actor and session before processing the artifact.

Discard removes the current draft and records its audit in one row-locked transaction. It retains shared artifact bytes for reference-aware garbage collection, including concurrent discard retries.

Admin item review, whole-bundle review and publication require the checksum displayed with the reviewed artifact. Item decisions are audited against that checksum, and the row-locked whole-bundle review records the same revision and item-hash evidence used by headless publication. Missing, stale or unaudited item decisions cannot approve a bundle. Replacement clears saved item decisions as well as bundle reviews. A legacy bundle-only approval does not become revision evidence; the reviewer must explicitly reaffirm it with every item decision in detailed Admin review or the headless revision review flow. Identical publication retries remain idempotent.

Scoped Idea and Product lifecycle tools require a run whose bootstrap was already bound to the authenticated actor and session by `workflow.start`. A newly supplied bootstrap does not upgrade an unbound legacy run. On `AUTHORING_MCP_LEGACY_RUN_RESTART_REQUIRED`, obtain a fresh playbook and restart the run through the catalog with the same scope and source. Existing legacy-compatible reads and submissions retain their explicitly permitted transition behavior.

An unchanged legacy bundle-only decision can be reaffirmed with complete item decisions even after another reviewer changes the global status. The reviewer must retain their original decision and notes. Admin exposes whether the current reviewer has revision evidence; those item controls are locked only once that evidence exists, so legacy reaffirmation remains available.

Unsaved item-note changes block bundle confirmation until the reviewer saves the item decision or explicitly discards the note changes. Reloaded and locked reviews display server-saved notes for the active checksum. Legacy confirmation displays the reviewer's original approval or rejection before reaffirmation. Product validation checks every Idea link on every Product; only database lookup IDs are deduplicated.

The Admin Idea editor blocks navigation, publication and review mutation until content is saved or explicitly cancelled. Cancel restores the saved draft; save locks every editor field until its exact submitted snapshot has completed.

Admin review workspaces guard same-origin links and browser Back and Forward, including query-driven views, while review or content changes are unsaved, and warn on reload or tab close. Pending requests and their context refresh must finish before leaving. Changed Idea content requires confirmation when it invalidates existing reviewers’ decisions; unchanged content saves do not restage.

Admin detail returns `reviewReset` with `revision`, `itemReviewCount`, `bundleReviewCount`, and an opaque keyed `fingerprint`. Counts cover every review row, including pending rows and other reviewers, without exposing their notes. A changed save sends `expectedRevision` and, after explicit confirmation of review deletion, `reviewResetFingerprint`. The shared staging transaction compares both under the import lock before deleting reviews. `IDEA_BUNDLE_REVIEW_RESET_REQUIRED` and `IDEA_BUNDLE_REVIEW_RESET_STALE` return HTTP 409; reload the summary and obtain a fresh explicit decision. A concurrent review can require confirmation even when the first summary was empty. The Admin refreshes the aggregate without replacing a local draft; if the revision changed, it keeps the old checksum and asks before discarding the draft to load the new revision. An unchanged replacement is a locked no-op and does not require reset acknowledgement.

Headless callers read the same aggregate from `authoring.get_import` as `import.reviewReset` and explicitly pass `reviewResetFingerprint` to `authoring.restage_idea_bundle`. The same reset errors include retry guidance. No browser interaction is required.

The [flexible revision contract](authoring-revisions.md) defines stable-ID MCP edits, persistent drafts separate from live content, release-impact planning, explicit affected review, mixed reference manifests and atomic replacement for Idea V3 and learning Product V3/V4/V5. The original profile-specific schema, source and publication gates remain required. Restoration creates a new draft rather than mutating history. The implementation is in progress; remote deployment acceptance is separate.

# Product Bundle V3 Contract

Product withdrawal requires the caller-observed checksum at both the Admin API and shared service. The MCP tool additionally requires a fresh session-bound bootstrap and either a bound learning-product run or explicit `recovery: "exact_import"` without a run. Exact-import recovery validates the staged checksum and course and remains withdrawal-only, without a Source Pack or Admin website step. The write transaction locks and rechecks the import snapshot before retiring projections; retry uses the same checksum.

V2/V3 archive reads recognize the [historical checksum format](product-bundle-v2.md#contract) without rewriting the artifact or stored identity. A match must cover the full canonical manifest and every non-manifest file using either the current serializer or the exact pre-2026-09-05 serializer. This does not relax any review, scope, dependency or withdrawal check, and does not apply to V4 or later.

Status: `ACTIVE` behind `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1` for new submission and structured review. V2 remains readable during transition.

An Article V3 stores `sections` and has no flat root blocks. A section contains stable identity, kind, title, slug, order, optional parent, learning objective, Idea links, source references, and semantic blocks. `topic` requires exactly one `learningSectionId`. `overview` and `summary` may synthesize multiple Ideas without one learning section.

Each block stores `contentMarkdown`, `blockType`, optional title, Idea IDs, and source references as fields. Metadata is never embedded in Markdown. The compiler preserves block types in the semantic AST and derives `artikel.contentMarkdown` deterministically for compatibility, search, and vector indexing.

- Every Idea is covered and traceable to a source.
- Every topic has a learning objective, core explanation, understanding check, and provenance.
- Examples, analogies, visuals, formulas, misconceptions, and warnings are required only when pedagogically relevant.
- Each topic declares a structured learning-time estimate for reading, examples, and practice. Completeness is judged against its objectives, not a fixed word count or reading-duration target.
- A chapter has overview, synthesis or summary, and a final understanding check.
- Pedagogy metadata binds objectives to explanation and formative-check blocks, declares prerequisites and symbols, and records whether a visual is required or not relevant.
- Formative checks are learning interactions only. `checkKind` supports `multiple_choice`, `short_answer`, `numeric_answer`, and `conceptual_explanation`. An optional typed `evaluation` uses `choice`, `text_exact`, `numeric`, or `ai_rubric` respectively. Without `evaluation`, the published check remains readable and reveal-only.
- `feedbackPolicy` is optional and may contain up to three progressive hints plus `allowRetry`. Evaluation and reveal routes authorize the published Article version and course enrollment, and never write attempts, grades, mastery, or assessment rows.
- Required visuals use typed, non-executable payloads. A mathematically sampled graph is explanatory evidence only and never replaces an analytic proof.
- Function plots may set `equalAxisScale: true` when geometric shape matters, such as circles and conics. This preserves the same display length per unit on both axes during zoom and pan. Included roots use filled markers; a hollow marker must not imply an excluded point when the function is defined there.
  Optional bounded `pointMarkers` identify excluded points (`open`) and defined values (`closed`), with finite coordinates, a label, and a valid series reference. Series may declare bounded `excludedX` inputs so sampling never joins branches across an undefined input or vertical asymptote. Static fallback must explain the same distinction.
  Embedded Article plots retain authored equations. Their fallback values are available through the keyboard-accessible "Nilai grafik" control rather than repeating a table below every graph; textual fallback remains available before the client renderer loads.
- MCP quality reports warn when a graph-relevant section has no linked visual, when one display formula joins multiple relations with commas, or when explanatory passages, worked-example steps, and verification repeat within a section. These warnings require editorial review; they do not prove a visual is always necessary or automatically rewrite content.
- Display formulas may use a short Markdown list with one relation per item. The quality count preserves mathematical inequalities such as `x<1` and does not mistake commas inside set notation for a crowded formula.

`review_item_bundle` identifies `targetType` and `targetId`. V3 Article review targets `article_section`; the V2 block endpoint remains an adapter for `article_block`.

Admin edits require `expectedRevision`, accept only safe content fields, recompute generation hashes and bundle checksum, preserve approval for unchanged sections, reset changed section approval, and mark an Article to Diktat dependency `STALE`. Stable IDs, provenance, and lineage identity cannot be edited.

Publication requires the approving admin to decide every Article section and record the exact checksum, current full-bundle fingerprint, policy version and eight anchored rubric criteria. Approval requires every section approved. A different reviewer cannot reuse another reviewer's approval. Multi-Article bundles review every Article and linked Diktat, independent of file order, and require current PDF evidence for each pair. Missing or stale approvals, stale dependencies, failed visual contracts, and missing, failed, or stale Diktat PDF evidence block publication. Publishing is transactional and idempotent.

The Diktat PDF worker compiles the authored Diktat from the linked Article and Diktat revision into a fixed two-column print layout with 10.5 pt body text, 1.38 line height, 12 pt section headings, and formulas at 1.05 em. Formula groups stay together across page and column breaks. The readable-v3 profile preserves the 4-page maximum without automatic font shrinking. It separates formula groups from symbol lists, renders formulas fail-closed, repeats contact details, a clickable website link, and current/total page numbers in the footer. The print header spans both columns to prevent a blank first page; paragraphs stay together. It records renderer and print-profile identity, verifies a 1 to 4 page PDF, then stores revision-bound evidence outside the ZIP. Only transient renderer, timeout, and storage failures are retried. Admins may render, retry, and preview this artifact. Students may download the published PDF only when authorized for the course. The generic storage proxy cannot expose protected Product Diktat keys.

section: Private local PDF operator for legacy drafts
content:
This path is for an explicitly authorized operator using the verified production target and an exact V2 or V3 learning-only draft containing an Article, with or without a linked Diktat. Allowed products are Article, Diktat, flashcard set and flashcard. It rejects assessment products, V4/V5 content and other versions. V4 continues to require its trusted verification receipt. This command creates PDF evidence only. It does not approve or publish a bundle.

First obtain the deployed 40-character source SHA from the authorized deployment record. The operator checks that the local canonical repository is clean and at that SHA, but cannot independently discover the deployed SHA. From current review context obtain the import ID, checksum and the original run that last created or replaced that draft. The actor must be the authorized active admin, including both the current admin membership and the legacy admin role. Production database and private storage targets use the same guard as the V4 local operator. Do not execute against an unverified target.

If the staging identity belongs to an Admin upload or edit rather than the current MCP run, an authorized active admin may call `authoring.adopt_product_draft_run` with the verified product run and bootstrap, import ID, exact checksum and `expectedStagingRunId` from current review context. The transaction records both identities and invalidates existing PDF evidence, verification and bundle review. Fetch context again and use its new `stagingRunId`; perform fresh verification and review. The artifact and checksum remain unchanged. A changed draft, actor, scope or staging identity fails the claim.

Discover the installed and reviewed browser pins with `node scripts/authoring/run-product-legacy-local.mjs --capabilities`. Use the pinned local Playwright Chromium, never a hosted renderer or CI fallback. A private settings JSON file outside the checkout, or ignored by Git, has the same format as the V4 operator: `{ "sourceRevision": "<deployed-sha>", "environment": { "DATABASE_URL": "...", "STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE": "neon", "NEON_STORAGE_BUCKET": "zyx-production", "AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3": "...", "AWS_REGION": "ap-southeast-1", "AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID": "...", "AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY": "...", "ZYX_ENVIRONMENT": "production", "ZYX_MCP_ENVIRONMENT": "production", "NODE_ENV": "production", "NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL": "https://www.zyxacademy.com", "BETTER_AUTH_URL": "https://www.zyxacademy.com", "AUTHORING_VERIFICATION_BROWSER_PROVIDER": "local_playwright" } }`. The production target guard validates the exact database and storage endpoint. Supply any other required server settings there as needed. Never paste real settings into a bundle, log or MCP response.

Create an input JSON file at an absolute path, with no secrets:

```json
{
  "privateFile": "/absolute/private/settings.json",
  "sourceRevision": "<40 lowercase hexadecimal characters>",
  "importId": "impor-product-<32 lowercase hexadecimal characters>",
  "runId": "mcp-run-<original staging UUID>",
  "expectedChecksum": "<64 lowercase hexadecimal characters>",
  "actorId": "<authorized admin ID>"
}
```

Run `node scripts/authoring/run-product-legacy-local.mjs --input /absolute/path/input.json`. Input is limited to 16 KiB and private settings to 128 KiB. Discovery returns `zyx-product-legacy-local-capabilities.v1`. The exact input and result JSON schemas are also available as `productBundle.legacyLocalOperator` from `workflow.get_contract`. Successful output contains `zyx-product-legacy-local-result.v1`, `status: "ready"`, the exact identity, browser version and revision, print profile, page count, PDF checksum, output directory and inventory of checksummed PDF, PNG and page text JSON files. Output may include JSON progress lines. A failed evidence attempt emits a `status: "failed"` result, followed by sanitized error JSON on stderr and a nonzero exit. Other errors emit sanitized stderr JSON and exit nonzero.

Each linked Diktat and each Article without a linked Diktat is an export target. Run once for each. If there is more than one target, provide `"diktatId": "<exact product ID>"` or `"articleId": "<exact product ID>"`; the fields are mutually exclusive. Omit both only for one eligible target. Each Diktat must link to its own Article revision. An Article-only export prints its ordered authored content and stores evidence under the Article ID. Its Article generation hash is also stored as self-lineage in the required legacy `diktatHash` column; no Diktat entity is created. The existing gate checks the actual Article version and hash. Formative answers remain protected. Safe inline links print their label and destination without fetching remote resources; unsupported reference-link syntax and unsafe protocols fail the export. Unsupported media, missing visual assets, invalid math, overflow or page-budget violations fail the attempt rather than omit content. Correct the source and restage if needed.

The process uses the existing compiler, print inspection and 1 to 4 page text inspection, verifies storage readback before marking evidence ready, then reads the stored PDF again and checksums the local files. It blocks external browser requests, limits the PDF and HTML sizes, runs one local process at a time and terminates its process group after 180 seconds. Artifacts are private local files under `artifacts/legacy-local-evidence/`. Inspect every page PNG and PDF for legibility, formulas, missing content and clipping before review. PDF readiness does not replace explicit semantic review by the authorized reviewer, which may be performed by an agent through the scoped MCP tools, or publication checks.

If the source, actor, staging audit or revision changes, obtain fresh context and make a new exact-revision decision. If the operator reports a lock, wait for the running process; only after verifying it exited, remove the indicated `zyx-product-local-<uid>.lock` directory in the system temporary directory. On timeout or interrupted export, check current evidence and readback before retrying. A pending or failed attempt is not ready. If the pinned browser is missing or mismatched, install the version reported by capabilities in the authorized local environment. On content or page-budget failure, correct and restage content, then use its new checksum and staging run. Never substitute a manually uploaded PDF, local assertion or V4 receipt for the required evidence.

The request outcome GET may add `supersededByAttemptId` to an accepted outcome. This is a live attestation under the import lock that matching current-lineage evidence replaced the original attempt. The original acceptance audit stays immutable. The client adopts that exact replacement after a fresh detail read; it never treats an unrelated older ready PDF as acceptance. Once reconciled, status follows server evidence without a separate local pending mask.

A UUID saved before registration can remain unknown. If the bundle revision changes, the client can settle that original UUID and revision through POST. Registration either replays its terminal outcome or durably rejects the stale revision before any rendering. It does not submit a new render against the current revision. A request scope conflict offers the original account or an explicit stop of local tracking after refreshing current server readiness. That action removes only the browser pointer, leaving server request records and publication gates intact.

Admin and student previews use the same semantic section renderer. The admin review surface shows section decisions and PDF readiness below the full-width article. A legacy PDF request reserves a checksum-bound pending evidence ID and audit record under the import lock before enqueue. The response includes `attemptId` and `duplicate`; concurrent requests for the same active attempt reuse the ID without sending another event. The event uses that ID for provider deduplication and the worker claims the same evidence. Pending evidence blocks older artifacts in status, review and publication, including across tabs and before a worker starts. Queue rejection marks only its own pending attempt failed. A transient worker retry keeps the same attempt and deadline. After 15 minutes from acceptance, status reports `failed` with `RENDER_TIMEOUT`, even if no worker wrote anything; an explicit retry reserves a new ID. The stored pending row continues to block publication until replaced, and an expired or superseded worker cannot commit. A pending attempt for an older checksum is reported as stale for the new revision and does not prevent a new request. The status refresh preserves review and content drafts for the unchanged revision; a revision change requires explicit reconciliation. A failed status refresh is not an active request: the reviewer can retry, or explicitly confirm leaving and discarding unsaved work. An interrupted POST requires a correlated outcome lookup; a terminal outcome then triggers draft-preserving status reconciliation before render or publication actions can resume. An unresolved outcome or failed reconciliation shows an unknown status, hides last-known ready links and offers a status retry. The history guard retains its origin during URL-tab replacements and advances it for inline item pushes, without bypassing Next URL-hook synchronization. It tracks entry positions before drafts become dirty. If an incoming position cannot be identified, it restores the origin by pushing its saved URL and state, discards unknown forward entries, and offers the intended destination after confirmation; it never probes an unknown document. Once current-lineage evidence exists for the current renderer print profile, selection uses that profile for status, review and publication, including pending or failed retries. Older-profile imports retain their fallback until then. V4 remains bound to its receipt. Internal Idea and provenance identifiers remain in the data model but are omitted from the reading surface and student view.

When `FEATURE_STRUCTURED_ARTICLE_READER_V1=1`, new Product Bundle submission must use V3 or later. An explicit V2 restage remains available only for the exact existing V2 draft and checksum in a verified matching run scope. The student material reader always prefers published canonical Article rows. Disabling the flag restores V2 submission without deleting V3 data or hiding published products.

PDF page images can be reused in `contentMarkdown` through the absolute `imageUrl` from a completed `source.read_file` or `source.get_read_job` response after requesting `representation: "image"` or `"both"`, followed by its human-readable `citation.label`. Preserve the source title, PDF page position, and document checksum in provenance. Never invent bibliographic details. Page renders are not isolated figures or typed interactive visuals and do not satisfy a typed-visual requirement.

Publication on both Admin and MCP requires the displayed 64-character checksum and an explicit whole-bundle approval by the publishing admin for that revision. Pedagogic approval alone cannot create or replace it. Readiness uses the same publisher, current dependency and V4 receipt checks on both surfaces. Restaging compares parsed Article and Diktat content before retaining PDF evidence, independently of the declared generation hash. Section decisions are read under the import lock before preservation.

Readiness and publication select the same PDF evidence row for the current Article and Diktat lineage. V4 additionally requires the current plan, attempt, signed receipt, print profile, page count and exact receipt artifact key; attachment must succeed before verification completes. A canonical Diktat version with a different existing file key is a version conflict and requires a new reviewed version. Legacy Article-owned PDF fallback follows the same selection policy in both gates.

MCP restaging checks the existing target artifact before processing replacement bytes, for every supported profile. Its exact checksum, course and chapter must match the active run, and it must contain learning products only. A historical assessment draft cannot be replaced through the learning-product tools, even with a learning-only replacement. The staging transaction still compares the caller's checksum before any review is cleared.

Refreshing PDF readiness preserves unsaved Admin rubric entries and decision notes when checksum, content fingerprint and policy are unchanged. If those identities change, the old draft remains visible and publication is blocked; opening the new revision requires explicit confirmation before discarding that draft.

Scoped lifecycle and verification tools require the actor and session bootstrap to be bound to the run at creation. A separate fresh bootstrap cannot upgrade an unbound legacy run. Restart through `workflow.start` with the same scope and source, then adopt an existing Product draft into that run when required by its staging identity before repeating verification and review.

Admin content-editor cancellation restores the server content without clearing review entries. Saving content applies the same revision-change confirmation as PDF refresh. PDF rendering and bundle review remain disabled while the content editor is open. Rubric and decision-note controls are disabled during submission. Closing mobile notes hides the field while preserving its text.

Local Product verifier launchers share one machine lock across imports, checkouts and legacy/V4 profiles, including capability discovery. The lock is acquired before bundling; each launch uses a private temporary module and cleans it up on exit. If a process is forcibly killed, first verify that no operator remains, then remove the per-user `zyx-product-local-<uid>.lock` directory under the operating system temporary directory before retrying. Per-import locks still protect the exact V4 attempt.

Structured section notes block bundle decisions, navigation, content edits and PDF requests while dirty or saving. Reviewers must save the section or explicitly discard its note changes; the section input is locked while saving. Non-Article legacy learning bundles expose approve and reject decisions, not the unsupported pedagogic request-changes action.

Admin review workspaces guard same-origin links and browser Back and Forward, including query-driven views, while review or content changes are unsaved, and warn on reload or tab close. Pending requests and their context refresh must finish before leaving. Changed Idea content requires confirmation when it invalidates existing reviewers’ decisions; unchanged content saves do not restage.

The optional Admin PDF route binds each action to one Diktat and a client-generated UUID. `POST /api/admin/bundles/product/{importId}/pdf` requires JSON `{ "productId": string, "expectedRevision": string, "requestId": UUID }`. The checksum is the exact 64-character lowercase revision. The authenticated admin is part of the request scope. The server registers that identity before loading the staged ZIP, and records acceptance with the pending evidence under the import lock before sending the worker event. Accepted POST responses use HTTP 202 and include `{ "requestId", "outcome": "accepted", "attemptId", "duplicate" }`, plus the target, revision and pending status. The accepted attempt may be shared with an already pending attempt for the same target and revision. Its original event retains its original actor.

After an ambiguous transport error, query `GET /api/admin/bundles/product/{importId}/pdf?outcome=1&requestId={uuid}&productId={productId}&expectedRevision={checksum}` with the same authenticated actor. HTTP 200 returns `{ "requestId", "outcome": "unknown" | "processing" | "accepted" | "rejected", "attemptId"?, "duplicate"?, "error"? }`. `unknown` means the request has not yet registered, and a delayed POST may still arrive. `processing` means registered without a final outcome. `accepted` names the exact attempt, while `rejected` is terminal for that request and has a safe error code. Reusing a UUID with another actor, import, product or revision returns `PRODUCT_DIKTAT_REQUEST_CONFLICT` (409). Explicit rejections include `outcome: "rejected"`; an invalid body or authorization failure is not a registered outcome. An unexpected service failure does not establish rejection.
