Quiz attempts check the attempt and student IDs; article progress checks the article, version and section; material progress checks student and material IDs; interventions check every row's student ID. Student endpoints that support `x-student-id` compare that expected actor with the authenticated session. These checks complement server authorization; a key or header never grants access.

Legacy SQL count strings are accepted only where existing endpoints or stored JSON actually return them. Conversion accepts digit strings and then enforces a nonnegative integer, rejecting null, booleans, empty strings and fractional values. Preserve documented nullable and optional fields without filling required fields with made-up defaults.

The stored quiz answer map remains an explicit unknown-value boundary because it also contains the server's attachment registry. Review code narrows each rendered answer by question type; submission code builds its own allowed answer snapshot instead of sending that registry back.

Pass the query function's `signal` to its GET. Cache cancellation and removal can then stop obsolete requests. Mutation functions do not receive an automatic AbortSignal from TanStack Query; explicit controllers, upload cancellation and keepalive behavior remain feature decisions.

`lib/query/client.ts` creates a fresh client for server execution and one stable client in the browser. Default query freshness is 30 seconds and inactive retention (`gcTime`) is five minutes. Freshness controls when data needs a refresh; inactive retention controls when an unused entry can be removed. Neither is a browser HTTP cache policy.

Default focus refetch is off. TanStack's stale mount/reconnect behavior remains available unless a feature overrides it. Safe reads may retry once for an HTTP 5xx or network `TypeError`; authentication failures, other 4xx, rate limits, invalid responses and cancellation do not retry. Mutations default to no retry. Reads with side effects or provider/job implications explicitly disable retry.

| Domain | `staleTime` | Automatic refresh | Retry |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Today's plan | 60 s | Learning invalidation; sidebar focus/visibility refresh with a 60 s success throttle | None; GET also updates streak/recommendations |
| Sidebar enrollment fallback | 0 | Enabled after Today fails; refreshed for the failed scope | At most one transient read retry |
| Sidebar course metadata | 5 min | Account/course change and stale remount | At most one transient read retry |
| Study path | 60 s | Course/day key changes and learning invalidation | None; GET may compute/persist a path |
| Article progress | 60 s | Starts from the actor's RSC progress; later read refresh and write receipts | At most one transient read retry |
| Quiz attempt review | 30 s | Every 3 s while feedback is needed, for a 30 s window; explicit retry starts another window | None; review reads record disclosures |
| Quiz analytics | 30 s | Every 4 s while status is `processing`; stops on error or terminal status | None; GET can enqueue missing analytics |
| Admin ops metrics | 55 s | Every 60 s | At most one transient read retry |
| Admin AI analytics | 25 s | Every 30 s | At most one transient read retry |
| Admin key diagnostics | 25 s | Every 30 s | At most one transient read retry |
| Admin feature flags | 20 s | Every 30 s | At most one transient read retry |
| Admin usage range | 60 s | Range change or stale remount | At most one transient read retry |
| Admin products and leaderboard | 30 s | Filters, explicit refresh and relevant mutation invalidation | At most one transient read retry |
| Zyra ops and proposal lists | 30 s | Manual ops refresh; proposal settlement invalidates actor lists | At most one transient read retry |
| Student interventions | 30 s | Learning invalidation; confirmed dismiss invalidates its account entry | At most one transient read retry |
| Discussion counts | 60 s | Every 120 s and the existing counts-changed event | At most one transient read retry |
| Zyra allowance | 30 s | Course change and the owner's `refreshKey` invalidation | None |
| Public pricing | 0 | Every 30 s; always refresh on focus | None |

All configured polling uses `refetchIntervalInBackground: false`. Domain intervals preserve the existing product cadence; a global interval is not added. Most entries inherit the five-minute inactive retention. Quiz submission mutations set `gcTime: 0` to avoid retaining settled answer payloads unnecessarily.

`invalidateLearningQueries` refreshes Today, study paths, interventions and the flashcard domain for the current actor. It also targets the attempt and analytics when an attempt ID is known. If Today has a pending optimistic completion, it marks Today stale without fetching over the optimistic items; the last completion settles that read. These invalidations target client summaries, not every server-rendered page.

| Write | Required behavior |
|---|---|
| Today completion | Cancel the matching read, save only the item's previous `done` value, update it optimistically, roll back only that item, and refresh after the last pending completion. Concurrent items must not restore whole-list snapshots over one another. |
| Quiz submit | Keep the immediate duplicate-submit lock, deadline handling, answer snapshot and upload wait. Use `networkMode: 'always'` and `retry: false` so an offline submission fails visibly. Mutation keys alone do not deduplicate writes. |
| Article progress | Validate the receipt and merge progress monotonically. Do not replay an uncertain elapsed-time delta. After a failed completion, further scroll events cannot resubmit it; an explicit finish action can retry with only new elapsed time. Until a read or receipt confirms completion, ordinary visibility/exit writes preserve fresh time but cap that section's depth at 89%, below the API's 90% completion threshold. Preserve small `keepalive` PUT writes during navigation and exit. Multiple section completions share summary invalidation. |
| Material progress/status | Use the extracted tracker and typed mutation adapters. Reading and status writes share a per-account/material mutation scope to preserve order. Website-material time writes use `keepalive`; canonical Article/Diktat and PDF status retain the authorized Server Action. |
| Chapter summary | Generate only on explicit request through `useChapterSummary`; validate the result and disable retries. It can spend provider allowance and is not a polling query. |
| Flashcard review | Validate the Server Action input/result; keep the current queue local. A successful write appends a review and advances SM-2, so automatic retry and offline replay remain off. |
| Intervention dismiss | Require a successful, validated acknowledgment before animating away. Failure keeps the suggestion visible; invalidate only its account entry. |
| Proposal create/review/confirm | Preserve explicit user actions and exact version preconditions. No optimistic lifecycle transition or automatic write retry. Re-read all proposal lists for the actor after settlement, including ambiguous failures. |
| Pricing settings | Validate the save result before updating the shared public pricing entry. |

`mutationOptions` and `useMutation` own request state, not server idempotency. A shared mutation `scope.id` serializes calls; it does not turn repeated requests into one operation. Keep critical cache updates in the mutation's configured callbacks. Per-call callbacks are suitable for mounted UI effects such as the dismiss animation, since they can disappear after unmount.

`queryCacheUpdated` on the existing learning activity event prevents the sidebar from repeating invalidation already performed by a migrated feature. Other event consumers and local study state remain intact. Browser `keepalive` improves the chance that a small request survives navigation; it does not guarantee delivery after the process exits. No mutation cache is persisted for later offline replay.

Live session consumers call `useSyncQueryAccount` only after Better Auth has a confirmed session result. A temporary pending state does not clear private data. Confirmed account changes cancel and remove another actor's queries and mutation entries while preserving public pricing. The shared `signOut` wrapper clears private state after successful sign-out. In-flight server mutations cannot be undone by cache removal; their completion callbacks check the current actor before changing a cache.

RSC-provided progress or attempt props can outlive a browser account change. `useQueryAccountCurrent` fences those consumers until navigation supplies current data. Components with account-specific local state reset through account keys. Demo adapters bypass private server reads and preserve their existing local behavior.

Keep initial course/content loading and authoritative access in RSC and server services. Do not import database modules, provider credentials or server-only contracts into client query modules. If server prefetch/hydration is added, create the server QueryClient per request and hydrate only authorized data. Avoid two independently displayed copies of one mutable response in an RSC and a client query without an explicit refresh policy.

The Query cache, Next.js route/data caches and RSC request memoization are separate. `invalidateQueries` does not invoke `revalidatePath`, refresh the Router Cache, or regenerate server HTML. Preserve existing server revalidation and `router.refresh()` where a mutation affects server-rendered content. Imperative client reads use `client.query(options)` with the same factory as their hook.

Repeated browser reads should use an authenticated GET backed by the existing server service, as the sidebar navigation extraction does. Server Actions remain useful for authorized mutations and their revalidation behavior. Introducing another client read mechanism is unnecessary for data already rendered once on the server.

The current migration covers shared Query infrastructure; Today and sidebar reads; study paths; intervention reads/dismissal; quiz player/submission/review/analytics boundaries; article progress and material progress/status/summary logic; flashcard review and local session logic; discussion counts; Zyra allowance and proposals; pricing; admin ops, diagnostics, flags, usage, product catalog and leaderboard reads.

The product catalog panel currently appears in the admin loading visual fixture; this does not establish broad live catalog use. Article bodies and flashcard queues retain their server/local owners. The following inventory comes from repository client fetches, imported Server Action reads and their consumers. It is an ownership map, not proof that all runtime data paths have been exercised.

| Flow | Current locations | Reason |
|---|---|---|
| Server content, authorization and database work | `app/**/page.tsx`, `lib/student/course-access.ts`, server repositories and jobs | Retain server access decisions, bounded projections, transactions and initial HTML. Query is a browser response cache. |

| Live quiz and terminal transport | `components/live/use-live-quiz-socket.ts`, `lib/coding/remote-runtime.ts`, `lib/coding/remote-warm.ts` | Preserve WebSocket tickets, ordered events, command state and connection cleanup. |

| Coding drafts | `components/coding/use-coding-draft.ts` | Keep local recovery, revision conflicts and the ordered save queue; a read refresh must not overwrite unsaved code. |

Material reading is already extracted into typed keepalive mutations. The old `MaterialViewer` timer/API mix and its `sendBeacon` path are not listed as remaining migration work.

| Domain | Remaining sources | Suggested boundary |
|---|---|---|
| Notifications | `components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx` | Account-scoped unread/history queries; validated bodies and invalidation after read actions and foreground FCM events. Preserve toast delivery. |
| Coding problem/history | `components/coding/article-coding.tsx`, `components/coding/live-coding-exercise.tsx`, `components/coding/coding-workspace.tsx` | Shared problem/version reads; history keyed by actor, course, problem and surface; poll only pending submissions. Keep runtime and editor state local. |

A separate migration must preserve cursors, signed observations, read-through state and revision checks. Only count badges have migrated. |

Existing action TypeScript types do not supply the shared runtime response validation/cache policy. |

These are follow-up opportunities, not completed migrations or requirements to rewrite each feature in this PR. Choose work by repeated reads, stale-data risk, user impact and validation cost. Preserve domain-specific concurrency rules while extracting the read layer.

Focused tests cover key isolation, malformed responses, cancellation, retry limits, concurrent optimistic completion, late account results, quiz state/submission, article/material progress, flashcard review contracts, admin filters and proposal/dismissal behavior. Relevant suites live under `tests/unit/` and `tests/contracts/`; feature browser checks live under `tests/visual/`.

The Query lifecycle workflow runs a production build against a disposable PostgreSQL database with the full migration chain. It also runs the quiz, learning, dashboard and admin browser fixtures at 380 x 844 and 1536 x 864, and keeps the report, screenshots and traces as a CI artifact. The primary agent must inspect every required capture before visual signoff.

Record the exact commit, commands, results and remaining boundaries in the PR. Fixture responses and a disposable build database do not establish authenticated staging behavior, provider usage, database contention, navigation-exit delivery or measured performance savings. CI success and merge status do not establish deployment status.

- [TanStack Query options](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-options): colocated typed keys, functions and options.
- [Query keys](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-keys): serializable inputs and deterministic hashing.
- [Important defaults](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/important-defaults): freshness, inactive retention and automatic refetch.
- [Query functions](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-functions) and [cancellation](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-cancellation): error handling and AbortSignal consumption.
- [Retries](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/query-retries) and [network mode](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/network-mode): retry and offline behavior.
- [Mutations](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/mutations) and [useMutation](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/reference/useMutation): lifecycle callbacks, serial scopes and retry defaults.
- [Optimistic updates](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/optimistic-updates) and [invalidation after mutations](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/invalidations-from-mutations): cancellation, rollback and reconciliation.
- [QueryClient](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/reference/QueryClient) and [advanced server rendering](https://tanstack.com/query/latest/docs/framework/react/guides/advanced-ssr): imperative reads, request isolation and data ownership.
- [Next.js data fetching](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/fetching-data) and [updating data](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/updating-data): server/client reads and Server Action boundaries. For changes in this repository, also read the installed Next.js guides under `node_modules/next/dist/docs/`.
- [Zod basics](https://zod.dev/basics): runtime parsing and inferred types.

# Database Guide

Zyx Academy uses PostgreSQL via Drizzle ORM (`db/schema.ts`, `lib/db/index.ts`). Staging and production run on separate Neon PostgreSQL branches with separate private Neon S3-compatible object-storage buckets (`STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon`). The adapter requires PostgreSQL in development, CI, staging, and production; it never falls back to SQLite or Turso.

| Environment | Engine | Neon Project / Branch | Database | Object Storage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Local development & CI | PostgreSQL (or PGlite for isolated contract tests) | Local or isolated test DB | Local / PGlite | Local / configured bucket |
| Staging | Neon PostgreSQL | Project `muddy-sky-44104897`, branch `br-gentle-scene-azq0gp91` | `neondb` | Private bucket `zyx-staging` (`STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon`) |
| Production | Neon PostgreSQL | Project `muddy-sky-44104897`, protected root `br-wandering-butterfly-azi11h8r` | `neondb` | Private bucket `zyx-production` (`STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon`) |

- Use the pooled Neon endpoint (`-pooler`) for application traffic and the direct endpoint for migrations and administrative operations.
- Keep environment-specific credentials in ignored `.env` files (`.env.local`, `.env.staging`, `.env.prod`). Never commit credentials or print `DATABASE_URL` in logs.
- Legacy Turso/SQLite and R2 resources are retained strictly as cold recovery backups and are never used by serving traffic.

docTitle: 3. Apply pending migrations to the verified target
content:
All schema changes are authored in `db/schema.ts` and generated into `drizzle-postgres/` (42 migrations through `0041_discussion_search_indexes.sql`):

```bash
# 1. Edit db/schema.ts (Drizzle ORM PostgreSQL schema)
# 2. Generate SQL migration files in drizzle-postgres/
bun run db:generate
# 3. Apply pending migrations to the verified target
bun run db:migrate
```

Rules:
- Never hand-edit generated migration files in `drizzle-postgres/`.
- `bun run db:push:prod` is intentionally disabled. Remote migrations must run through the guarded PostgreSQL migrator (`db/postgres-migrate.ts`) after verifying the exact Neon project, branch, host, and database.
- Take a Neon branch snapshot before applying destructive or backfill-dependent migrations to staging or production.
- Web and worker deployments do not run migrations or seeds automatically. Apply schema migrations before releasing code that depends on new columns, tables, or indexes.

docTitle: 3. Apply pending migrations to the verified target
content:
- **Timestamps**: PostgreSQL columns use `timestamptz`. Always normalize dates and Jakarta day boundaries through `lib/date-utils.ts`.
- **Dual hashing**: Content entities track `sourceHash` (raw content) and `derivedHash` (structured attributes) to avoid unnecessary regeneration on cosmetic edits.
- **External vector storage**: Semantic embeddings (768-dimensional Gemini embeddings) live in Cloudflare Vectorize, synchronized transactionally via `vector_sync_queue` and `admin_ops_knowledge_sync_queue`.
- **Idempotent outboxes**: Gamification awards, vector sync, and queue task checkpoints (`queue_task_checkpoints`) use transactional outbox tables so background workers can retry safely without duplicate side effects.

# Deployment Guide

This guide defines the current production and staging deployment topology for Zyx Academy across web, background workers, edge services, and native mobile and desktop applications.

```text
Clients (Web Browser / Capacitor Mobile / Tauri Desktop)
 ├── Web Tier
 │    ├── Production: Vercel (Next.js 16.3, region sin1)
 │    └── Staging: Vercel custom staging OR Cloud Run Bangkok (via Cloudflare Edge Worker)
 ├── Data & Storage
 │    ├── Neon PostgreSQL (separate staging & production branches)
 │    └── Neon Object Storage (private buckets, STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon)
 ├── Background Execution
 │    ├── Queue Provider: Inngest Cloud (default) or Google Cloud Tasks + Scheduler
 │    └── Compute Worker: Neon Functions (workers/neon-background, function zyxcompute)
 └── Cloudflare Edge & AI Services
      ├── Cloudflare AI Gateway (dynamic multi-provider routing & BYOK)
      ├── Cloudflare Vectorize (768d canonical & admin_ops_knowledge indexes)
      ├── Cloudflare Workers KV (AI catalog cache & shared tutor cache)
      └── Cloudflare Workers (vector-api, zyra-control-plane, realtime, diktat-renderer, python-runtime, staging-web-edge)
```

| Target | Branch | Trigger | Workflow | Notes |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| CI Validation | PR, `staging`, `main` | Automatic | `.github/workflows/ci.yml` | Runs `scripts/ci/plan.py` dependency-scoped lint, typecheck, and tests |
| Production Web | `main` | Gated CI or manual dispatch | `.github/workflows/deploy-web.yml` | Region `sin1` in `vercel.json`; respects `HOLD_WEB_DEPLOYMENT` |
| Staging Web (Vercel) | `staging` | Manual dispatch only | `.github/workflows/deploy-web.yml` | Targets custom environment `staging` (`--target=staging`), no branch tracking |
| Staging Web (Cloud Run) | `staging` | Manual dispatch only | `.github/workflows/deploy-cloud-run-staging.yml` | Dedicated `staging-cloud-run` environment; supports `candidate`, `promote`, `rollback`, `import-secrets` |
| Background Worker | `staging` / `main` | Manual (`staging`) / Gated (`main`) | `.github/workflows/deploy-neon-worker.yml` | Deploys `workers/neon-background` to Neon Functions and verifies function count and checksum |
| Mobile & Desktop Apps | `staging` / `main` | Manual dispatch only | `.github/workflows/release-apps.yml` | Channels `nightly` (staging) and `stable` (production) |
| Authoring Plugin Mirror | `main` | Manual dispatch only | `.github/workflows/sync-plugin.yml` | Mirrors packaged MCP skills to `soezyxstt/zyx-authoring-mcp` |

Web and worker releases never run database migrations or catalog seeds automatically. Apply guarded PostgreSQL migrations (`bun run db:migrate`) before deploying application code that relies on new schema objects.

- Hosted on Vercel project `zyxacademy` (`vercel.json` pins serverless functions to `sin1` to stay close to Neon `ap-southeast-1`).
- Connected to protected Neon production root `br-wandering-butterfly-azi11h8r` (`neondb`) and private bucket `zyx-production` with `STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon`.
- Keep `.vercelignore` intact so local environment files and temporary artifacts are excluded from CLI deploys.
- `deploy-web.yml` forwards `ANDROID_APP_LINKS_SHA256_FINGERPRINTS` from GitHub Environment `production` when configured so `/.well-known/assetlinks.json` stays current.

- **Vercel staging**: Uses custom environment `staging` inside project `zyxacademy` with Git branch tracking disabled. See [operations/vercel-staging.md](operations/vercel-staging.md).
- **Cloud Run staging**: Packages Next.js standalone output (`Dockerfile.cloud-run`) in Bangkok (`asia-southeast3`) behind `workers/staging-web-edge`. See [operations/cloud-run-staging.md](operations/cloud-run-staging.md).
- Both staging targets share Neon branch `br-gentle-scene-azq0gp91` (`neondb`), private bucket `zyx-staging`, and Neon Function `zyxcompute`.

Background jobs run on Neon Functions (`@neon/functions`), replacing the retired Deno Deploy runtime.

- Deploy via `.github/workflows/deploy-neon-worker.yml` (selecting `staging` or `production`).
- Readiness and smoke checks derive the expected function count directly from the canonical compute registration list and verify archive checksum parity.
- Ensure the web and worker revisions match whenever shared contracts (bundle V4 verification, queue payloads, or schema queries) change.

`QUEUE_PROVIDER` selects how background tasks are dispatched:

- `inngest` (default): Uses Inngest Cloud with per-environment `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`, `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`, and `INNGEST_ENV`.
- `cloud-tasks`: Uses Google Cloud Tasks queues (default queue + concurrency-2 PDF queue in Singapore) and Cloud Scheduler (`POST /internal/cron/tick` authenticated via Google OIDC ID token). Requires migration `0035_queue_task_checkpoints.sql`.
- `noop` / `memory`: Local test and development modes.

**Cloud Tasks rollback procedure**:
1. Pause the Cloud Scheduler dispatcher and stop new Cloud Tasks enqueues.
2. Record outstanding task identities and restore `QUEUE_PROVIDER=inngest` with verified Inngest function registration.
3. Reconcile pending outbox, PDF, and verification rows against terminal states before replaying.
4. Resume a single cron owner and confirm end-to-end delivery.

AI requests route through Cloudflare AI Gateway (`CF_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, `CF_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN`) with convention BYOK aliases and query-key fallback:

- **Dynamic discovery**: The model registry reads provider model-list metadata through AI Gateway without issuing generation probes or consuming quota. Discovered catalogs are cached in Workers KV for 12 hours (with a 14-day stale-usable window on upstream outage and a 5-minute retry delay).
- **Latency probes**: Scheduled at 00:00 and 12:00 UTC (or triggered manually in `/admin/ops/models`) using 3-sample median latency measurements with automatic retry on incomplete probes.
- **Alias cooldown**: Three consecutive failures place a provider alias into a 5-minute cooldown while healthy fallbacks serve traffic.
- **Control plane**: `workers/zyra-control-plane` coordinates distributed quota leases and health state (`ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN`). Deploy production updates with `bun run prod:zyra-control:deploy`.

- **Vector API (`workers/vector-api`)**: Proxies 768-dimensional Cloudflare Vectorize operations (`VECTORIZE_WORKER_URL`, `VECTORIZE_SHARED_SECRET`).
- **Diktat PDF Renderer (`workers/diktat-renderer`)**: Generates static Diktat PDFs via Cloudflare Browser Run (`DIKTAT_RENDERER_URL`, `DIKTAT_RENDERER_SECRET`). Deploy with `bun run staging:diktat-renderer:deploy` or `bun run prod:diktat-renderer:deploy`.
- **Realtime Classroom (`workers/realtime`)**: WebSocket worker for Live Quiz (`NEXT_PUBLIC_REALTIME_URL`, `LIVE_HMAC_SECRET`, gated by `FEATURE_LIVE=1`).
- **Python Runtime (`workers/python-runtime`)**: Isolated Python execution and WASI terminal ticket verification (`PYTHON_RUNTIME_TOKEN_SECRET`, `CODING_BROWSER_PROVIDER`).

Product Bundle V4 verification supports three browser providers configured via `AUTHORING_VERIFICATION_BROWSER_PROVIDER`:

- `local_playwright` (recommended production operator path): Runs Chromium locally on the operator machine against the deployed `/authoring-verification` client shell with build-fingerprint verification and signed receipt submission. See [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md#local-v4-verification).
- `cloudflare`: Uses Cloudflare Browser Rendering (`CF_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CF_API_TOKEN` or `CF_BROWSER_API_TOKEN`).
- `steel`: Uses Steel CDP sessions (`STEEL_API_KEY`, pinned `AUTHORING_VERIFICATION_STEEL_BROWSER_VERSION`).

Switching providers changes verification plan hashes and requires a fresh verification attempt and PDF receipt before publication.

Google Calendar sync requires migration `0040_google_calendar_sync.sql` before deploying matching web and worker code:

- Uses personal offline OAuth consent for individual users and the shared host `GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN` for Zyx primary calendar sync.
- Daily synchronization is dispatched via the configured queue provider, with manual sync available in the schedule toolbar.
- Follow the token rotation procedure in [DEVELOPMENT.md](DEVELOPMENT.md#replace-the-shared-google-host-token-through-oauth-playground) when adding or refreshing Calendar scopes.

Run **Release Apps (Desktop & Mobile)** (`.github/workflows/release-apps.yml`) manually from `staging` with channel `nightly`, or from `main` with channel `stable`. Web-only changes take effect through web deployment; reserve native releases for wrapper, plugin, signing, or offline asset changes.

The workflow produces:
- **Android**: Signed APK (`com.zyx.academy` for Stable, `com.zyx.academy.nightly` for Nightly) using separate Nightly and Stable Android signing keys and separate Firebase app configs (`FIREBASE_STABLE_GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON` / `FIREBASE_NIGHTLY_GOOGLE_SERVICES_JSON`).
- **Desktop (Tauri v2)**: Windows NSIS installer, macOS Apple Silicon DMG, Linux AppImage and Debian packages, plus signed `tauri-plugin-updater` artifacts (`TAURI_SIGNING_PRIVATE_KEY`, `TAURI_UPDATER_PUBKEY`).
- **iOS**: Distributed via TestFlight (no iOS binaries are published by GitHub Actions). Push notifications use HTTP/2 JWT APNs (`APNS_KEY_ID`, `APNS_TEAM_ID`, `APNS_PRIVATE_KEY`, `APNS_BUNDLE_ID`, `APNS_USE_SANDBOX`).

**Delta patches (Nightly)**:
- For each package, CI compares up to the two most recent Nightly releases and uploads a version-specific patch when it saves at least 20% of the full download, alongside full packages for fresh installs and recovery.
- Android verifies reconstructed APKs byte-for-byte before in-place install; Desktop verifies Tauri signatures or release SHA-256 checksums.
- To disable patches for a release, remove its `.zyxdelta`, `.zyxdelta-apk.gz`, and `.zyxdesktop.gz` assets while retaining full installers and checksums.

# Development Guide

This guide covers local setup, core commands, CI scope, environment variables, feature flags, AI Gateway configuration, bilingual development, and local operator tools for Zyx Academy.

- **Runtime**: Bun `1.3.14` (pinned in `package.json`), Node.js 22+
- **Database**: PostgreSQL (`DATABASE_URL`); isolated contract tests use PGlite automatically
- **Optional native wrappers**: Android Studio / Xcode for `apps/mobile`, Rust + Tauri v2 prerequisites for `apps/desktop`

```bash
bun install
cp .env.neon.example .env.local   # fill in local/dev secrets
bun run db:migrate                # apply drizzle-postgres/ migrations
bun run dev                       # http://localhost:3000 (Next.js 16.3 Turbopack)
```

Before running the full test suite locally, generate the authoring skills bundle once:

```bash
bun run build:authoring-skills
```

| Command | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `bun run dev` | Start Next.js 16.3 dev server (Turbopack) |
| `bun run build` | Build authoring skills, prepare V4 verification fingerprint, and run `next build` |
| `bun run start` | Start production server |
| `bun run lint` | Run ESLint |
| `bun run typegen` | Generate Next.js route types without building |
| `bun run typecheck` | Incremental application TypeScript check (`.cache/typecheck/app.tsbuildinfo`) |
| `bun run typecheck:tests` | TypeScript check for the full test project (`tsconfig.test.json`) |
| `bun run typecheck:structured-articles` | Typecheck structured Article contracts and compiler core |
| `bun run test` | Run Bun unit and contract tests |
| `bun run test:ai-contracts` | Run deterministic zero-network contract tests (`scripts/test-contracts.ts`) |
| `bun run i18n:check` | Validate paired `messages/id/` and `messages/en/` catalogs and key usage |
| `bun run audit:web-boundaries` | Verify client/server and worker import boundaries |
| `bun run audit:ui-separation` | Verify mobile/desktop UI separation boundaries |
| `bun run worker:deno:audit` | Audit background worker dependency graph |
| `bun run build:ops-docs` | Rebuild `lib/admin-ops-ai/ops-docs-index.json` from `docs/` and `AGENTS.md` |
| `bun run db:generate` | Generate Drizzle SQL migration in `drizzle-postgres/` |
| `bun run db:migrate` | Apply PostgreSQL migrations via `db/postgres-migrate.ts` |
| `bun run db:seed` | Seed local database with development fixtures |
| `bun run ci:plan -- --base <sha> --head HEAD` | Preview dependency-scoped CI plan locally |

`.github/workflows/ci.yml` runs automatically on pull requests and pushes to `staging` and `main`. Its first job runs `scripts/ci/plan.py` (Python standard library) to compute the exact dependency closure of changed files:

| Changed Input | Selected CI Work |
| --- | --- |
| Frontend / API / `lib/` code | Application typecheck, ESLint on changed files, affected Bun tests and test compilation; web release on `main` push |
| Background worker modules (`workers/neon-background`, `jobs/`) | Worker dependency audit, typecheck, and asset checks; worker release on `main` push |
| V4 renderer or fingerprinted CSS | V4 binding/verification contracts; coordinated web and worker release on `main` push |
| Schedule or Authoring domains | Dedicated schedule or authoring contract suites and locked skills checks |
| Documentation (`docs/`) | Web release on `main` push (for Admin Ops Knowledge); skips compiler checks when only prose changed |
| Lockfiles or CI planner | Full check suite conservatively |

Staging pushes run CI validation only and never auto-deploy web or workers. Use manual `workflow_dispatch` on branch `staging` for `deploy-cloud-run-staging.yml`, `deploy-web.yml`, or `deploy-neon-worker.yml`.

Test the CI planner locally:

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s .github/scripts -p 'test_*.py' -v
```
All environment variables are validated at startup by `lib/env.ts` (`@t3-oss/env-nextjs`). Never commit real secrets.

| Variable | Required | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `DATABASE_URL` | Yes | PostgreSQL connection URL (Neon pooled URL in staging/prod) |
| `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET` | Yes | 32+ char high-entropy secret (`openssl rand -base64 32`) |
| `BETTER_AUTH_URL` | Yes | Canonical public app origin for OAuth callbacks |
| `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` | Yes | Google Web application OAuth credentials |
| `GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN` | Optional | Shared Google Workspace host token (Meet, Forms, Sheets, Drive, Calendar) |
| `RESEND_API_KEY` | Yes | Transactional email API key |
| `GEMINI_API_KEY` (`_2`, `_3`, `_4`) | Yes (primary) | Gemini API keys with optional 4-slot failover and `GEMINI_PROJECT_ALIAS_1..4` |
| `QUEUE_PROVIDER` | Optional | `inngest` (default), `cloud-tasks`, `noop`, or `memory` |
| `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`, `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY` | Unless `cloud-tasks` | Inngest Cloud event and request-signing keys |

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE` | `neon` (serving staging/production) or `r2` (adapter default when unset) |
| `NEON_STORAGE_BUCKET`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3`, `AWS_REGION`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Private Neon S3-compatible object storage |
| `R2_ENDPOINT`, `R2_BUCKET`, `R2_PUBLIC_URL`, `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY` | Cloudflare R2 storage (optional/legacy) |

| Variable | Description |
| --- | --- |
| `CF_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, `CF_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN` | Cloudflare AI Gateway base URL and authorization token; required for provider dispatch |
| `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` | Distributed Zyra quota and health control-plane Worker |
| `CF_ACCOUNT_ID`, `CF_KV_NAMESPACE_ID`, `CF_API_TOKEN` | Cloudflare Workers KV for shared AI catalog and tutor cache |

The model registry in `/admin/ops/models` reads provider model lists through Cloudflare AI Gateway without generation probes or quota reservations:
- Discovered catalogs are cached in Workers KV for 12 hours (usable up to 14 days if upstream discovery fails, with a 5-minute retry delay).
- Background latency probes run at 00:00 and 12:00 UTC (or on demand via manual refresh) using 3-sample median latency with automatic retry on incomplete samples.
- Models sort newest first using verified release dates, then valid provider `created` timestamps; undated models remain selectable at the end. Video-only entries and quarantined models are excluded from text selection.
- Three consecutive failures trigger a 5-minute cooldown on the failing alias while fallback aliases serve traffic.
