section: Replace the Shared Google Host Token Through OAuth Playground
content:
1. Open Google OAuth 2.0 Playground and click the gear icon; enable **Use your own OAuth credentials** and enter the target environment's `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`.
2. Select all required Workspace scopes (Google Meet, Forms, Sheets, Drive, and Calendar events `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/calendar.events`) so existing integrations remain intact.
3. Authorize with the designated Zyx host account, exchange the authorization code for tokens, and copy the new refresh token.
4. Update `GOOGLE_REFRESH_TOKEN` in the target environment's secret store (never in Git) and verify manual and scheduled sync against a non-production account before rotating production.

When `AUTHORING_VERIFICATION_BROWSER_PROVIDER=local_playwright` is configured, operators verify staged Product Bundle V4 drafts locally against the deployed `/authoring-verification` shell:

1. Check out the exact clean Git revision matching the deployed web build.
2. Discover current browser and runtime pins:
   ```bash
   node scripts/authoring/run-product-v4-local.mjs --capabilities
   ```
3. Run verification for the exact import, staging run, and checksum:
   ```bash
   node scripts/authoring/run-product-v4-local.mjs --input <absolute-input-json-path>
   ```
4. The runner enforces target origin and build-fingerprint parity, renders via pinned local Chromium, captures evidence and PDF readback, and writes the signed verification receipt. Semantic review and publication remain separate MCP actions.

- **Mobile (Capacitor 7)**: See [apps/mobile/README.md](../apps/mobile/README.md). Point to a local server via `ZYX_MOBILE_SERVER_URL=http://10.0.2.2:3000 npm run sync:android`.
- **Desktop (Tauri v2)**: See [apps/desktop/README.md](../apps/desktop/README.md). Point to a local server via `ZYX_DESKTOP_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3000 npm run dev`.

# Discussions

The composer reuses the source-backed Zyra editor for live formatting and math, without separate write and preview tabs. Up to four image tiles stay in one horizontal row above the editor. A single help button contains the current channel audience, Zyra context, image policy and allowance information; validation and recovery remain inline. Open questions use normal text, answered questions use muted text, and resolved questions have a collapsed section with separate, lazy server pagination. Status remains available to assistive technology without visible status badges.

Local integration checks cover the production read-retry effect and callback with the real service and signed receipt. A later visible message saves at watermark 0 before the earlier gap closes to 2. The production React lifecycle and authenticated shell remain unverified. Staging schema migration passed on 2026-11-17; application acceptance remains open.

The post35 source repairs stop ordinary provider fallback immediately after an unconfirmed response, including malformed output. Structured repair and conversational tutoring preserve uncertainty in their failure result and telemetry. Admin and Tutor layout guards await creation-winner-only legacy identity provisioning before canonical role checks. Sign-in and sign-up pages verify the server session before redirecting; an invalid cookie can reach authentication without losing the safe local `next` target.

Mention candidate discovery uses an extension-free GIN index of adjacent name pairs, followed by the escaped case-insensitive substring predicate and current authorization. This supports two-character substrings without changing search semantics. Tutor discovery prunes unassigned course scopes in SQL before resolving aliases; the resolver uses alias maps and at most 500 input IDs per query group. The local 1,000-inaccessible-course-pair warm-cache fixture uses 29 SQL calls, one discovered scope and at most eight bindings per statement. The rare and absent two-character fixture across 10,000 eligible accounts visits one and zero user rows respectively. These are local single-process measurements.

Discussion pushes process at most ten recipients and 100 tokens per recipient per step. A composite user/token-ID range supplies the next page; the inbox metadata persists `pushCursor` and `pushContinue` after delivery. Current access, mute and read state are checked again for each page. Confirmed pages continue without waiting for failure backoff; provider failures retain the previous cursor for retry. A crash between provider acceptance and outcome persistence can still duplicate that page. The local 1,201-device regression completes in 13 pages with at most 102 token-row visits per page. New tokens sorting before an already persisted cursor belong to later notifications, not a guaranteed snapshot of this event.

Storage cleanup now retains an `expired` ownership tombstone after its second object-deletion pass. It is excluded from subsequent sweeps and cannot be attached or read. An authorized same-owner, same-channel unattached draft can classify ready-expired, deleting, failed or expired uploads as recoverable after the immutable submission replay check, retaining file bytes for re-upload. Historical rows already removed before this change lack that ownership evidence and remain fail-closed.

New notification payloads retain the event message target; history preserves that target while normalizing role-neutral URLs. Successful read signals refresh the mounted notification bell, with identity and response-version guards. Exhausted read acknowledgements show a retry action that starts a fresh visible-content observation. Signed message observations can acknowledge a visible revision on a targeted later page independently of the contiguous read watermark. They clear or suppress only that message's observed revisions; earlier unseen edits, newer revisions and status events remain unread. The watermark advances only after every intervening message has an accepted observation, and status events retain their separate revision and sequence checks. Report pagination survives opening a thread and returning within the mounted workspace; reported targets regain focus when their page returns. Reaction controls include the message reference. Mathematical spans remain atomic inside emphasis, including multiplication asterisks.


Status: OPEN / IN PROGRESS. Local checks and staging schema migration have passed. Authenticated runtime, external services and application deployment remain separate acceptance gates. See [staging migration](#staging-migration-2026-11-17).

The intended feature is always-on structured questions and answers, with no discussion feature flag. A question has an open or resolved thread, explicit answers and contextual replies. Active students, tutors and admins can use the global channel. Course channels require current full content access; a preview alone is insufficient. Course-scoped tutors also need the applicable assignment. Canonical and legacy course identities must agree or access fails closed.

Technical and academic team channels are private to their requester and authorized staff. Technical channels admit admins; academic channels also admit tutors, with course assignment and entitlement checks when a course is specified. Reads, writes, mention candidates, forwarded sources, attachments and notification visibility recheck access. Mentions are limited to ten eligible members per message. Forwarding stays inside a private channel, within the same course audience, or from global to an authorized course; it cannot move a private message outward. Forwarded source access is checked again when read.

Students need PKA registration to join PKA course discussions; admins and assigned tutors do not need a student registration. Authenticated legacy accounts without a canonical identity can be provisioned atomically. An existing identity without any role remains denied: the stored rows do not distinguish interrupted provisioning from deliberate role revocation, so neither discussion access nor the shared course resolver restores a legacy role automatically. Fresh legacy identities and their initial roles are created in one transaction; a request that loses the identity-creation race cannot add a role. Existing roleless identities require an authorized account repair, even if an earlier partial write caused them.

Authors can edit their own human messages for less than five minutes after creation. Admins can edit human messages beyond that window or moderate other authors' messages. Edits use a revision check. Authors and admins can delete messages; deletion is soft. The thread author or an admin can resolve and reopen a thread. Eligible participants can report another person's message, and admins can resolve or dismiss reports. Writes and reports are rate limited.

The discussion renderer supports a restricted Markdown subset, links, code and bounded math, including math inside emphasis and compact reply context. It does not render raw HTML or remote Markdown images. Attachments use a private authenticated endpoint, with inline viewing and download. Each message accepts at most four still JPEG, PNG or WebP images, each up to 8 MiB, 16 million pixels and 4096 pixels on either edge. Server decoding rejects invalid or animated images and strips metadata. Images over 1 MiB may be resized and converted to WebP when useful; smaller images avoid optional lossy compression, with lossless re-encoding when orientation requires it. New uploads also store a WebP preview up to 480 px and 128 KiB. The full image loads on opening or download; old rows without a preview show an openable placeholder. Both objects require current authorization and are covered by cleanup. Only the uploader can access an unattached ready image, and attached images require current access to the message. Storage keys are not returned to clients.

Mute is per user and channel. It suppresses new inbox and push delivery, including mentions, while thread unread counts continue to track messages. Reading advances a monotonic sequence watermark. Signed response receipts bind the viewer, thread, fetched message revisions and thread status revision; acknowledgments persist only the covered, visible message IDs. Notification clearing and delayed delivery use these accepted revisions, not transaction timestamps. A later-page read cannot acknowledge an unseen earlier edit. Older events without a revision deliver conservatively.

The dispatcher derives notification IDs from the event and recipient, traverses bounded recipient pages with durable progress, and rechecks channel access before inbox and push delivery. Atomic participant summaries avoid rediscovering all authors from message history for each event. Writers capture the participant sequence cutoff under the thread lock, including edits, deletion and resolution; fanout uses membership at that sequence rather than transaction-start timestamps. Pending legacy events without a cutoff restart participant discovery conservatively against current membership, access, mute and read checks; completed legacy events are not reopened. Token reads and push outcome writes are batched, and failed events use retry backoff. Push content does not include discussion text. Question, message, edit, deletion and resolution events notify eligible participants; reports notify eligible admins through the reports tab. An uncertain push acknowledgement can cause a duplicate push, while inbox IDs remain deterministic. Event writers capture validated mention snapshots in the mutation transaction, preserving queued mentions through later edits. Local service-to-worker regressions exercise both ordering boundaries.

Eligible students receive 5 base XP for a new question and 10 base XP plus 1 LP for an explicit answer to another person's question, subject to separate Jakarta-day caps of five questions and ten answers. Existing rank-based bonus XP applies. The outbox and reward keys make awards idempotent per student, reward kind and thread. Staff activity, self-answers, edits, contextual replies and forwards do not earn these rewards. Deleted evidence is ineligible before processing; an already paid award is not automatically clawed back. Discussion activity does not create course learning credits, checklist progress, badges, missions or qualified learning days. See [gamification](gamification.md).

The adapter defaults to the author's equipped, owned chat skin. The server also permits an explicitly selected owned skin after checking its catalog slot and inventory ownership, and stores only that skin ID on the message. Authorized participants can see it without receiving the author's inventory or private profile. A Zyra answer can inherit the invoking message's skin. Course chat's separate assistant-only appearance remains unchanged.

An explicit Zyra request is recorded against the invoking author. The worker rechecks their access and active-assessment boundary, then constructs context from the question title, bounded to 160 characters and treated as untrusted content, the complete invoking message, up to 12,000 characters, and excerpts of at most five earlier visible messages, up to 2,000 characters each. Context and attachment identities are fingerprinted and rechecked before publication. Free-tier requests reject images on the invoking message, while keeping earlier text and omitting earlier images. Students in channels without a course use the Free policy even with a paid course; tutors and admins use the standard policy. The composer help explains the applicable scope. Eligible requests prioritize the invoking images and use remaining slots and bytes for recent earlier images, up to four total; excess earlier images do not block a text invocation. The prompt identifies omitted images and prohibits inferring their contents. Image requests also depend on the existing Zyra image capability and its byte limits. The request is configured with the invoker's identity and allowance, a stable idempotency key, cache bypass and one executor attempt. A stored result can be recovered after revalidation; an uncertain dispatched result is not automatically regenerated. Failure does not undo the human message.

Question creation enqueues a label request. Automatic labels currently use deterministic classification and retain an explicit help category; they do not debit a student's tutoring allowance. A session-authorized staff classification action can request AI classification under that staff member's budget, with a deterministic fallback. Fully automatic provider classification needs an application-owned operational budget identity, which is not configured by this change. Labels never widen staff access.

Discussion generation and staff classification use the shared executor's `singleDispatch` option with a stable idempotency key. This bypasses shared caches and disables provider fallback, SDK retries and structured-output repair for the invocation. Confirmed terminal HTTP failures on the router refund the application lease after complete provider-attempt settlement, without another dispatch. Ambiguous outcomes remain uncertain for reconciliation instead of being refunded and regenerated. Legacy single-dispatch HTTP failures remain uncertain because the same control-plane settlement cannot be verified there. Ordinary legacy callers can settle their own application lease after terminal HTTP 400/422 or an exhausted retryable chain only when every attempted failure is confirmed HTTP; any earlier uncertain attempt prevents that refund. Across ordinary and single-dispatch calls, timeouts and unknown billable outcomes stop automatic fallback. This deliberately trades immediate availability for avoiding a second provider charge after an unknown result. Reconciliation failures are also uncertain. The pedagogy harness and tutor RAG preserve that outcome and stop their own legacy-generation fallback, including requests without an idempotency key; shadow telemetry uses the executor and harness outcome contracts. The worker environment projection retains `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_URL` and `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN` for the existing deployment filter. Local fake-provider tests exercise these boundaries; live provider accounting and deployed configuration are unverified.

PR #339 migrations `0024` through `0034` were rehearsed on branch `br-snowy-queen-az21y3vg`, then committed in one transaction to Neon project `muddy-sky-44104897`, staging branch `br-gentle-scene-azq0gp91`, compute `ep-sparkling-lab-azrp3ymj`, database `neondb`. Backup branch `br-dry-block-az9ndjdc` retains the pre-migration state without a compute. Production was not changed.

The preflight matched all 26 historical ledger entries and found no discussion tables. The transaction locked the migration ledger, rechecked the exact baseline, executed unchanged generated SQL with lock and statement timeouts, and appended its actual hashes and timestamps. A separate readback verified all 26 original rows unchanged and all 11 new entries, for 37 ledger rows. The count differs from the 35 local migration files because staging retains two independently applied upstream entries. Known historical hashes were preserved. The stock migrator was not used to reinterpret that history.

All 13 discussion tables exist; their constraints and indexes passed validity checks. The existing staging application role has SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE and DELETE privileges, and a separate connection as that role read the empty discussion tables successfully. Accounts, notifications and cosmetics remained at 70, 162 and 28. There were no historical discussion rows to backfill and no discussion writer to drain on this target; the existing-data fence and backfill rules below still apply to other targets.

Application deployment, authenticated discussion flows, provider accounting, storage, push and concurrent runtime behavior were not exercised by this schema migration. Merging into `staging` can schedule its existing worker deployment after CI; the staging web release remains manual. Do not reopen old fenced writers or infer application acceptance from a completed migration.

Pull-to-refresh in the student workspace reloads the current question page, selected thread and expanded resolved history through their existing reads. It keeps the current navigation and invalidates the badge separately. The workspace catalog and metadata reads return channel identity and mute preference without loading per-channel aggregates. The count endpoint and counted service reads keep their existing contract. The first exact course catalog page can use the authorized course channel directly after checking both aliases.

The workspace loads thread pages, the channel catalog and channel metadata through the session-bound `/api/discussions/workspace` handler. Its responses are private and uncached, and the session account must match the account that opened the workspace. Thread observations and catalog provisioning use POST. Unscoped question lists can load while the channel catalog is pending. In-page selection updates the shareable URL and browser history without fetching a new route render. Existing service checks still authorize every read. Message-body search uses an independent full-text subquery so PostgreSQL can use the existing GIN index without a correlated body search per candidate thread.

Resolve and reopen hide the affected row while the write is pending. A failed write restores the row and shows a retry message. A confirmed write refreshes the current question list, any expanded resolved history and the selected thread's signed observation when needed. The floating Zyra launcher is hidden in course discussions.

Local source includes session-derived server actions, `/api/discussions/attachments` upload and `/api/discussions/attachments/[id]` read/download handlers, presentation components and an isolated visual fixture. Entry points are `/dashboard/discussions`, its `/discussions` alias, `/courses/[id]/discussions`, `/tutor/discussions`, `/tutor/[courseId]/discussions` and `/admin/discussions`. The admin reports tab is addressable with `?discussionTab=reports`; thread links use `?thread=`. Sidebars expose the role-appropriate destination and an authorized unread badge. The notification, AI and expired-image sweep jobs are registered in `jobs/compute.ts`.

Question, channel and report pages apply current visibility before pagination. Forward-target queries also filter open threads before pagination. Answer counts are maintained transactionally. Exact unread counts scan messages after the read watermark; a long unread suffix can still be expensive. Initial catalog discovery and aggregate visibility resolve relevant course scopes, while filtered or later channel pages avoid full catalog provisioning. `getDiscussionCounts` with `courseId` scopes authorization and aggregation to that course: `total`, `scopes.course` and `course` are equal, and other scopes are zero. Without `courseId`, a cold aggregate covers all authorized thread-bearing channels. Audience and course predicates constrain discovery before IDs are returned. Student, course-scoped and explicit-channel queries use an ordered indexed thread probe. Unscoped staff discovery applies audience predicates to indexed channels with a positive count revision before probing threads. First thread creation raises that revision atomically; there is no application hard-delete path for threads. This avoids traversing empty channels or another requester's technical channels merely because they contain threads. Bounded channel metadata requests reuse the same authorized count cache rather than recounting each visible channel. A process-local cache retains at most 256 aggregate DTOs for an absolute five-minute lifetime, admitted by stable actor and requested scope, with one current authorization fingerprint per scope. The fingerprint includes current role, authorized channels, monotonic channel count revisions and per-user/channel read revisions. A changed version replaces that scope's obsolete entry. Hits retain their original expiry. Once all 256 entries are occupied, excess keys bypass admission until entries expire, preserving useful admitted entries during cyclic polling; those excess keys still compute uncached. Authorization and the fingerprint are checked before and after either a cold query or a cache hit. Count-affecting mutations increment the channel revision transactionally; body edits do not. A read revision changes only when acknowledgement changes the thread's unread contribution. Observation fetches, duplicate acknowledgements and unrelated-course reads do not invalidate that scoped aggregate. Unchanged polls avoid rescanning threads; cold or changed global aggregates still grow with visible threads.

Failed read acknowledgements retry at most twice after the initial attempt, with backoff and current visibility and receipt guards. They do not require another scroll or observation callback. Read state follows message content after a meaningful visible, uncovered 600 ms dwell, and acknowledges visible edits, deletions and resolution changes even when the last sequence is unchanged. Author-row intersections do not count. The client records each acknowledged snapshot to avoid a refresh loop. Fetching a thread updates only the viewer's observed sequence without taking the shared thread's exclusive lock. Forward-target pagination and scoped mention search live inside their dialogs and composers. The editor distinguishes selected namesakes with numeric suffixes. New messages store each selected handle alongside its authorized recipient ID so the bubble can show the current full name and open the correct profile. Namesake context uses one indexed channel/user participant pointer and one bounded message lookup. A deleted, forwarded or unavailable first pointer yields no context. Channel metadata is refreshed in bounded batches on focus, timers and mutations with stale-response protection. Moderation includes the reported message context; opening it carries `thread` and `message` in one navigation, loads a bounded authorized page around that message, and focuses the target. Every later message page supplies its immediate previous-page cursor, so repeated backward navigation retains nearby context. Edit conflicts preserve the draft and require a choice before resubmission. Discussion notifications use `/discussions`, which resolves the authenticated actor's current role before redirecting to the appropriate workspace. Absent sessions redirect through sign-in with the complete local discussion URL; authenticated access denial remains fail-closed. History normalizes earlier role-specific URLs after its current-access filter, so a role change does not strand an otherwise authorized discussion link.

New questions can choose a public audience or prepare the requester's academic or technical team channel in the current course context. Private channel labels show the authorized course and, for staff, requester context; audience copy distinguishes the requester from the staff member posting. Namesake mention choices use role and authorized message context; unresolved collisions are disabled. Mention search returns at most 100 currently authorized candidates, in a scrollable list sized for three standard rows; ambiguity is checked across the complete bounded set. A 101-row overflow fails closed with narrowing guidance. Translated system-channel searches paginate all matching aliases independently.

Course-private questions open in the corresponding full discussion workspace. Send actions return controlled error codes, and image upload failures distinguish size, pixel limits, format, rate limits, access and unexpected storage failures. Unknown submission outcomes retain and lock the complete payload for an unchanged idempotent retry. Immutable submission fingerprints bind the original normalized question, answer, reply or forward payload, so later edits and soft deletion do not invalidate a verified retry. Legacy rows with no fingerprint require manual inspection of an authorized target and explicit discard; they are never retried automatically under a new request ID. Forward recovery also reauthorizes the stored source. Confirmed expired owned uploads retain their bytes for re-upload. Temporary session absence hides the workspace but preserves drafts for the same verified identity; a different verified account purges them and revokes preview URLs. An uncertain forward retry explains a resolved destination while retaining its original identity. Message action names and delete confirmation identify the author, sequence and a bounded excerpt. A non-pending forward dialog can be dismissed and reopened without losing its locked retry identity. The composer retains retry identity rather than exposing raw backend errors.

Generated PostgreSQL migrations `0024_strong_newton_destine.sql` through `0034_aromatic_silhouette.sql` and their snapshots exist locally. They include durable recipient deliveries, preview metadata, answer and status counters, version observations, participant summaries, serialized participant cutoffs, channel count revisions, scoped read revisions, an indexed notification thread lookup, immutable submission fingerprints, partial audience indexes on channels with positive count revisions, indexed name candidates and token paging, and expired-upload ownership retention. They were applied to the verified staging target on 2026-11-17 as recorded above. Other targets require their own verification. Any target with existing discussions needs answer counts and participant summaries backfilled under a discussion write fence before new writers or dispatchers resume. Participant backfill includes soft-deleted human messages: retain each author's lowest sequence and its timestamp, plus their earliest timestamp and its lowest sequence. Populate each participant's `channel_id` from its thread. Reconcile all four values, channel identity and participant keys against source messages before resuming in-flight event cursors. Drain old writers before enabling channel revision-based count reuse. Under that fence, set count_revision to 1 for every existing thread-bearing channel whose revision is zero, and verify none remain before new readers resume. Empty channels stay at zero. This backfill is required for the staff discovery indexes; the generated index migration alone does not perform it. Read revisions may begin at zero when the new process caches are empty and old writers are drained. Generated defaults alone do not perform the other backfills, and edited legacy payloads cannot safely be assigned guessed submission fingerprints.

The interface uses the existing Indonesian and English catalog system. Additive message and report metadata distinguish system placeholders from authored content, so translation never depends on matching a person's text. Upload errors and AI statuses expose allowlisted recovery codes. Notification count-only and mark-all operations discover only unread referenced channels; specific-ID updates discover only the supplied owned IDs. Full history still applies current authorization before pagination. Moderation pagination retains PostgreSQL timestamp precision in its cursor, including sub-millisecond report boundaries.

The Node core suite has 35 cases against generated migrations through 0034, including the production read-retry signed-receipt transaction. A fresh isolated run on 2026-11-17 passed all 35 cases on PR head `77d5b3eacf6328115d49da912e9d6186ed312038`; GitHub CI passed on that head separately. The suite covers transactional read-version rollback and repeated preceding pages near sequence 450. The metadata regression verifies an unchanged refresh reuses counts and a count revision forces a fresh aggregate. A 257-live-scope cache regression verifies bounded admission without extending expiry; a 128-user, two-scope revision-change case verifies replacement of obsolete entries. The tutor discovery plan also excludes 10,000 populated inaccessible technical channels, and unread or specific-ID notification authorization excludes 1,000 existing already-read course channels. Separate generated-migration and local PostgreSQL-dialect fixtures cover attachment authorization, notification delivery, precise report cursors, immutable replay after editing and deletion, and bounded report targets. A fictional 10,000-thread, 100,000-message PGlite fixture confirms indexed activity ordering and unread ranges: the scoped cold aggregate visits 20 relevant threads and the global cold aggregate visits 10,000. Repeated counts retain their original cache expiry; count-neutral edits and unrelated private channels or read histories do not invalidate scoped results. Discovery is also checked with 10,000 unrelated private channels containing threads. Another 20,000 unrelated private channels are excluded from ordinary provisioning reads. Thirty reports use batched authorization and 16 SQL calls. With 10,000 empty private channels, each role's count path uses 29 calls and visits at most two relevant channels per version check; either one or ten mentions use 34 calls. The notification thread index is checked with a 20,000-row unread backlog and a generic query plan. Namesake context plans stay bounded with 10,000 messages or participant threads, including deleted, forwarded and missing pointers. These are local query results, not deployed capacity or concurrent PostgreSQL measurements. Deployed acceptance remains open. Earlier fixture checkpoints did not run build, lint or typecheck. Subsequent PR validation on `77d5b3eacf6328115d49da912e9d6186ed312038` passed CI, including affected lint and type checks. No new application build was run for this documentation and staging migration update.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
# Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows

This catalog documents the active user-facing and operational capabilities of Zyx Academy across Student, Tutor, Admin, Public, Native App, and MCP surfaces.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Saved sessions**: The sidebar account menu keeps up to 5 signed-in Zyx accounts so users can switch sessions without re-authenticating with Google.
- **Native Google account chooser**: On Android builds with `ZyxGoogleAuth`, adding an account opens the Credential Manager chooser; older APKs, iOS, Desktop, and Web use the native system browser flow with session `login_hint`.
- **Session cleanup**: Switching or signing out clears account-scoped TanStack Query caches, private offline reader storage, guarded coding drafts, and active Zyra language overrides.
- **Role redirect**: Signed-in users visiting marketing entry pages redirect directly to their role dashboard on the canonical public origin.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Staff and Student profiles**: Authenticated staff have basic profile access; gamification and Pet Studio are student-only.
- **Editor tabs**: Academic, Privacy, and Appearance tabs save independently; academic drafts survive tab switches and failed saves.
- **Profile completeness**: Inline completeness indicator and mobile-friendly inline dialog actions.
- **Bilingual UI (`id` / `en`)**: Full Indonesian and English interface across student, tutor, admin, and public routes, including bilingual Admin (`/admin/docs`) and Tutor (`/tutor/docs`) documentation hubs.
- **Notification preferences and quiet hours**: Granular activity and email notification categories with atomic saves, confirmation links, signed 30-day one-click unsubscribe tokens, per-account quiet-hour push digests, native push isolation, and signed-in device session revocation. See [notifications.md](notifications.md) and [notifications-quiet-hours.md](notifications-quiet-hours.md).
- **Bilingual first-use tours**: Interactive Indonesian and English onboarding tours for students and tutors.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- Dedicated desktop and mobile LMS shells (`features/`) with responsive sticky horizontal tabs (`More` / `Lebih` overflow popover), history-backed overlay dismissal, and global `cmdk` search.
- Mobile surfaces include pull-to-refresh, navbar refresh actions, tab icons, meaningful haptics, and OS share/file integration in the Capacitor app.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Structured Articles (V4 default)**: Ordered scientific sections, catalogue-based headings, chapter numbering, decoded canonical product URLs, compact formula rows with KaTeX macros, and subsection navigation.
- **Embedded Learning Visuals**: Always-on typed `zyx-visual` Markdown embeds (interactive function plots, 2D geometry, reading-first graphs with optional parameter controls and explicit interaction activation) plus sandboxed `interactive_document` widgets that preserve state while scrolling and pause offscreen playback.
- **Article selection handoff**: Selecting text on desktop (popover) or mobile (selection action) sends a saved quote directly to Zyra for contextual explanation.
- **Diktat**: Authored 1 to 4 page printable scientific PDFs with inline viewer and authorized download.
- **Standalone Solution Collections (V5)**: Reviewed problem-and-solution collections under `/courses/[id]/solutions/[collectionId]`.
- **Videos**: Course video playlists powered by Vidstack player, streaming via short-lived presigned storage URLs for optimized playback and proxy efficiency.
- **Offline Reader**: Decoupled offline service worker and native offline reader (`/offline`) for saved readings when offline.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **SM-2 Flashcards**: Idea-linked spaced-repetition flashcards with flip, grade (1 to 4), due queues, and mastery-based suppression.
- **Chapter Mastery & Study Path**: Per-Idea mastery tracking, concept explorer (`/courses/[id]/concept/[slug]`), chapter-level mastery browsing, topic feedback, and adaptive study paths.
- **Weekly Reflections**: Student reflection journal (`/profile/reflections`) with optional reminder emails (`FEATURE_REFLECTION_EMAIL`).

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- Editable Python Markdown blocks directly inside student Articles, plus a dedicated viewport-aware Playground (`/courses/[id]/playground`).
- Browser Pyodide execution, staging WASI terminal support, explicit Submit grading, guarded code insertion from Zyra, and beginner-friendly Python coaching. See [coding-foundation.md](coding-foundation.md).

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Reservation and timing**: Quiz attempts reserve canonical items at start. Untimed quizzes (`timeLimitSeconds: null`) omit countdown timers and expiry effects.
- **Timeout and late submission invariant**: POST `/api/quiz/attempts/[id]` accepts timeout and late submissions and caps the recorded duration at `timeLimitSeconds` when configured, preventing zombie attempts. Drafts are preserved on failed submission and cleared only after server acknowledgement.
- **Answer safety**: Active attempt GET endpoints redact `correct_indices` and stored explanations until submission.
- **Provenance and grading**: Canonical Idea-linked questions record per-Idea mastery evidence; legacy unprovenanced snapshots remain gradeable without attributing Idea evidence. Essays support manual tutor grading.
- **Tryouts**: Multi-chapter timed exams with recovery for interrupted submissions and detailed post-submission summaries.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content: - Real-time host and student quiz sessions (`/courses/[id]/live`, `/courses/[id]/live/host`) powered by `workers/realtime` with durable live answers.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content: - Free multi-stage PKA simulation campaign (`/courses/tutorial-pka`), registration, schedules, announcements, and progress reports.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Conversational tutoring**: Live SSE streaming with response progress indicators, article-style KaTeX math rendering, proactive grounded visual exploration, and safe retry handling when generation fails.
- **Contextual follow-ups**: Policy-validated subtle follow-up quick actions and automatic Zyra AI session titles.
- **Multimodal input (`FEATURE_ZYRA_IMAGE_INPUT_V1`)**: Private authenticated learner image uploads with sanitizer validation and persistent thumbnails.
- **Language override**: Temporary per-conversation language switching (in-memory, up to 32 sessions) without mutating account locale.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Model configuration (`/admin/ops/models`)**: Dynamic Cloudflare AI Gateway model discovery, 12-hour KV catalog cache, release/creation date sorting, 3-sample median latency probes (12-hour scheduled + manual refresh), global and per-feature model selection, and 5-minute alias cooldown after 3 consecutive failures.
- **AI analytics (`/admin/ops/analytics`)**: Deduplicated usage, latency, error bucket, and allowance telemetry with Asia/Jakarta day boundaries and zero prompt/PII retention.
- **Admin Ops AI Copilot**: Grounded in `admin_ops_knowledge` Vectorize namespace and curated docs; generates 30-minute expiring action proposals requiring explicit admin confirmation before any mutation.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content: - Course and general discussion channels (`/discussions`, `/courses/[id]/discussions`, `/tutor/discussions`, `/admin/discussions`) with full-text search (GIN indexes), mention handles, emoji status, compact composer with square image thumbnail strips, and `@Zyra` AI dispatch with hardened cooldowns. See [discussions.md](discussions.md).

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
section: Schedules, Bookings, and Google Calendar Sync
content:
- **Role calendars**: Route-owned Student (`/calendar`, `/dashboard/schedule`), Course, Tutor (`/tutor/schedule`), and Admin (`/admin/schedules`) calendars with on-demand week loading, tutor availability configuration, configurable tutorial email reminders, and filtered slot booking.
- **Google Calendar sync**: Personal offline OAuth calendar sync and shared Zyx host primary calendar sync via daily queue dispatch and manual toolbar sync controls.
- **Study Groups & Tokens**: Transactional enrollment token redemption (`Zyx-XXXXXXXX-{capacity}-{courseIds.length}`) forming study groups (`/dashboard/groups`) with shared rosters and booking quotas.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Combined Leaderboard (`/leaderboard`)**: URL-addressable `Rank` (participation XP: week/month/all-time/following) and `Academic` (course-scoped academic ranking) tabs. `/leaderboard/academic` redirects to `?tab=academic`.
- **Achievements & Rewards (`/achievements`)**: Overview, Badges (6 families x 5 tiers), Missions, and Rewards (animated frames, chat skins, Pet Studio items).
- **Pet Studio (`/pet`)**: 4 3D GLB companions (cat free; tiger, rhino, crocodile purchasable with LP) with unique actions and 15 fitted LP suits.
- **Social Identity**: `StudentProfileDialog` and people search (250 ms debounce, 2 to 80 chars, max 10 results) with member visibility, follow/unfollow, block, and report controls. See [gamification.md](gamification.md).

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content: - Course overview, read-only material list (with Admin authoring override), video management, quiz authoring and attempt review, tryout management, essay grading (`/tutor/[courseId]/grading`), participant roster, live classroom hosting, schedule/slot management, discussions, and bilingual Tutor Docs (`/tutor/docs`).

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- **Hybrid domain-grouped sidebar**: Home, Academic & Content (Courses, Materials, Bundles, Schedules, Tutorial PKA, Discussions), Evaluation (Question Bank, Quizzes, Quiz Insights, Distractors, Generation Jobs, Leaderboard), Tools & Communications (Form Studio, Meet, Media Library, Blog, Short Links, Important Links, Pricing & Discounts, Notifications), Users & Access (Users, Groups, Tokens), and System & Ops (Ops Monitor, Models, Analytics, API Keys, Feature Flags, Feature Usage, Web Analytics, Tutor Activity, Admin Docs).
- **Form Studio (`/admin/forms`)**: Revamped Google Forms style builder with less-cards layout, per-question or per-section publication, upload size labels, submission confirmation, and Google Sheets export with attachment URLs.
- **Pricing & Discounts (`/admin/pricing`)**: Admin-managed platform and tutorial discount schedules backed by singleton `pricing_settings`.
- **Course Access Categories**: Admin-managed free/paid course access categories and scheduled free access windows.

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- Streamable HTTP MCP endpoint supporting OAuth PKCE with 4 default scopes plus explicit publication and admin consent grants.
- Full canonical workflow: Source Pack ingestion -> Idea Bundle V3 -> Product Bundle V4/V5 -> Flexible stable-ID revisions -> verification -> review -> atomic publication.
- Admin MCP tools for blog, forms, media, schedules, groups, tokens, notifications, and operation receipt recovery. See [operations/admin-mcp.md](operations/admin-mcp.md) and [operations/agent-first-content.md](operations/agent-first-content.md).

docTitle: Zyx Academy Product Features and Workflows
content:
- Marketing routes (`/`, `/about`, `/plans`, `/blog`, `/testimonial`, `/tautan`, `/privacy`, `/terms`, `/f/[slug]`, `/meet/[slug]`).
- **Interactive Public Demo (`/demo`)**: Reuses the exact student shell, course catalog, dashboard, articles, read-only diktats, flashcards, quizzes, tryout, calendar, groups, achievements, leaderboard, and scripted Zyra with first-chapter Free policy and browser-persistent fictional state. See [operations/public-demo-seeding.md](operations/public-demo-seeding.md).

docTitle: File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy
content:
# File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy

Dokumen ini adalah standar resmi penamaan berkas dan struktur direktori untuk tim admin, tutor, dan sistem *ingestion* Zyx Academy. Standar ini memastikan seluruh berkas materi, latihan, dan evaluasi terorganisasi secara konsisten, mudah dicari, dan otomatis berurutan secara kronologis.

---

docTitle: File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy
content:
1. **Tahun dan Periode di Akhir**: Penempatan tahun di akhir nama file menjaga nama topik tetap terkelompok rapi saat diurutkan secara alfabetis, sekaligus memudahkan komparasi edisi materi antar-tahun.
2. **Deterministik dan Terurut (*Sort-Friendly*)**: Menggunakan dua digit angka untuk bab (`bab01`, `bab02`, ..., `bab12`) agar urutan tidak berantakan di sistem operasi atau *object storage*.
3. **Format Karakter Aman**: Hanya gunakan huruf kecil (`a-z`), angka (`0-9`), garis bawah (`_`) sebagai pemisah segmen utama, dan tanda hubung (`-`) sebagai pemisah kata dalam satu segmen.
4. **Bebas Karakter Ilegal**: Dilarang menggunakan spasi, tanda kurung, aksen, tanda petik, dan em dash atau en dash. Gunakan tanda hubung tunggal (`-`), koma, atau titik dua standar.
5. **Hierarki Mengikuti Domain Zyx**:
   `[Mata Kuliah / Course] -> [Bab / Topik] -> [Kategori] -> [Tahun / Semester]`

---

docTitle: File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy
content:
Format baku penamaan file adalah:

```text
[KODE_MK]_[BAB]_[KATEGORI]_[DESKRIPSI]_[ROLE]_[TAHUN-SEMESTER].[ext]
```

docTitle: File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy
content:
| Posisi | Segmen | Status | Format / Contoh | Penjelasan |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `KODE_MK` | Wajib | `ma1101`, `fi1101`, `ki1001` | Kode resmi mata kuliah (huruf kecil). |
| 2 | `BAB` | Wajib jika spesifik bab | `bab01`, `bab02`, `modul03`, `general` | Dua digit angka untuk menjamin urutan sorting. |
| 3 | `KATEGORI` | Wajib | `materi`, `diktat`, `tutorial`, `kuis`, `uts`, `uas` | Jenis atau klasifikasi dokumen. |
| 4 | `DESKRIPSI` | Kondisional | `limit-kontinu`, `hukum-newton`, `paket-a` | Topik spesifik (kebab-case). |
| 5 | `ROLE` | Kondisional | `soal`, `solusi`, `pembahasan`, `slide` | Pembeda lembar soal dan kunci jawaban. |
| 6 | `TAHUN-SEMESTER` | Wajib | `2024-sem1`, `2025-sem2`, `2026-sp`, `2025` | Tahun akademik dan periode semester. |

---

docTitle: File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy
content:
- **Materi Pembelajaran (*Learning Content*)**:
  - `materi`: Slide presentasi dosen atau handout kuliah.
  - `diktat`: Diktat bab, modul komprehensif, atau kompilasi teori.
  - `catatan`: Catatan tutor, *cheatsheet*, atau rangkuman rumus.
  - `silabus`: Satuan Acara Perkuliahan (SAP) atau RPS.
- **Latihan & Pembelajaran Formatif (*Practice*)**:
  - `tutorial`: Lembar soal tutorial mingguan resmi.
  - `latihan`: Bank soal latihan mandiri per bab.
  - `pr`: Pekerjaan rumah atau tugas terstruktur.
- **Evaluasi & Ujian (*Summative Assessment*)**:
  - `kuis`: Kuis kelas atau evaluasi pendek per bab.
  - `uts`: Ujian Tengah Semester.
  - `uas`: Ujian Akhir Semester.
  - `tryout`: Simulasi ujian internal Zyx.

docTitle: File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy
content:
- `soal`: Lembar pertanyaan ujian/latihan tanpa kunci.
- `solusi`: Pembahasan rinci atau kunci jawaban resmi.
- `slide`: Format presentasi ringkas.

---

docTitle: File Naming Conventions and Directory Hierarchy
content:
Gunakan format empat digit tahun diikuti kode semester:

- `2025-sem1`: Semester 1 / Semester Ganjil (Gasal) Tahun Ajaran 2025.
- `2025-sem2`: Semester 2 / Semester Genap Tahun Ajaran 2025.
- `2025-sp`: Semester Pendek / Semester Antara Tahun Ajaran 2025.
- `2025`: Jika dokumen berlaku umum sepanjang tahun akademik penuh.

---

content:
# Gamification, Pet Studio, and Social Identity

Authoritative product and implementation contract for student gamification, Pet Studio, achievements, leaderboards, and public student profiles. Gamification is always-on (no feature flag) and student-only; the admin Gamification page and navigation entry have been removed while retaining server-side checklist helpers and existing student reward data.

docTitle: Gamification, Pet Studio, and Social Identity
content:
XP and course credits use integer millionths for exact allocation. Each eligible event awards base XP plus a rank bonus calculated from the student's rank prior to the event. LP (Learning Points) is a separate integer currency earned from badge tiers, missions, and eligible discussion answers, and spent in the cosmetics shop and Pet Studio.

| Rank | Total XP Minimum | Course Credits Minimum | Future XP Bonus | Zyra Daily Turn Bonus |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| Rakyat | 0 | 0 | 0% | 0% (15 turns) |
| Kades | 1,000 | 0 | 0% | 0% (15 turns) |
| Camat | 10,000 | 1 | 5% | 5% (15 turns) |
| Bupati | 30,000 | 3 | 10% | 10% (16 turns) |
| Gubernur | 60,000 | 6 | 15% | 15% (17 turns) |
| Presiden | 100,000 | 10 | 20% | 25% (18 turns) |

- The first eligible Zyra allowance read fixes the rank snapshot for the Asia/Jakarta day.
- Approved course checklists allocate reference pools over stable item IDs: Articles (up to 1,000 XP at 10 items), Explanations (up to 1,000 XP at 10 items), Questions (up to 6,000 XP at 300 items), and Flashcards (up to 2,000 XP at 200 items), contributing up to 1 course credit proportional to 10,000 possible XP.
- Discussion rewards award 5 base XP per eligible question (max 5/day) and 10 base XP + 1 LP per eligible answer to another student's question (max 10/day), once per reward kind per thread. Staff, self-answers, replies, forwards, and edits are excluded.

docTitle: Gamification, Pet Studio, and Social Identity
content:
Six achievement families each have 5 tiers (Bronze through Emerald), awarding 25, 50, 100, 200, and 400 LP per tier:

| Family | Tier Thresholds |
| --- | --- |
| Warrior Reader | 5, 15, 40, 100, 200 |
| Practice Knight | 20, 75, 200, 500, 1,000 |
| Memory Guardian | 25, 100, 300, 750, 1,500 |
| Steady Scholar | 3, 10, 30, 90, 180 |
| Comeback Champion | 5, 20, 50, 150, 300 |
| Consistency Captain | 1, 4, 12, 26, 52 |

Confirmed unread badge and rank awards display in top-center Sonner notifications (persisted atomically with rewards, polled at most once per minute while visible, paused in hidden tabs, and excluded from staff and demo contexts).

docTitle: Gamification, Pet Studio, and Social Identity
content:
- **Quizzes**: Rewardable quiz items require published canonical question, course, version, options, and answer provenance. Exposure history uses an indexed maximum-time projection (`gamification_question_exposure_projection`) per viewer, course, and question so prior disclosures prevent duplicate rewards without blocking grading.
- **Flashcards**: Requires two eligible due recalls of the same card separated by at least 7 days with qualifying grades.
- **Outbox**: Learning facts and receipts flow through `gamification_event_outbox` with idempotent ledger writes (up to 100 events per worker invocation with durable continuation and 5-minute cron recovery).

docTitle: Gamification, Pet Studio, and Social Identity
content:
- **Avatar frames (`CollectibleFrame` / `FrameChoreography`)**: 10 illustrated frame collections (`Orbit Zyx`, `Garuda Fajar`, `Samudra`, `Bara Komodo`, `Wayang Kencana`, `Merah Putih`, `Borobudur`, `Khatulistiwa`, `Anggrek`, `Naga`) served as lossless WebP under `public/gamification/collections/frames/`. Student photos remain centered and stable; hero frames animate with reduced-motion and offscreen pause support while small list avatars remain static.

Apply migrations (`0036_student_pet_studio.sql`, `0037_member_profile_visibility.sql`, `0038_discussion_mention_handles.sql`) and run the guarded catalog seed (`scripts/staging/seed-gamification-catalog.ts`) explicitly before releasing dependent web revisions.

content:
- **Leaderboard (`/leaderboard`)**: URL-addressable `Rank` (global/following participation XP by period) and `Academic` (course-scoped academic ranking) tabs. `/leaderboard/academic` redirects to `?tab=academic` preserving query parameters.

LP balances, emails, internal IDs, and private academic stats are never public.
  - Member visibility (`0037_member_profile_visibility.sql`), leaderboard opt-in, and bidirectional blocks are enforced server-side.
  - People search runs with 250 ms debounce for 2 to 80 character queries, returning up to 10 public student identities (excluded from staff, marketing, and demo search).
  - Public demo (`/demo`) reuses these exact renderers with browser-local fictional data.

# Quiet hours and signed-in sessions

- Preferences apply to account-wide **push notifications**, not transactional email. The inbox retains individual updates immediately. Default is off; start and end are local wall-clock times in the chosen IANA zone.
- During a quiet window, ordinary and discussion pushes enqueue the persisted notification ID in a durable Postgres queue. A Cloud Tasks job runs at the end; hourly recovery covers an enqueue outage. The worker rechecks the current preference, current unread state and discussion visibility, then sends one privacy-safe digest per bounded page. Stable OS notification tags replace repeat digest banners. Provider delivery remains at-least-once.
- Desktop's authenticated inbox polling stops advancing its cursor during quiet hours. Native app delivery depends on Android notification permission and correctly configured FCM. OS-level DND can still suppress banners.
- Session listing returns only IDs, device labels and timestamps. The session token and raw IP are never exposed. Remote sign-out uses Better Auth's revocation endpoint; session-bound push tokens cascade on deletion. Legacy unbound tokens rebind at the next registration. Session renewal time is not a precise last-activity timestamp.
- Never infer that two Chrome/Capacitor registrations belong to one physical device by IP or user agent. Only retire the browser push token automatically if a native registration proves that it shares the same authenticated session. Existing independent Chrome subscriptions can still be opted out explicitly.
- Android has a browser cleanup action in notification preferences. It opens the original browser and requires a separate explicit click to unsubscribe only that browser. A local pause flag prevents immediate re-registration; the browser can explicitly re-enable later.
- Native local study reminders shift their recurring wall-clock schedule to the next non-quiet minute using the latest synced account preference. One-off session reminders move to the quiet end only if that is still before the session starts. Offline devices cannot instantly learn about remote changes or revocations; recurring schedule changes across differing DST zones require a foreground sync.
- Android uses notification categories and conversation tags (replacement/grouping by thread, not full Android MessagingStyle). Active, visible discussion toasts and web foreground banners are suppressed.
- Device validation: install Nightly, allow OS notifications, test foreground/background/terminated (not force-stopped), log into Chrome separately, verify no cross-device token is removed, test overnight and non-overnight quiet windows and changes while queued, revoke an independent browser/device session, verify it cannot access protected routes and stops receiving push.
- Rollout: apply the additive migration before web/worker deployment and build a new Nightly for Android channel changes. The open contextual-notifications PR #499 touches the same schema and journal; reconcile its migration and delivery/preference semantics before merging either change into staging.

# Notification System Contract

Status: `ACTIVE` (local source; hosted rollout, live FCM/APNs/Resend delivery, and native store builds remain separate verification boundaries).

This document is the source of truth for notification scopes, delivery channels, interval schedules, and native app synchronization across Student, Tutor, and Admin roles in Zyx Academy. The executable registry lives in [`lib/notifications/catalog.ts`](../lib/notifications/catalog.ts).

- **In-app inbox + Push only**: Frequent, collaborative, or lightweight updates (discussions, ticket replies, quiz grading, due flashcards, daily tutor queue digest).
- **In-app inbox + Push + Optional Email**: Schedule changes, tutorial bookings, ticket decisions, PKA sessions, weekly learning reflections, and 7+ day inactivity re-engagement. Controlled by `email_notification_preferences` (`course_updates`, `events_and_schedules`, `learning_reminders`, `news_and_offers`).
- **In-app inbox + Push + Transactional Email**: Essential account/access events (group token redemption / course activation and critical admin operational alerts). Bypasses optional email preferences.

|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Discussion activity (reply, mention, resolved) | `discussion` | Yes | Never | None | `/discussions?thread=...` |
| Quiz published in enrolled course | `quiz_published` | Yes | Optional | `course_updates` | `/courses/{courseId}/quiz/{id}` |
| Quiz or essay attempt graded by tutor | `quiz_graded` | Yes | Never | None | `/courses/{courseId}/quiz/{templateId}` |
| Group token redeemed / course access activated | `payment_success` | Yes | Transactional | Always on | `/dashboard` |
| Tutor moves a scheduled tutorial session | `tutor_reminder` | Yes | Optional | `events_and_schedules` | `/dashboard/schedule` |
| Tutor approves or declines schedule ticket | `tutor_reminder` | Yes | Optional | `events_and_schedules` | `/dashboard/schedule` |
| New message on schedule ticket | `tutor_reminder` | Yes | Never | None | `/dashboard/schedule` |
| Tutorial PKA announcement, schedule, or Meet update | `announcement` | Yes | Optional | `events_and_schedules` | `/courses/tutorial-pka` |
| Admin broadcast | `admin_broadcast` | Yes | Never | None | Custom or `/dashboard` |

All interval jobs are registered in [`jobs/compute.ts`](../jobs/compute.ts), [`lib/queue/cron.ts`](../lib/queue/cron.ts), and [`app/api/internal/queue/route.ts`](../app/api/internal/queue/route.ts), and deduplicated per recipient and window using `notifications.metadata.dedupeKey`.

| Job ID | Audience | Schedule | In-App & Push | Email | Behavior |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| `weekly-reflection-cron` | Student | Monday 06:00 UTC (13:00 WIB) | Yes (`weekly_progress`) | Optional (`learning_reminders`) | Summarizes completed quizzes, flashcards, modules, mastery growth, and streak from the prior week. |
| `study-reengagement-cron` | Student | Daily 11:00 UTC (18:00 WIB) | Yes (`study_reengagement`) | Optional at 7+ inactive days (`learning_reminders`) | Targets active enrolled students with no `learning_events` for 3 to 30 days (4-day cooldown for 3 to 6 days inactive, 7-day cooldown for 7+ days) with a deep link to their recent course. |
| `flashcard-reminder-cron` | Student | Daily 01:00 UTC (08:00 WIB) | Yes (`flashcard_reminder`) | Never | Reminds students with 5 or more active SM-2 cards due (`kemajuan_flashcard_murid.due_at <= now()`). |
| `upcoming-session-reminder-cron` | Student & Tutor | Hourly in Inngest and Cloud Tasks | Yes (`tutor_reminder`) | No | Sends push/inbox reminders within 30 minutes of H-24h and H-1h, complementing Capacitor local reminders. |
| `tutorial-session-email-cron` / `tutorial-session-email-worker` | Student & Tutor | Five-minute discovery; exact queued delivery | No | Optional (`events_and_schedules`) | One email at H-1h by default; account preference can select once or repeated before start, with meeting details and participant attachments. Lead 1–1440 minutes, repeat interval at least 5 minutes, maximum 12 emails per session. |
| `tutor-daily-digest-cron` | Tutor | Daily 00:30 UTC (07:30 WIB) | Yes (`tutor_digest`) | Never | Summarizes pending reschedule tickets and ungraded completed quiz attempts when the queue is non-empty. |

- **Role coverage**: [`PushPermissionInit`](../components/notifications/push-permission-init.tsx) is mounted across Student, Tutor, and Admin layouts so all roles register FCM, APNs, WebPush, or Tauri desktop tokens. Student-only local study reminders remain scoped away from Admin surfaces.
- **Mobile inbox parity**: [`NotificationBell`](../components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx) is rendered across Student, Tutor, and Admin desktop sidebars and mobile top navbars.
- **Read-state synchronization on native tap**: [`sendToUser`](../lib/notifications/send.ts) generates the `notifications.id` UUID before push dispatch and embeds `notificationId` in FCM `data` and APNs payloads. When a user taps a native push notification, [`subscribeNativeNotifications`](../lib/native/notifications.ts) forwards `notificationId` to [`NotificationBell`](../components/notifications/notification-bell.tsx), which marks the record read via `PATCH /api/notifications/read` and dispatches `zyx:notifications-changed` to refresh unread badges across components.
- **Broadcast inbox completeness**: [`sendBroadcast`](../lib/notifications/send.ts) targets all accounts in `user` rather than only `user_push_tokens`, ensuring users without push tokens still receive broadcasts in their in-app inbox.
- **Role-aware fallback routing**: Missing or invalid deep links fall back to `/admin`, `/tutor`, or `/dashboard` according to the signed-in role.

Discussion activity is scoped to the thread author and recorded participants at the event's sequence cutoff. A channel subscription, staff role, or mention alone does not enroll someone in a thread. Moderation reports remain separately authorized for admins. The worker rechecks participation, access, account opt-out, channel mute and read state before inbox insertion and push retries. Private academic and technical discussion remote pushes keep generic copy; the authenticated inbox carries a bounded title and message preview. Deleted or superseded message revisions use a status fallback. Admin cross-account history does not expose authored previews. Existing notification rows are not rewritten.

Account activity preferences default on for discussions and flashcard reminders. They control new inbox records and push delivery, independently from email and device permissions. Essential and transactional events remain enabled. Local native study schedules remain device-specific. System templates place available quiz, group, course, or tutorial context in the first line, with details in the body; custom admin and announcement copy remains authored.

The permission reminder uses account-and-device local storage, with a seven-day cooldown from each display or deferral and a persistent never-show choice. Granted permission always bypasses the reminder; a blocked browser or OS gets settings guidance instead of repeated OS consent requests. The notification settings page uses immediate account-scoped activity updates. These personal UI preferences do not add or alter administrative MCP scopes or operations.

# Admin MCP operations

Status: `OPEN / IN PROGRESS`

The existing `/api/mcp/authoring` endpoint now registers admin domain tools alongside authoring. This is a local implementation and validation record. It does not certify a deployed host, OAuth connection, provider integration, or complete parity with every admin UI action.

- New admin permissions require an explicit OAuth request and consent. Existing bearer, cookie and compatibility connections keep their old authoring grants. Resource audience, live session, active admin status, and per-tool scope are checked. No new feature flag was added.
- Read the target and use its current revision. All new writes default to `dryRun: true`. Inspect the returned impact, then send the identical input, request key and confirmation token with `dryRun: false`. Confirmation expires after 10 minutes and binds actor, session, environment, operation and payload.
- Keep one request key per intended change. Business changes and the success/idempotency receipt commit in the same PostgreSQL transaction. Changed payloads under a prior key fail. Stale revisions require rereading and a new plan.
- API credentials and provider errors are never returned. Response data, user email, activation-token values and related operations have separate scopes. Legacy group labels containing activation tokens are redacted. Inputs and results are capped at 1 MB; list pagination is bounded.

See [agent-first content operations](agent-first-content.md) for registered capability discovery, structured scope recovery, own-operation receipts, shared blog revision checks and public media resolution. Repository plugin 0.5.0 adds five focused skills without changing environment identity or automatically granting scopes.

`admin_operation_jobs` is the durable outbox. The existing Deno Inngest registry runs `admin-operations-outbox` every minute, processes at most 25 queued jobs and allows only one function instance at a time. Jobs bind the originating live admin session, OAuth client, resource, required scopes and environment. Enqueue and execution both check persisted OAuth consent, including secondary response-read permission for exports. Revoked or narrowed consent prevents queued provider effects. Manual/session connections cannot delegate these admin provider operations; legacy jobs without client/resource binding fail closed. No bearer token is stored. Missing provider configuration fails before an effect.

A claim commits before provider work. A provider timeout or crash is marked `unknown`; claims older than 15 minutes become `unknown`. These attempts are never replayed automatically. Use `adminjobs.get`, inspect the provider, then use `adminjobs.reconcile` with a reason and evidence reference. This records an operator assertion, not automated provider verification. Only queued jobs can be cancelled. A queued tool result is not delivery or provider success.

Google Sheets exports use the existing entity spreadsheet, owned A1 block, fingerprint and conflict checks. Read `forms.responses.sheet_state` first. A changed data or sheet snapshot is rejected. Manual edits require the operator to type `TIMPA <form-slug>`; the skill forbids inventing that consent. Deleted linked spreadsheets are not automatically recreated by this MCP workflow. Google API writes and a database receipt cannot share a transaction, so uncertain provider outcomes require reconciliation.

Notification targets are explicit active user snapshots. Course and group audiences cannot silently widen to all users. A snapshot is limited to 1000 recipients. Email preferences are not bypassed by reusing generic broadcasts for campaign mail. The generic notification tool sends the existing in-app/FCM broadcast, not campaign email.

Meet operations use the existing Google adapter and member provisioning. A created provider reference is checkpointed before subsequent calls. Partial member provisioning is reported; an uncertain creation must be reconciled rather than recreated. Generation uses the existing KO pipeline and its existing accounting path.

Form definitions validate all currently supported question types, options, grids, scale ranges, file-size limits and absolute schedules. Updates cannot reinterpret existing responses by changing their question array. Preview and simulation never submit, upload, spend the one-response allowance or update Sheets. Identity and file ownership are not attested in simulation. The embedded UI is an isolated answer preview; server simulation remains authoritative for schedule/access checks.

The MCP Apps UI has no network or upload access and uses text nodes for supplied content. Text/structured results remain available to hosts without UI support. Response summaries omit identity and open answers, use respondent denominators, and count each multiselect bucket once per respondent. Summary and Sheets snapshots cap at 5000 responses per date filter. CSV export is paged and guards formula-like cells. Response date filters use native PostgreSQL timestamp comparisons.

Media listing uses bounded provider pagination. Small media uploads support at most 512 KiB, use the shared key builder, check the allowed type signature, create a new object, and clear stored upload bytes after success. Larger files retain the existing upload UI. No arbitrary path, SQL, HTTP or shell tool is exposed.
