It creates a session, connects CDP, visits the empty public verification preview without cookies or bundle data, captures a screenshot and PDF in memory, and releases the session. It logs only version, status and byte lengths. The diagnostic does not retry long provider delays inside an open request. The manual deployment diagnostic workflow uses the same provider selection and skips Cloudflare-specific account diagnostics for Steel.

Before running a real chapter, use `Operate V4 verification` with `inspect` on the matching environment branch. Recheck the actual revision rather than trusting an old checksum. Cancel only the exact old Cloudflare native run if it remains queued/running, then retry through the deployed trusted worker with consistent web/worker identity. Do not sign receipts locally. Keep code validation, successful Steel smoke, all checks PASS, ready receipt, persisted PDF evidence and independent pedagogical approval as separate acceptance results. No completed chapter run is established by this implementation or by a smoke test.

HTTP acquisition preserves `Retry-After` for transient 429 responses. The active queue adapter schedules bounded retries using both job and queue limits without keeping a worker request open; missing or invalid delay headers use 25 seconds. Explicit daily browser quota exhaustion, denied access and invalid session metadata stop without retrying. Cloudflare can return the canonical `browser-rendering` CDP route for a `browser-run` acquisition; accept either route only on the exact API origin, account and acquired session. Terminal state preserves the sanitized browser failure category. Run the existing Deno deploy workflow manually with `browser_diagnostics=true` and the exact `diagnostic_environment` to count active sessions, acquire/release an empty browser, then exercise a real Playwright CDP connection, preview hydration and screenshot without deploying or changing application data. The probe logs only sanitized status, counts, endpoint family, browser version and quota classification. Its bounded retry respects acquisition rate limits between probes. An empty active-session list alone cannot identify the exhausted quota. Cloudflare's [limits](https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/limits/) and [session lifecycle](https://developers.cloudflare.com/browser-run/cdp/session-management/) document these separate limits and cleanup endpoints.

The manual `Operate V4 verification` workflow runs only from the matching `main`/production or `staging`/staging branch and uses that environment's existing secrets. `inspect` checks staging Deno variable context metadata when its deployment token is available, without logging values, then lists draft V4 titles and revision checksums read-only; an exact revision also reports artifacts, trace errors and retry scheduling. `retry` requires one exact inspected checksum, requests the established trusted job and waits for its complete receipt plus matching PDF-persistence marker, or reports the provider's persisted future retry time. `cancel` cancels only the unique run attached to that exact draft revision and records its before/after status. It cannot review or publish content. `evidence` downloads only verified artifacts plus learning content into a private GitHub artifact with a 3-day retention for visual review; it omits credentials, account identities and private storage keys. A local or CI command must never execute browser checks and sign a production receipt in place of the deployed trusted worker.

For local testing only, build the Node ESM adapter from the current workspace:

```powershell
bun scripts/authoring/build-local-verification-renderer.ts
node artifacts/authoring-verification/renderer.mjs --base-url http://127.0.0.1:3100 --port 3101
```

Set `AUTHORING_VERIFICATION_RENDERER_URL` to this local adapter and provide `AUTHORING_VERIFICATION_RENDERER_SECRET` through the process environment. Keep the existing `DIKTAT_RENDERER_URL` and secret for its separate `/render` API. The local adapter binds loopback and needs Playwright Chromium. Actual PDF pages are counted and rasterized by the existing PDF parser; Poppler is not a deployment prerequisite.

The build resolves workspace aliases and leaves installed packages external. It embeds the actual build fingerprint and expected Chromium metadata, then records the bundle SHA and fingerprint in `renderer-build.json`. The fingerprint binds explicit source bytes, installed package versions, KaTeX CSS/font bytes, Playwright browser metadata, contract, playbook and print profile. At startup, embedded and live fingerprints must match; an old bundle refuses changed source or dependencies instead of claiming their newer identity. The runner retains that snapshot and checks plan fields plus the actual launched Chromium version before execution. Rebuild and restart after a relevant source or dependency change. Keep all `PRODUCT_V4_RUNTIME_FILES`, package manifests and KaTeX assets available in the runtime trace.

The application build runs `prepare-web-verification.ts`, embeds its public fingerprint in the verification preview, and generates `lib/compute/product-v4-build-runtime.json` for Deno. The Deno release pipeline regenerates that identity from the exact source and locked packages before upload. Deno consumes the build identity instead of reading frontend files excluded from its deployment. A stale web build cannot satisfy trusted checks.

The controlled `/authoring-verification` preview excludes site telemetry. Its executor rejects unexpected external requests rather than suppressing their errors. A local production build, Node HTTP renderer and synthetic canonical V4 ZIP have exercised all 22 derived checks, including web states and PDF page capture. This is local evidence; it does not certify deployed endpoints, installed plugin imports or a complete chapter's pedagogic acceptance.

Reader checks reject display-math scrolling at normal text size and require named, keyboard-accessible scroll regions at doubled text size. Pixel-based typography is explicitly doubled and measured; scientific diagram coordinates retain their existing zoom controls. Chapter captures preserve the configured CSS viewport and allow at most 300 slices per check.

Verification checkpoints preparation, each requirement, final receipt readback and PDF persistence as separate durable job steps through the selected queue adapter. Step discovery performs no database or storage requests outside those steps. Long web captures use at most 2 viewport slices per step on the existing Hono transport, with a 15-second timeout per screenshot and a 60-second deadline for remote browser work. Cleanup has a separate 15-second bound and starts before database/storage evidence writes, reducing idle browser billing. Abort guards prevent delayed asset loading from starting a new browser after the deadline. Capture outputs contain artifact metadata rather than image bytes. Progress reports completed/total checks and an update timestamp. Provider backoff persists `retryAt`; the 20-minute stale lease starts after that scheduled time instead of expiring while a scheduled retry waits for quota. Attempts without updates or a future retry time still expire after 20 minutes. Artifacts and dependency/attempt checks remain mandatory before a passing receipt.

Machine render receipts and independent pedagogic/visual review are separate gates. A passing browser job establishes the recorded machine checks, not mathematical equivalence or human readability by itself.

The focused suite exercises initialization, both catalogs, 21 independent fixture skills, complete frontmatter, text/blob digests, cursors, isolation, traversal, tampering, size limits, and a local HTTP import rehearsal. Linux CI runs the symlink case; Windows skips it because link creation depends on host privileges.

Local verification on 2026-10-21 additionally exercised the real six-skill V4 candidate through MCP HTTP transport, checked every resource digest, confirmed plugin `0.4.0` bootstrap compatibility and rejected candidate serving in deployed environments. The distribution suite passed 11 tests with one Windows symlink skip; Python packaging passed 11 tests for both environment identities. Runtime-binding tests reject live dependency drift, course/excerpt swaps, changed asset bytes, unknown figure permission and newer plans presented to an older embedded renderer. Primary-agent browser/PDF verification is recorded separately.

Run `bun scripts/test-contracts.ts tests/contracts/product-v4-publication-integration.test.ts` in its own process. Its isolated PostgreSQL-compatible fixture exercises the real publication and quality gates: a current signed fixture receipt, explicit section/rubric approval and PDF evidence permit publication; stale or forged receipt, incomplete review, stale PDF, changed source and missing section approval reject atomically. Its fixture executor tests gate wiring; it does not substitute for actual browser/PDF execution.

A read-only host doctor observed an existing Antigravity staging package at `0.2.0` with legacy connection identity and checksum drift; its production package was absent. No package was installed or reloaded by these checks. Codex/ChatGPT active imports, OAuth sessions, external pinned-source updates and deployed MCP endpoints require their own observed acceptance and are not certified by local package tests.

After deployment, supply a short-lived read-only token through `AUTHORING_MCP_SMOKE_TOKEN`, without printing or saving it:

```powershell
bun scripts/smoke-authoring-skills.ts --url https://staging.zyxacademy.com/api/mcp/authoring
bun scripts/smoke-authoring-skills.ts --url 'https://staging.zyxacademy.com/api/mcp/authoring?skills=all'
```

Repeat on the exact authorized production hostname after staging passes. The smoke calls initialize, every catalog page, skills/get, and every resources/read, verifying all bytes. It makes no authoring or database writes and does not prove ChatGPT import.

In the plugin draft, use Scan Tools against the default endpoint, confirm the matching `zyx-authoring-stg` or `zyx-authoring` router and all workflow references, then review and submit the new plugin version. Adding a custom MCP URL does not guarantee installation. Native package uploads and MCP snapshots require separate host acceptance evidence.

Deployment evidence is recorded in per-rollout smoke receipts. ChatGPT Scan Tools acceptance requires an observed successful scan and confirmation of the imported draft. OpenAI Platform requires a verified developer identity before creating or uploading that draft.

section: Exact production draft fixture in staging
content:
The manual `Operate V4 verification` workflow with action `prepare-fixture` runs only from `staging`, with an explicitly inspected revision checksum. Use it only after the operator authorizes copying that draft and its required learning dependencies to staging. Its production job issues SELECTs and downloads the exact ZIP; it exports no account rows, sessions, learner data, reviews or receipts. The private transfer artifact expires after 1 day.

The staging job uses the existing staging guard, checks all identity references and current dependency pins before writes, inserts only missing parent/Idea/source/chunk rows, and refuses conflicts. Account identities must already exist in staging. Source-figure assets and external product dependencies are deliberately unsupported by this focused transfer. Existing drafts are left for native inspection and retry rather than creating another attempt. A new draft is staged through `stageProductBundle`, keeps the original bundle checksum, and requests the normal deployed trusted worker. Polling waits for all checks, a ready receipt and matching persisted PDF evidence; it does not execute checks or sign receipts locally. Pedagogic approval and publication remain separate.

Fresh URL connections offer all 46 OAuth scopes with the four existing authoring defaults selected. Explicit narrower requests remain exact. OAuth consent grants only selected requested scopes; legacy session and compatibility tokens retain the five authoring scopes. Reauthorize to add permissions. Package 0.5.4 uses short environment IDs, portable call names and distinct staging skill names; see [MCP host compatibility](mcp-host-compatibility.md) for naming, migration, and scope recovery. Verify the tool catalog and scope grants in the target environment before use. Local implementation does not verify deployment or external client behavior.

The native package includes `zyx-admin-operations` and five focused workflows for blog, content revisions, forms, media and recovery alongside the six academic authoring skills. Admin operations use explicit scopes, signed plans and outbox receipts rather than authoring bootstrap stages. The locked server snapshot remains separate; package contents alone do not prove that an installed MCP host can discover these workflows. See [Admin MCP operations](admin-mcp.md).

# Cloud Run Staging

Status: `ACTIVE` staging candidate workflow. Vercel remains available via the [manual Vercel staging runbook](vercel-staging.md).

The container image (`Dockerfile.cloud-run`) packages the Next.js 16.3 standalone build on Linux AMD64 (Debian glibc): Bun installs the frozen lockfile and runs `build:authoring-skills`, V4 fingerprinting, and `next build`, while the runtime serves under Node 24 as an unprivileged user with `.next/static` and `public/` copied separately.

| Setting | Candidate |
|---|---|
| Project | `zyx-academy` |
| Region | Bangkok, `asia-southeast3`, Tier 1 |
| Service | `zyx-academy-staging-web` |
| Platform | Linux amd64, second generation |
| Runtime | 1 vCPU, 1 GiB, 8080, 300-second request timeout |
| Scaling | Minimum 0, service maximum 1, concurrency 8 |
| Billing | Request-based with CPU throttling |
| Data | Existing pinned staging Neon PostgreSQL and private Neon Storage |
| Background | Existing staging Neon Functions and Inngest. Follow the matching-worker release gate. |

The Cloudflare Worker forwards dynamic requests to the Google service URL. The Cloud Run gateway rejects traffic without the shared origin credential before forwarding it to Next.js. Treat that credential as a bearer secret. Direct traffic can still reach the gateway and incur Cloud Run requests, so monitor rejected traffic. Configure separate Worker and Google secrets with the same value and coordinate their rotation. Keep origin credentials out of shell history, request logs and PRs. Use TLS across both hops.

The edge caches only eligible anonymous immutable `/_next/static/*` responses with no query or a single deployment ID query. Requests carrying session cookies bypass the shared cache. Everything else goes to the originating handler with shared caching disabled, including API, storage proxy, server actions, session traffic, RSC, telemetry, and `/_next/image`. Next.js retains local image optimization and its ephemeral per-instance cache. Authorized course and review images use direct browser requests so their access checks are applied on every request. Prefer an existing good-sized WebP or AVIF derivative for newly reviewed public photographs. Measure the first optimizer request and repeats before considering paid edge transforms or generating variants on upload. Static cache misses reach Cloud Run. Keep both Cloud Run revisions and their immutable images. An open page from a previous release may need to reload if a chunk is absent from the new serving revision. Validate old-tab navigation during candidate testing before DNS acceptance.

Bangkok's native Cloud Run domain mapping is unavailable. An origin rule alone still needs the correct origin TLS hostname, trusted application host and the origin credential. The Worker supplies those without adding a Google load balancer. A Google external load balancer adds forwarding-rule and processing charges and is outside this candidate. [Cloud Run custom domains](https://cloud.google.com/run/docs/mapping-custom-domains) · [Worker Custom Domains](https://developers.cloudflare.com/workers/configuration/routing/custom-domains/) · [Next.js self-hosting](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/guides/self-hosting)

The `import-secrets` operation reads GitHub Environment `staging`. It imports the required application credentials, including `PYTHON_RUNTIME_TOKEN_SECRET`, `CF_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, `CF_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN`, `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, and `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN`, along with configured optional Google, Gemini fallback, Vectorize, Live Quiz, Steel, and analytics credentials. Companion server settings are versioned with those credentials. Empty optional settings are skipped. CI credentials, unused R2 rollback credentials, public build settings and feature flags are excluded. Existing staging Firebase credentials remain separately managed to preserve project isolation.

Provision each destination under `zyx-staging-web-`, grant the staging runtime access, then run the approved import. Imports print only secret names and numeric versions. Attach those numeric versions to a candidate before promotion; importing alone does not configure Cloud Run. Preserve existing bindings when repairing missing settings, use the currently serving image, verify the candidate and keep the prior revision available for rollback. Deployment validation requires the Python ticket key, Cloudflare AI Gateway settings (`CF_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, `CF_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN`), and Zyra control-plane settings (`ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_URL`, `ZYRA_CONTROL_PLANE_TOKEN`). This repairs existing API and MCP environment configuration without changing tools, scopes, consent, capability discovery, playbooks or packaged skills.

Staging Web and Android Nightly use Firebase project `zyx-academy-staging`. Production Web and Android Stable are configured as separate apps in the same project, with separate sender accounts. App registration separates client configuration, but Firebase messaging permissions and the sender ID remain shared at project scope. Keep `NEXT_PUBLIC_FIREBASE_*` aligned in `CLOUD_RUN_STAGING_PUBLIC_CONFIG` in both GitHub environments, `staging` and `staging-cloud-run`, and in the staging Cloud Run runtime. The browser worker imports `/firebase-config.js`, which exposes only public runtime Firebase settings with `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The staging sender is `zyx-staging-fcm-sender@zyx-academy-staging.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, with only `cloudmessaging.messages.create` on the staging Firebase project. Bind `FIREBASE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON` to a numeric version of Secret Manager secret `zyx-staging-web-firebase-service-account-json` in Google project `zyx-academy`. Its value is base64-encoded sender JSON. The Cloud Run staging runtime identity has access to this secret. Private keys belong in Secret Manager and restricted operator backups, never in Git or public configuration.

Build with `operation=candidate`; retain existing traffic until browser background delivery and Android Nightly registration and delivery have been checked. Firebase API acceptance alone does not prove device delivery.

Record the results of these read-only commands with an authenticated operator account. Share only sanitized metadata.

```bash
gcloud projects describe zyx-academy --format='value(projectId,projectNumber)'
gcloud billing projects describe zyx-academy
gcloud run services list --project=zyx-academy --region=asia-southeast3
gcloud run services list --project=zyx-academy --region=asia-east1
gcloud artifacts repositories list --project=zyx-academy --location=asia-southeast3
```

Have the billing owner verify available credits, expiry and eligible SKUs. Review incremental costs before enabling required APIs or creating resources. In IAM, create separate staging deploy and runtime identities. Scope Artifact Registry Writer to the candidate repository, Cloud Run Developer to the bootstrapped candidate service, and Service Account User on the runtime identity to the deploy identity. Give the runtime identity Secret Manager Secret Accessor on the specific staging secrets. Give the deploy identity access to the dedicated preflight secrets it reads. Grant the GitHub federated principal Workload Identity User on the deploy identity. Pin WIF to repository ID `1192540511`, owner ID `139353811`, staging ref and the exact workflow ref. Map `google.subject=assertion.sub` and `attribute.repository_id=assertion.repository_id`. Use this provider attribute condition:

```text
assertion.repository_id == '1192540511' &&
assertion.repository_owner_id == '139353811' &&
assertion.ref == 'refs/heads/staging' &&
assertion.workflow_ref == 'soezyxstt/zyxacademy/.github/workflows/deploy-cloud-run-staging.yml@refs/heads/staging'
```

Bind Workload Identity User on the CI identity to `principalSet://iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/attribute.repository_id/1192540511`. Use explicit Secret Manager versions and dedicated staging-only resources. [GitHub federation setup](https://cloud.google.com/iam/docs/workload-identity-federation-with-deployment-pipelines)

Configure the `staging-cloud-run` GitHub environment with a deployment branch rule for `staging` and no required reviewers. Candidate, promote, and rollback run on manual dispatch. The `import-secrets` job uses the shared `staging` environment and still requires reviewer approval. GitHub registers manual dispatch from the workflow definition on `main`. Dispatch with `--ref staging`. [GitHub manual workflows](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/manage-workflow-runs/manually-run-a-workflow)

Copy these variables from `staging` to `staging-cloud-run` before adopting the workflow change. Keep the workload identity provider variable in both environments for secret import.

| Variable | Value |
|---|---|
| `CLOUD_RUN_STAGING_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER` | Full `projects/PROJECT_NUMBER/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/POOL/providers/PROVIDER` name |
| `CLOUD_RUN_STAGING_PUBLIC_CONFIG` | Flat JSON of allowed public build settings with exact `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` |
| `CLOUD_RUN_STAGING_PREFLIGHT_DATABASE_VERSION` | Numeric Secret Manager version of `zyx-staging-web-preflight-database-url` |

Re-enter the existing `SENTRY_AUTH_TOKEN` as an environment secret in `staging-cloud-run` to preserve source map uploads. If staging sets `QUEUE_PROVIDER` as an environment variable, configure the same value there. Verify the Workload Identity provider and deploy identity accept the OIDC subject for `staging-cloud-run` with the repository, ref, and workflow restrictions above intact.

Use deploy identity `zyx-staging-web-ci@zyx-academy.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, runtime identity `zyx-staging-web-runtime@zyx-academy.iam.gserviceaccount.com`, and a Standard Docker repository named `zyx-staging-web` in Bangkok. CI publishes unique commit-and-run tags and deploys immutable digests. Bootstrap only the new service with an approved harmless placeholder image. Configure its single container with the runtime identity, ingress `all`, a default URL, and the invoker IAM check disabled so the Worker can reach the application-layer gate. Validate that the placeholder exposes no staging application or data. Set the runtime environment and Secret Manager bindings on that service before dispatch. Reserve a controlled window for changing the service template.

Set `ZYX_ENVIRONMENT=staging`, `ZYX_MCP_ENVIRONMENT=staging`, `BETTER_AUTH_URL` to the exact build origin, `STORAGE_PROVIDER_MODE=neon`, `NEON_STORAGE_BUCKET=zyx-staging`, `AWS_REGION=ap-southeast-1`, `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL_S3` to the documented branch endpoint, and `INNGEST_ENV=staging-40f1da25`. Use the existing staging endpoints for `COMPUTE_SERVICE_URL` and `DIKTAT_RENDERER_URL`. Mirror the public JSON as plaintext runtime settings. Bind `DATABASE_URL`, `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `BETTER_AUTH_SECRET`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID`, `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `GEMINI_API_KEY`, `INNGEST_EVENT_KEY`, `INNGEST_SIGNING_KEY`, `COMPUTE_SERVICE_SECRET`, `DIKTAT_RENDERER_SECRET`, `CF_API_TOKEN` or `CF_BROWSER_API_TOKEN`, and `CLOUD_RUN_ORIGIN_TOKEN` to numeric versions of dedicated `zyx-staging-web-*` secrets. Set `CF_ACCOUNT_ID` for Browser Run. Use the staging application database role and a distinct read-only `zyx_staging_web_preflight` login with access to the migration journal and cutover marker. Scope the CI Secret Accessor grants to these two database URLs and the origin token. Consult the workflow's validator for the complete runtime allowlist.

The `import-secrets` operation copies only the required staging credentials to dedicated Secret Manager destinations. It uses the same branch restriction and federated deploy identity as the release job, with required reviewer approval in the shared `staging` environment. It sends values through standard input and records only setting names and numeric versions. It performs no deployment. The staging database URL must use the pinned pooler and application role.

In Cloud Shell, prepare empty destinations and give CI temporary permission to add versions. This example expects new names. If any destination already exists, inspect its metadata and IAM before continuing.

```bash
(
  set -e
  project=zyx-academy
  staging_ci=zyx-staging-web-ci@zyx-academy.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  staging_runtime=zyx-staging-web-runtime@zyx-academy.iam.gserviceaccount.com
  for suffix in aws-access-key-id aws-secret-access-key better-auth-secret cf-api-token \
      compute-service-secret database-url diktat-renderer-secret gemini-api-key \
      google-client-id google-client-secret inngest-event-key inngest-signing-key resend-api-key; do
    secret="zyx-staging-web-$suffix"
    gcloud secrets create "$secret" --project="$project" --replication-policy=automatic
    gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding "$secret" --project="$project" \
      --member="serviceAccount:$staging_runtime" --role=roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor
    gcloud secrets add-iam-policy-binding "$secret" --project="$project" \
      --member="serviceAccount:$staging_ci" --role=roles/secretmanager.secretVersionAdder
  done
)
```

After the workflow is registered on the default branch and the import code is on `staging`, dispatch `gh workflow run deploy-cloud-run-staging.yml --ref staging -f operation=import-secrets`. Review and approve the resource-scoped transfer in GitHub. Record the listed versions. If the import stops partway, it reports the last successful version references. A retry can add versions to an already imported name. Only explicitly pinned versions are used by deployments. Remove the temporary CI Secret Version Adder binding on each destination once the transfer is complete. Keep CI Secret Accessor only on the exact runtime database URL, preflight database URL and origin token. The origin token and new read-only preflight credential are provisioned separately.

After registering the workflow and provisioning the target, dispatch the candidate from the exact accepted staging ref:

```bash
gh workflow run deploy-cloud-run-staging.yml --ref staging -f operation=candidate
gh workflow run deploy-cloud-run-staging.yml --ref staging -f operation=promote -f revision=REVISION
gh workflow run deploy-cloud-run-staging.yml --ref staging -f operation=rollback -f revision=PREVIOUS_REVISION
```

Use the tagged candidate URL as the temporary Worker origin for acceptance. Choose the exact revision for any traffic change. After promotion, move the Worker to the stable service origin and verify it. The first release has a placeholder behind the stable service URL and uses Vercel as its fallback. Validate the rollback on a later compatible two-revision pair before depending on it.

Mirror the public build values used by Vercel staging for Firebase, realtime, analytics and flags. Align the candidate HTTPS origin in the build URL, Better Auth URL and Worker config. Use the staging OAuth client and register its exact `/api/auth/callback/google` URI for the temporary and final origins as needed. Review compute, renderer, Vectorize, Zyra, Inngest, email, Sentry, PostHog and signed-download CORS settings against the eligible staging environment. Preserve existing application feature states. Never export an existing runtime secret through CI output.

Use the staging branch `br-gentle-scene-azq0gp91` in project `muddy-sky-44104897`, database `neondb`, the documented pinned pooled host, and private branch-scoped bucket `zyx-staging`. Follow [DATABASE.md](../DATABASE.md) and the [manual Vercel staging runbook](vercel-staging.md). Verify the migration journal read-only, then verify the matching staging worker. Deploying web code performs no migration, backfill, seed, worker restart, or scheduler registration. Cloud Run does not run Vercel cron definitions.

Cloudflare's connected account returned no `zyxacademy.com` zone. Public DNS returned Cloudflare nameservers `elliot.ns.cloudflare.com` and `lucy.ns.cloudflare.com`, and the staging CNAME currently resolves to `a5534c9d38d29398.vercel-dns-017.com`. Request access to the existing zone from its owner. Preserve authoritative nameservers. Export the active zone and verify production, staging, MX, SPF, DKIM, DMARC, CAA, verification and subdomain records before any approved cutover.

The repository Worker config disables automatic routes. Copy `workers/staging-web-edge/wrangler.jsonc` to `workers/staging-web-edge/wrangler.candidate.jsonc` and keep the copy local. Enable `workers_dev` only in that copy. Set `PUBLIC_ORIGIN` to `https://zyx-academy-staging-edge.<account-subdomain>.workers.dev` and `CLOUD_RUN_ORIGIN` to the exact tagged Cloud Run HTTPS URL. Deploy with the lockfile-pinned Wrangler and set the origin secret using its prompt:

```bash
bunx --no-install wrangler deploy --config workers/staging-web-edge/wrangler.candidate.jsonc
bunx --no-install wrangler secret put CLOUD_RUN_ORIGIN_TOKEN --config workers/staging-web-edge/wrangler.candidate.jsonc
node --test deploy/cloud-run/origin-gateway.test.mjs workers/staging-web-edge/index.test.mjs
```

Keep preview URLs disabled. The Worker reports Cache API outcomes in `X-Zyx-Edge-Cache`. Record `CF-Cache-Status` separately when present.

Cloudflare Access can disable Worker Cache API behavior. Verify production-like cache on the approved custom domain if the temporary endpoint or its access policy bypasses it. Use a temporary staging Worker endpoint first, with its exact HTTPS host consistently configured on Worker, Cloud Run and OAuth. For the approved final cutover, save the current staging record, then replace only that CNAME by attaching the Worker Custom Domain `staging.zyxacademy.com`. Cloudflare provisions the DNS record and TLS certificate. The dedicated R2 public bucket uses a separate custom domain, `cdn-staging.zyxacademy.com`. Verify both HTTPS endpoints and leave other DNS records alone. Cache Rules and final-host cookies, OAuth and external callbacks require a live hostname after setup.

The dedicated `zyx-staging-public` bucket did not exist in the connected account. Create a Standard bucket after checking billing and approving the domain activation. Keep managed `r2.dev` access off. Publish the reviewed repository image with an account and API token restricted to that bucket:

```bash
node scripts/cloud-run/publish-public-media.mjs
node scripts/cloud-run/publish-public-media.mjs --publish
```

The first command validates the manifest and hashes locally. The second uploads only the listed repository file with its immutable content-derived key. Attach the R2 custom domain and verify the exact key, content type, immutable response header and cache behavior before setting `NEXT_PUBLIC_STAGING_MEDIA_ORIGIN=https://cdn-staging.zyxacademy.com` for the candidate build. An unset value keeps the bundled image URL. Replacements use a new checksum. Retain reviewed old versions through rollback. For a takedown, delete the exact object and purge the exact Cloudflare URL. A previously downloaded immutable file can remain in browser caches through its advertised TTL. [R2 public domains](https://developers.cloudflare.com/r2/buckets/public-buckets/) · [Cloudflare purge](https://developers.cloudflare.com/cache/how-to/purge-cache/)

| Material | Treatment |
|---|---|
| Reviewed brand cover in the manifest | Public and immutable |
| Course, Diktat, article, video and interactive-document assets | Existing enrollment and entitlement paths, including protected downloads and signed access |
| Quiz, exam, schedule and Zyra user attachments | Existing user, tutor, course and administrative checks |
| Form and question images | Existing reference- and route-specific access. Require individual review for publication. |
| Product bundles, source packs, source images, renderer and temporary outputs | Keep private |
| Existing media library or legacy URLs | Preserve existing paths and audit individual keys before any publication |

The connected account reported managed public endpoints enabled for the legacy `zyx` and `zyx-staging` buckets, disabled for both `zyx-zyra-private-*` buckets. The staging legacy list returned three unclassified screenshots. Treat the inventory as partial, keep their URLs out of the candidate configuration, and review direct legacy access with the storage owner. # MCP host compatibility

Status: `ACTIVE`

This contract covers the HTTP MCP endpoint, initial OAuth consent, tool schemas and names, and the 0.5.4 plugin package. Repository checks establish local behavior. A merged change, deployed endpoint, and installed host package are separate release targets.

The initial HTTP 401 challenge requests the complete supported OAuth set. An authorization request with no scope, or a blank scope, uses that same set. It currently contains 46 permissions: five authoring permissions and 41 admin permissions. The consent view groups them into Authoring, Academic, Content, Access, Coordination, and System.

For that complete initial set, only `authoring:read`, `authoring:stage`, `authoring:review`, and `authoring:withdraw` start selected. Publication and all admin permissions require a selection. An explicit narrower request keeps its exact scope set and selection behavior. The server never adds unavailable options to a narrow request or grants an unselected permission.

The authorization action validates that selected scopes are a nonempty subset of requested scopes. Authorization codes, access tokens, and persisted consent contain only that selection. Silent authorization cannot enlarge an existing grant. Existing session/manual connections retain their five authoring scopes; the full initial OAuth set does not expand those paths. Existing live-session, active-admin, resource-audience, and per-tool checks still apply.

If a host keeps requesting the old four-scope set, the server correctly shows those four. Start a fresh OAuth connection to discover the new initial challenge. Refreshing tools or adding `?skills=all` does not add permissions. Incremental reauthorization must request the intended complete grant, including any existing permissions that should remain, because explicit consent replaces the prior selection.

`tools/list` exposes one portable name per registered tool. Names use ASCII letters, digits, `_`, and `-`, with a maximum of 40 characters. Most names replace dots with underscores. One existing long name has a fixed alias:

| Canonical operation ID | Public call name |
| --- | --- |
| `admin.environment` | `admin_environment` |
| `workflow.get_playbook` | `workflow_get_playbook` |
| `forms.responses.list` | `forms_responses_list` |
| `authoring.get_solution_collection_review_context` | `authoring_solution_review_context` |

A public SDK transport adapter maps call names back to canonical IDs before SDK validation. It translates only the names in `tools/list` and `tools/call`, preserving schemas, annotations, metadata, request identity, transport options, and response data. Each fresh stateless server builds its map during registration, so an alias call does not depend on an earlier list request. Duplicate aliases, cross-name collisions, or overlong names fail registration rather than acquiring unstable numeric suffixes.

Legacy dotted calls remain accepted but do not appear as duplicate catalog entries. Canonical IDs still identify scopes, signed plans, receipts, retry keys, and browser Ops AI operations. In particular, `admin_operation_receipt` still accepts an argument such as `operation: "blog.create"`.

`admin_capabilities` returns `callName` beside each canonical operation name and `callNames` beside workflow operation IDs. Authoring playbooks and contracts expose `toolNaming`, including the fixed alias. Their existing `nextActions` and tool references remain canonical operation IDs. The server instructions and all 12 skills tell agents to use the listed public call names while preserving dotted operation arguments. Embedded forms previews do not issue tool calls.

Antigravity plugin tool declarations can include both plugin and server IDs before the remote name. The package therefore uses short, distinct environment IDs:

| Environment | Plugin ID | MCP server key | Resource endpoint |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Staging | `zyx-stg` | `zyx-stg` | `https://staging.zyxacademy.com/api/mcp/authoring` |
| Production candidate | `zyx-prd` | `zyx-prd` | `https://www.zyxacademy.com/api/mcp/authoring` |

The composed pattern `mcp_<plugin>_<server>_<tool>` has a 20-character prefix for either package. The 40-character tool budget keeps it within 64. The current catalog has 194 tools, unique aliases, and a longest composed name of 59 characters. Package and server checks cover this complete catalog, not only one sample. An arbitrary longer host-selected server label can still exceed a provider's limit; use the documented short key for URL-only connections too.

Upgrading the server does not rename an installed plugin. Update the package through the host's supported installation flow, replace the old staging connection with `zyx-stg`, and refresh its tool catalog. The package doctor reports the old long IDs; it does not edit host caches or silently delete connections. Installing the staging package does not migrate a production connection. The production render remains a local candidate until its separate release.

OAuth remains direct HTTP. A renamed host installation may register a new OAuth client and need consent again. The resource URL stays fixed. A manual-bearer stdio proxy is not equivalent: manual connections cannot delegate the admin/provider jobs that require persisted OAuth consent.

Every advertised tool input schema must validate against both Draft-07 and Draft 2020-12 meta-schemas. Any advertised output schema receives the same check. The current catalog contains 194 input schemas and no output schemas. A catalog regression test uses the real HTTP `tools/list` response and an invalid legacy tuple as a negative control.

`source_extract_figure.crop` is a homogeneous array of exactly four finite numbers between 0 and 1, with `items` as a schema object and `minItems`/`maxItems` equal to 4. Runtime validation also requires `x1 > x0` and `y1 > y0`. This preserves crop geometry and prevents Draft-07 tuple syntax (`items: [...]`) from disabling the tool in strict 2020-12 hosts. Invalid crops fail SDK validation before source access.

The package renderer gives every staging skill directory, frontmatter name, cross-skill link and host invocation prompt exactly one `-stg` suffix. Production keeps the canonical skill names. For example, staging installs `zyx-product-bundle-mcp-stg`, while production installs `zyx-product-bundle-mcp`. The compact MCP router is `zyx-authoring-stg` on staging and `zyx-authoring` on production; their resource paths and ZIP roots are distinct too.

The explicit `skill` argument in `workflow_get_playbook` remains a canonical bootstrap role, such as `zyx-product-bundle-mcp`. It is not the installed host skill name. Generated examples preserve those six protocol role IDs. Tool names and dotted operation arguments follow their separate rules above.

`Sync Zyx Authoring MCP Plugin` builds both environments and verifies that their skill names do not overlap before publishing the selected target. It compares published files against the remote baseline and keeps production publication restricted to `main`. The renderer removes obsolete generated paths only in an owned output tree. The host doctor reports old unsuffixed staging installations; updating a host package and refreshing its installed skill list remains a host action.

Skills use the server's existing job and receipt tools. Cloud Tasks and Scheduler manage delivery through the shared queue adapter; retained Inngest symbols do not identify the active provider. Keep job IDs, verification attempt IDs, operation receipts and bootstrap tokens in their own fields. Respect returned retry times, inspect uncertain outcomes before repeating a mutation, and retain trusted verification and publication checks.

OAuth access refresh belongs to the configured host connection. Waiting for a job does not require reconnecting. If the server reports missing consent, revoked refresh authorization or an expired plan, apply that specific remedy and recheck the same target before resuming.

Focused tests cover the real MCP HTTP catalog, both JSON Schema dialects, portable and legacy calls on fresh servers, SDK crop validation, alias collision and length guards, exact consent selections, narrower requests, and refusal to widen grants silently. Discovery tests preserve canonical receipt identity. Package tests render both environments and check all 12 skills, host prompts, disjoint skill names, canonical bootstrap arguments, namespace budgets, migration diagnostics, and deterministic releases. Catalog tests verify that both environment routers keep valid references and distinct resource identities.

The local consent fixture exercises all 46 options, four selected defaults, an added admin selection, no selection, keyboard focus, and an explicit narrow request at 380 by 844 and 1536 by 864 in both themes. It uses synthetic identities and does not authorize a real account. Installed Antigravity/ChatGPT acceptance and live OAuth remain separate checks. Public endpoint probes from this workspace encountered Cloudflare error 1010; no bypass was attempted.

Primary references: [MCP authorization](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization), [MCP tool names](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/server/tools#tool-names), [Antigravity plugin MCP namespace](https://antigravity.google/docs/build-plugins/#mcp-servers), and [Antigravity MCP loading](https://antigravity.google/docs/mcp#eager-loading). MCP permits dots; the portable subset also satisfies the stricter host error reported for this integration.

# Public Demo Snapshot Seeding

Operational contract and guarded seeding procedure for the anonymous interactive demo at `/demo`.

The public demo reuses the shared student shell, course catalog, dashboard, articles, read-only diktats, flashcards, quizzes, tryouts, calendar, groups, achievements, leaderboard, and scripted Zyra via `StudentAccountBoundary` and browser-local fictional state.

Eligible real content is strictly bounded to the first active chapter of the four canonical courses (**Matematika I**, **Fisika Dasar I**, **Kimia Dasar I**, **Berpikir Komputasional**):

- **Article and Diktat**: Must belong to the first active chapter and pass published Free eligibility. Diktat renders read-only with downloads disabled.
- **Flashcards**: Must be a published Free-eligible set scoped to the first chapter.
- **Quiz**: Must match a published Free quiz template and canonical quiz assessment with an explicit unique fixed question set confined to the first chapter. Initial payloads omit answers; grading runs through signed stateless page tokens (up to 3 questions per page). When no eligible real quiz resolves, the runtime falls back to authored fictional questions in `lib/demo/fictional-products.ts`.
- **Sanitization**: Unsafe links, source-figure assets, generic PDFs, storage keys, paid bodies, answer keys, and coding locators are stripped or withheld.
- **Isolation**: Demo sessions never mutate live accounts, enrollments, schedules, or profiles, and never consume live AI quota. Resetting the demo clears browser-local progress, social, and reward overlays.

Migration `drizzle-postgres/0003_kind_shinko_yamashiro.sql` creates `public_demo_snapshots` (`id`, unique `course_id` referencing `mata_kuliah.id`, `snapshot` jsonb, `updated_at`). Rows are validated on read by `publicDemoSnapshotSchema` in `lib/demo/snapshot.ts`; invalid rows are skipped.

Required JSON fields:
- `version`: `2`
- `contentPolicy`: `"free-first-chapter"`
- `courseId`, `revision`, `displayName`, `asOf`, `streakDays`
- `course`, `inProgressDocuments`, `flashcards`, `weakConcepts`, `availableAssessments`, `history`
- Optional `mockChapters` (fictional later-chapter metadata only)

Changing `revision` invalidates previous browser-local overlays cleanly without requiring manual browser storage cleanup.

1. Verify the exact target host and database read-only first (`DATABASE_URL`, `NEON_EXPECTED_HOST`, `NEON_EXPECTED_DATABASE`).
2. Run dry-run validation (defaults to read-only):
   ```bash
   bun --conditions=react-server --env-file=.env.prod scripts/seed-public-demo.ts
   ```
3. Confirm each of the four canonical course titles resolves uniquely and that all four V2 JSON payloads pass schema and boundary validation.
4. Apply the transactional upsert only after explicit authorization:
   ```bash
   bun --conditions=react-server --env-file=.env.prod scripts/seed-public-demo.ts --apply
   ```
5. Verify `/demo` serves all four courses with no private storage keys, answer keys, or real user data exposed.

# Zyra Operations Runbooks

Version: `zyra-ops-runbooks-v2`

These runbooks apply to staging and production operations review. Investigate alerts using only privacy-safe alert codes and masked diagnostics. Never retrieve a prompt, response, raw API key, object key, or learner identity during incident triage.

Compare active reservations against the configured allowance cap and `workers/zyra-control-plane` diagnostics. If the count cannot be explained by normal traffic, roll back to the last verified application version and preserve lease rows for reconciliation. The allowance ledger is always-on and has no env kill switch.

Stop promotion of the affected release, reconcile application leases against control-plane commits, and roll back to the last verified application version if the invariant is not restored. Never delete lease rows.

Keep the authoritative allowance ledger active, repair only the documented compatibility projection, and rerun reconciliation after the grace window. Escalate if any committed lease is missing or duplicated.

Inspect masked provider/alias health and outcome buckets in `/admin/ops/models` and `/admin/ops/analytics`. Confirm Cloudflare AI Gateway (`CF_AI_GATEWAY_URL`, `CF_AI_GATEWAY_TOKEN`) reachability and verify that healthy fallback aliases are configured. Three consecutive failures trigger an automatic 5-minute alias cooldown. Roll back to the last verified application version if safe fallback cannot serve text traffic.

Verify bounded request caps, inspect alias cooldown state in `/admin/ops/models`, and allow health-aware fallback across configured BYOK aliases and query-key fallbacks to settle. Trigger a manual 3-sample median latency probe only after upstream pressure subsides.
Pause premium-tier experiments and verify that standard student tutoring retains its declared daily reserve (15 to 18 turns per Jakarta day depending on rank). Roll back if reserve accounting drifts.

Stop cache promotion and inspect only cache contract metadata and hashes. Disable `FEATURE_ZYRA_SEMANTIC_CACHE_V1` immediately if any learner, image, assessment, or profile field can enter a shared cache.
Freeze semantic writes, preserve calibration metadata, and compare scope and profile hashes. Disable `FEATURE_ZYRA_SEMANTIC_CACHE_V1` if false reuse or scope drift is observed.

Disable learner image input via `FEATURE_ZYRA_IMAGE_INPUT_V1` (and `NEXT_PUBLIC_FEATURE_ZYRA_IMAGE_INPUT_V1`), preserve private storage objects and database rows, and inspect only masked scope outcomes. Do not copy or expose attachment bytes.

Disable `FEATURE_ZYRA_IMAGE_INPUT_V1` if sanitizer rejections exceed the accepted threshold. Keep text tutoring active, retain masked failure reason codes, and retest only with approved synthetic fixtures.

Roll back the affected deployment, disable image input if involved, preserve leak-scan evidence, and block active-assessment traffic until `tests/contracts/assessment-redaction.test.ts` and policy validators pass.
Keep the typed response boundary fail-closed, inspect stable violation codes in `zyra_operational_events`, and roll back if deterministic safe composition is unavailable.

Keep quota and learner responses authoritative, verify PostgreSQL write health for `zyra_operational_events`, and restrict or roll back the operations route if it causes request failures. The `/admin/ops/analytics` dashboard is admin-gated and always-on. Never replace ledger truth with telemetry estimates.
Reject pending proposals in `zyra_proposals`, verify that the mutation confirmation boundary remains fail-closed, and do not apply any proposal while preconditions or audit linkage are uncertain.

For bundle-managed Ideas, source chunks, Articles, questions, and solutions, inspect the exact environment and canonical entity status before any authorized replay:

- A `vector_sync_queue` row represents historical intent, not authority to republish. Workers reread canonical state before embedding and again under advisory locks before provider writes. An old upsert for withdrawn content becomes a delete; an old delete for an active shared entity is skipped.
- Dispatch and cron process up to 250 rows per invocation in five checkpointed batches and schedule a durable continuation when eligible work remains.
- Malformed payloads stop at `VECTOR_SYNC_INVALID_PAYLOAD` (attempts 10) without blocking healthy sibling rows.
- Provider batch failures split by vector identity so independent upserts/deletes complete while failing identities back off (30 seconds, up to 10 attempts).
- Legacy namespaces (`learning`, `practice`, `past_exams`, `idea`, `product`) are retired and quarantined (`VECTOR_SYNC_LEGACY_NAMESPACE_RETIRED`). Do not replay them into `canonical-content-v2`.

1. **Scope and namespace**: Admin Ops AI uses the dedicated Cloudflare Vectorize namespace `admin_ops_knowledge` (768 dimensions, cosine similarity), completely isolated from student tutoring namespaces. Curated sources are defined in `CURATED_ADMIN_KNOWLEDGE_ALLOWLIST` (`lib/admin-ops-ai/admin-knowledge-sources.ts`).
2. **Local index rebuild**: Whenever documentation under `docs/` or `AGENTS.md` changes, rebuild the precomputed fallback index:
   ```bash
   bun run build:ops-docs
   ```
3. **Remote vector sync**: Trigger the synchronization worker via event `admin/knowledge.sync` (or `bun scripts/staging/smoke-admin-ops-knowledge.ts` on verified staging). Obsolete chunk vectors are deleted automatically.
4. **Verification**: Confirm `admin_ops_knowledge_sources` reflects the updated `contentHash`, `chunkCount`, and `active` status.

section: Admin Ops Knowledge index rollback without runtime flag
content:
Knowledge retrieval is always-on for admin surfaces with no runtime feature flag:
1. Revert the affected markdown file in Git to its prior verified commit and run `bun run build:ops-docs`.
2. Re-run synchronization (`admin/knowledge.sync` or `bun scripts/staging/smoke-admin-ops-knowledge.ts --apply`) so newer chunks are marked `stale`, deleted from Vectorize, and prior chunks are restored.
3. For emergency cleanup, invoke `markChunksStale()` in `lib/admin-ops-ai/admin-knowledge-store.ts` for the affected source ID.

section: AI Gateway and provider failure mitigation
content:
1. **Routing and cooldowns**: All LLM traffic routes through Cloudflare AI Gateway with dynamic catalog discovery (12-hour KV cache, 14-day stale-usable window) and per-feature or global model selection in `/admin/ops/models`. Three consecutive failures place a provider alias into a 5-minute cooldown while healthy aliases serve traffic.
2. **Typed errors**: Quota exhaustion emits `RATE_LIMITED` (`retryable: true`); upstream timeouts/5xx emit `PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE` (`retryable: true`).
3. **Manual fallback**: If provider degradation persists, switch the affected feature's model/alias in `/admin/ops/models` or perform admin operations directly via standard `/admin` routes.

section: Admin action proposal retention and expiration policy
content:
1. **TTL**: Action proposals in `zyra_proposals` expire automatically after 30 minutes if not confirmed by an authenticated admin.
2. **Idempotency and preconditions**: Executed proposals cannot re-run; duplicate requests return the recorded result idempotently. Live preconditions are checked immediately before execution and fail with `STALE_PRECONDITION` on drift.
3. **Audit retention**: `zyra_proposals` and `ops_ai_mutation_audit` are immutable audit trails; retain records for at least 90 days before archival.

# Zyx Academy: Engineering Case Study

> Public-facing case study for Zyx Academy. It intentionally excludes private course content, credentials, internal admin data, proprietary prompts, and sensitive operational details.

**Live:** https://zyxacademy.com

Zyx Academy is a full-stack, multi-platform learning management system for university students. It combines structured scientific learning content, spaced-repetition flashcards, adaptive assessments, interactive Python coding, scoped Q&A discussions, gamified progress, and an AI tutor called Zyra.

The core engineering challenge is not just generating educational content with AI. It is building a verifiable, source-backed content pipeline so articles, printable diktats, questions, flashcards, vector retrieval, and AI tutor responses remain traceable to reviewed academic sources.

- **Multi-platform delivery**: Next.js 16.3 web app with separated mobile and desktop LMS shells, Capacitor 7 mobile wrapper (Android/iOS), and Tauri v2 desktop wrapper (Windows/macOS/Linux) with offline reading and delta updates.
- **Canonical authoring pipeline**: Source Pack ingestion, atomic Idea Bundle V3 extraction, structured Product Bundle V4 (interactive scientific articles, printable diktats, flashcards), standalone solution collections (V5), and flexible stable-ID revisions.
- **MCP-first authoring and operations**: Streamable HTTP MCP server with OAuth PKCE consent, scoped playbooks, and packaged skills (`soezyxstt/zyx-authoring-mcp`).
- **Assessment and coding platform**: Timed and untimed quizzes, tryouts, live real-time classroom quizzes, and an interactive Python playground with browser/WASI execution and Zyra coding coaching.
- **Grounded AI tutor (Zyra)**: Retrieval-augmented tutoring over 768-dimensional Cloudflare Vectorize namespaces, dynamic multi-provider model routing via Cloudflare AI Gateway, distributed quota leasing, and structured pedagogical responses with KaTeX math and interactive visuals.
- **Student engagement and collaboration**: Bilingual (`id`/`en`) scoped discussions with `@Zyra` mentions, SM-2 spaced-repetition flashcards, mastery analytics, Google Calendar schedule sync, and student gamification with a 3D Pet Studio.

section: 1. Treat AI Output as a Versioned Pipeline Artifact
content: Generated content never goes straight from an LLM response to students. Source Packs, Idea Bundles (V3), and Product Bundles (V4/V5) pass deterministic schema validation, coverage checks, browser/PDF verification, and explicit review gates before atomic publication.

Every Idea, Article block, flashcard, question, and vector chunk retains provenance links back to source document pages and checksums. Assessment answer keys are strictly excluded from shared caches and student tutoring retrieval.
External AI agents can validate, inspect, and stage revisions over MCP, while publication requires explicit scoped consent and verified revision receipts.

section: 4. Multi-Provider AI Resilience and Quota Isolation
content: All AI traffic routes through Cloudflare AI Gateway with dynamic catalog discovery, 3-sample median latency probes, automatic alias cooldown on consecutive failures, and a distributed Cloudflare Worker control plane for quota leases.

# Agent instructions for Zyx Academy

This file contains durable rules for work in this repository. Read the relevant sections before acting, but use source code and `docs/` as the authority for current feature behavior and deployment status. Do not treat this file as a release ledger.

- The brand is **Zyx**, never `ZYX`, except in literal filesystem paths.
- Token prefixes use `Zyx-XXXXXXXX-{capacity}-{courseIds.length}`.
- Use short, sentence-case UI copy. Prefer numbers over long explanations. Do not add exclamation marks.
- Do not use sparkle icons in UI.
- Treat filler descriptions as visible copy that only labels a self-evident demo, sample, preview, or mock; explains that static marketing content is not account or usage data; repeats a heading, card, input placeholder, or visible control; narrates an obvious click or selection; or restates values already shown next to it. Remove the copy entirely, including its wrapper, spacing, `caption`, `meta`, or reserved height.
- On landing and marketing surfaces, assume the composition already establishes demo context. Do not add labels such as "Simulasi", "Contoh", or "Pratinjau", or disclaimers such as "bukan metrik" and "bukan data pengguna", unless omitting them could cause a real safety, legal, authority, or accuracy misunderstanding.
- Keep copy when it communicates non-obvious product behavior, access or eligibility terms, a price unit users must decide on, safety or accuracy boundaries, dynamic state, required action or format, recovery guidance, or instructional content. Keep these statements as short as possible and do not duplicate a placeholder.
- Before finalizing a surface, audit nearby rendered copy for the same pattern. Do not replace removed filler with another generic caption or helper paragraph.
- Never use em dashes or en dashes in code, copy, metadata, or documentation. Use commas, semicolons, or periods instead.

- Keep a change inside the requested surface. Reuse existing flows and components instead of rewriting adjacent systems.
- Check `git status --short` before editing. Preserve unrelated worktree changes. Never use reset or checkout to discard them.
- Audits and reviews are read-only unless implementation is explicitly requested.
- Before any staging, production, database, storage, Google Drive, or other external mutation, verify the exact environment and target, inspect it read-only first, and obtain explicit authorization when the action is not already part of the request.
- Distinguish verified local structure or tests from unverified runtime, visual, OAuth, staging, production, or external-service behavior.
- Do not expose secrets in source, logs, reports, or documentation. Keep environment-specific credentials in the appropriate `.env` file.

Every feature change must check the affected workflow against MCP tools, scopes, consent, capability discovery, playbooks, packaged skills and host prompts. Update every affected contract and its focused checks in the same change. Verify existing clients and exact environment bindings. Record the affected workflow and verification in the handoff, or explain why the change has no MCP impact. For intentionally UI-only actions, keep the operations coverage catalog accurate. Distinguish repository changes from published packages and deployed servers.

1. Read `db/schema.ts` and `lib/env.ts` before changing database, environment, or server behavior.
2. For Next.js APIs, routing, or framework behavior, read the relevant guide in `node_modules/next/dist/docs/` first. This project uses Next.js 16.3 and its APIs may differ from older examples.
3. Search for an existing route, server action, helper, component, feature flag, and test before creating a new one.
4. Read the relevant document in `docs/` before changing a documented contract.
5. Foundational capabilities are always-on by default. If a new capability or material change could be always-on or flag-gated, ask before implementing it. A flag needs a key, rationale, default, scope, rollback path, owner, and removal condition. Check `lib/feature-flags.ts` for existing operational gates and obtain approval before adding or removing a flag.
